title: Update IR V4 types to match latest finos/morphir spec
description:
The Classic ↔ V4 converter cannot be fully implemented until we update our IR V4 type definitions to match the most recent specification from finos/morphir.

## Background
The steel thread migrate command currently only supports same-format passthrough (V4→V4, Classic→Classic). Cross-format conversion is blocked because our IR V4 types are incomplete - they use `serde_json::Value` placeholders instead of typed expressions.

## References
- V4 Spec: https://github.com/finos/morphir/blob/main/docs/spec/ir/schemas/v4/
- What's New in V4: https://github.com/finos/morphir/blob/main/docs/spec/ir/schemas/v4/whats-new.md
- Complete Example: https://github.com/finos/morphir/blob/main/docs/spec/ir/schemas/v4/complete-example.json

## Current State (What Works)
- Distribution structure (Library/Specs/Application) - matches spec
- FormatVersion (string "4.0.0" or int 4)
- Wrapper object serialization in v4.rs
- TypeAttributes/ValueAttributes with source, constraints, extensions
- Core Type enum (7 variants) - Variable, Reference, Tuple, Record, ExtensibleRecord, Function, Unit
- Core Value enum (18+ variants) including V4-only Hole, Native, External
- Literal types with IntegerLiteral (alias WholeNumberLiteral)
- JSON-level converter works for Classic ↔ V4

## Tasks (Priority Order)

### Phase 1: Serde for Type<A>
- [ ] Implement Serialize for Type<A> with V4 wrapper object format
- [ ] Implement Deserialize for Type<A> with V4 format + shorthand support
- [ ] Add tests with sample V4 type expressions
- Files: `crates/morphir-core/src/ir/type_expr.rs`, add `serde_v4.rs`

### Phase 2: Serde for Value<TA,VA>
- [ ] Implement Serialize for Value<TA,VA> with V4 wrapper object format
- [ ] Implement Deserialize for Value<TA,VA> with V4 format
- [ ] Add tests with sample V4 value expressions
- Files: `crates/morphir-core/src/ir/value_expr.rs`

### Phase 3: Replace serde_json::Value placeholders
- [ ] Replace in TypeSpecification.type_expr
- [ ] Replace in ConstructorArgSpec.arg_type
- [ ] Replace in ValueSpecification.inputs/output
- [ ] Replace in TypeDefinition.type_expr
- [ ] Replace in ConstructorArg.arg_type
- [ ] Replace in ValueDefinition.output_type
- [ ] Replace in InputTypeEntry.input_type
- [ ] Replace in ValueBody::ExpressionBody.body
- [ ] Replace in ValueAttributes.inferred_type
- File: `crates/morphir-core/src/ir/v4.rs`

### Phase 4: Add IncompleteTypeDefinition
- [ ] Add IncompleteTypeDefinition variant to TypeDefinition enum
- [ ] Include incompleteness reason (similar to HoleReason)
- [ ] Add serialization support
- Files: `crates/morphir-core/src/ir/type_def.rs`, `v4.rs`

### Phase 5: Integration Tests
- [ ] Test with real V4 IR files from finos/morphir examples
- [ ] Test round-trip conversion: V4 JSON → typed IR → V4 JSON
- [ ] Test Classic → V4 conversion produces valid V4 JSON
- [ ] Add fixtures to integration-tests/fixtures/steel-thread/

## V4 Format Details

### Wrapper Object Format
```json
{"Variable": {"name": "a"}}
{"Reference": {"fqname": "morphir/sdk:list#map", "args": [...]}}
{"Tuple": {"elements": [...]}}
{"Record": {"field-name": type, ...}}
```

### Compact Shorthand (for deserialization)
- Type variable as bare string: `"a"` instead of `{"Variable": {"name": "a"}}`
- Simple reference as FQName: `"morphir/sdk:basics#int"` 
- Reference with args: `{"Reference": ["morphir/sdk:list#list", "a"]}`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Type<A> and Value<TA,VA> implement Serialize + Deserialize
- [ ] All serde_json::Value placeholders replaced with typed expressions
- [ ] Round-trip V4 JSON works (deserialize → serialize = same structure)
- [ ] Classic → V4 converter produces valid typed V4 IR
- [ ] Integration tests pass with real Morphir IR files

## Blocks
- Steel thread P0 completion (cross-format migration)
- morphir-rust-steel-thread
close_reason: PR #63 merged with V4 IR types update and comprehensive test coverage

title: Setup acquires the MoonBit toolchain (moonc) for the MoonBit backend
description: Decision (Damian, 2026-09-26): for now the setup and install experience acquires moonc; embedding it is investigated separately (morphir-ukvn.5.4). The MoonBit extension declares that it needs the MoonBit toolchain (a pinned moon/moonc/core version, since moonc must match its core library exactly); the CLI's setup or extension install path checks for it and, with the user's consent, installs the pinned version (official installer or mise), then runs moonc as a separate process. Sizes (spike, macOS arm64): native moonc 35 MB, full toolchain about 245 MB (bin 175 MB, lib 70 MB); moonc as wasm-gc 8.9 MB plus moonc.js (needs a JS host); npm @moonbit/moonc-worker 5.5 MB JS, no license field. Done when installing the MoonBit extension on a machine with no MoonBit leaves a working, version-matched moonc and the extension finds it.

title: Decide whether the MoonBit compiler license is acceptable for Morphir
description: The E0 spike found moonc under the MoonBit Public Source License (not OSI; SSPL-style clause for offering it as a service; modification only for non-commercial use). Compiled output is free of it; moon and moonrun moved to Apache-2.0 on 2026-09-11 and the core library is Apache-2.0. Morphir would run a user-installed moonc as a separate process, never bundle it. Needs a FINOS legal or maintainer decision before E1. Also correct the out-of-date AGPL note in docs/design/draft/extensions/distribution-and-acquisition.md:34-41. Done when the decision is recorded.

title: E0: spike, compile Morphir to WASM through MoonBit
description: Compile two or three small models to MoonBit by hand or with a minimal generator, build with moon build --target wasm-gc, run in wasmtime, compare with morphir-runtime. Measure the SDK mapping, currying and closures, whether moonc runs as WASM, debuggability and build time. Output is a recommendation (route 2 or the Cranelift fallback); everything built is thrown away. Spec: design of morphir-ukvn (section 4).

Report is the comment on this bead.

Oracle: morphir-runtime for integers, custom types, pattern matching, lists, recursion (arity model in spec/ir/semantics/v3 with cases/arity.json; local-count); doc-comment expectations in crates/morphir-tests/fixtures/classic/evaluator-tests.json for records, Maybe, Dict. morphir-sdk MoonBit package is a placeholder; map the SDK onto MoonBit core. MoonBit compiler is AGPL (docs/design/draft/extensions/distribution-and-acquisition.md:34-41): shipping moonc inside an extension needs a licensing check.

comments.author: Damian Reeves
comments.text:
# E0 spike report: Morphir IR to WASM through MoonBit

Bead: `morphir-ukvn.5.1`. Date: 2026-09-26. Toolchain: `moon` 0.1.20260803, `moonc` v0.10.6+62c2592d1, `moonrun` 0.1.20260803, core 0.10.6.

## Question

Can Morphir IR compile to MoonBit source that MoonBit builds to wasm-gc and that runs correctly? What does the SDK mapping cost? The spike must end with a recommendation: route 2 (MoonBit) or route 1 (Cranelift fallback).

## Recommendation

**Take route 2 (MoonBit).** Continue to E1, with four conditions:

1. **Do not ship `moonc` in a Morphir extension.** Treat it as a toolchain that the user installs, the same way the user installs `cargo` or `gleam`. Run it as a separate process. See "Licenses".
2. **Morphir owns an SDK layer in MoonBit.** Do not map SDK calls directly to MoonBit core. The layer must fix the semantic differences that this spike found: String ordering, integer overflow, division by zero, `Dict.union` bias and lost abort messages.
3. **Emit MoonBit code that works on all targets, and select the target for each host.** Use `--target wasm` (linear memory) for Extism and component-model hosts, because the MoonBit Extism PDK and the component model use linear memory. Use `--target wasm-gc` for JS and browser hosts. Both targets gave the same results.
4. **Put a version lock on the MoonBit toolchain** in `mise.toml`, and test the backend output against that version in CI.

MoonBit passed every functional check. The mechanical translation was simple. One MoonBit source gave the same output on wasm-gc (V8 and wasmtime), wasm, js and native. Project builds took less than 0.5 s. A Cranelift backend would have to supply closures, GC or memory management, pattern-match compilation and a runtime, and it would give only one target. The risks listed at the end could change this answer. The license risk is the largest.

## What was tried

All work was done in a temporary directory (`/tmp/e0-spike-Js3s`, now deleted). No repository was changed.

1. **IR source.** I rendered IR values from two places into pseudo code. The arity rule came from the V3 distribution in `spec/ir/semantics/v3/cases/evaluation/five-cases.request.json`. The evaluator tests came from `crates/morphir-tests/fixtures/classic/evaluator-tests.json`. For `local-count`, I read the hand-built IR in `crates/morphir-runtime/tests/v3_arity.rs`.
2. **Hand translation.** I translated each value to MoonBit by hand, but mechanically, with one rule per IR construct (see the rule table). There was one MoonBit package for each Morphir module, plus SDK shim packages.
3. **Oracle 1.** I ran `cargo test -p morphir-runtime --test v3_arity` with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` in the temp directory. All 9 tests passed, and they confirm the five arity outcomes and `local-count = 3`.
4. **Builds and runs.** I built with `moon build` for the targets wasm-gc, wasm, js and native, in debug and release modes, and ran the output with `moonrun`. I also ran the wasm-gc output in **wasmtime 43.0.2**, the version that `extism` 1.30 in the morphir-rust `Cargo.lock` uses, with the same feature flags that Extism sets. For this, I built a 40-line runner offline from the local cargo cache in the temp directory. I did not install wasmtime globally.
5. **Host-facing module.** I linked a library module that exports scalar entry points through `link.wasm-gc.exports`, and called it from Node and from wasmtime.
6. **Compiler as WASM.** I tested `moonc` as a JS module and as a WASM module (npm `@moonbit/moonc-worker`, GitHub release `moonbit-wasm.tar.gz`), and read the license files and repository metadata.

## Results

The oracle for the first six rows is `morphir-runtime` (Oracle 1). The oracle for all other rows is the doc-comment `expected` value in `evaluator-tests.json` (Oracle 2).

| Model / value | Input | Oracle value | wasm-gc (moonrun) | wasm-gc (wasmtime 43) | js | native | wasm | Match |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `arity#check-arity` zero | 0, [] | `Valid` | `Valid` | same | same | same | same | yes |
| `arity#check-arity` one | 1, [Unit] | `Valid` | `Valid` | same | same | same | same | yes |
| `arity#check-arity` two | 2, [Unit, Unit] | `Valid` | `Valid` | same | same | same | same | yes |
| `arity#check-arity` too-few | 1, [] | `Mismatch 1 0` | `Mismatch(1, 0)` | same | same | same | same | yes |
| `arity#check-arity` too-many | 1, [Unit, Unit] | `Mismatch 1 2` | `Mismatch(1, 2)` | same | same | same | same | yes |
| `rules#local-count` | [(), ()] | 3 | 3 | same | same | same | same | yes |
| `record-field-test` | ctx | "Correct" | "Correct" | same | same | same | same | yes |
| `update-record-full-test` | ctx | {"Soso", 5} | `{ name: "Soso", number: 5 }` | same | same | same | same | yes |
| `maybe-map` | Just "Red" | "Bright Red" | "Bright Red" | same | same | same | same | yes |
| `maybe-map` | Nothing | "Ultraviolet" | "Ultraviolet" | same | same | same | same | yes |
| `dict-filter-test` | ctx | [(3,"Blue"),(4,"Blue")] | `[(3, "Blue"), (4, "Blue")]` | same | same | same | same | yes |
| `dict-update-test`, naive String rule | ctx | fromList [("Alice",1),("Bob",6)] | `[("Bob", 6), ("Alice", 1)]` | same | same | same | same | **same entries, wrong order** |
| `dict-update-test`, `MString` rule | ctx | fromList [("Alice",1),("Bob",6)] | `[("Alice", 1), ("Bob", 6)]` | same | same | same | same | yes |
| `let-recursion-fibonacci-test` | ctx | 34 | 34 | same | same | same | same | yes |
| `let-recursion-mutual-test` | ctx | (8, 9) | (8, 9) | same | same | same | same | yes |
| `pattern-match-constructor-test` | ctx | "Correct" | "Correct" | same | same | same | same | yes |
| `pattern-match-head-tail-test` | ctx | ("Dog", "Red") | ("Dog", "Red") | same | same | same | same | yes |
| `constructor-two-arg-curried-test` | ctx | TwoArg 5 "Blue" | `TwoArg(5, "Blue")` | same | same | same | same | yes |

"same" means that the output line is the same byte for byte as the wasm-gc (moonrun) output. I checked this with `diff` for debug and release builds on every target.

The wasmtime run also called the exported functions `check_arity_code(1,2) = 2`, `check_arity_code(1,1) = -1` (Valid) and `fib_test() = 34`. Node gave the same values.

The only mismatch is in `dict-update-test`, and its cause is a real semantic gap. In MoonBit, `impl Compare for String` uses **shortlex** order: the shorter string comes first, so `"Bob" < "Alice"` is `true`. Elm and Morphir compare strings in lexicographic order. The keys in a sorted map therefore iterate in a different order. The `MString` newtype, which compares with `String::lexical_compare`, corrects this.

## Translation rules

These are the rules that I applied. A rule that is marked "no clean mapping" needs a design decision in E1.

| IR construct | MoonBit emission | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Package + module path | One MoonBit package per Morphir module, for example `ir_specification/morphir/validation/arity` | The import alias is the last segment. If two modules have the same last segment, the backend must set explicit aliases (the SDK package `list` already clashes with core `list`). |
| Names | Values and fields become `snake_case`; types and constructors become `PascalCase` | MoonBit keywords get a trailing `_`: `test` becomes `test_` and `match` becomes `match_`. |
| Custom type | `pub(all) enum T[A] { C1; C2(X, Y) } derive(@debug.Debug, Eq, Compare)` | Positional fields. `derive(Show)` is deprecated in 0.10.6, so use `Debug`. |
| Single-constructor type (`FQName`, `Field`) | An enum with one case | A struct is also possible, but the enum keeps constructor patterns uniform. |
| Type alias | `pub type Name = @list.List[String]` | You cannot use `derive` on an alias. |
| Constructor, saturated | `TwoArg(5L, "Blue")` | |
| Constructor, partial or as a value | A lambda over the missing arguments, for example `arg2 => TwoArg(5L, arg2)` | MoonBit constructors are not first-class values (error E4203). |
| Top-level definition | `pub fn f(a : A, b : B) -> R`, uncurried | Types come from `inputTypes` and `outputType`. Free type variables become `fn[A]` generics. |
| Apply, saturated call of a known definition | Direct call `f(a, b)` | Nested `Apply` chains are flattened. |
| Apply, partial | A closure `b => f(a, b)` | |
| Apply, over-saturated | `f(a)(b)` | |
| Reference to a definition with arity 1 used as a value | The function name, for example `times3` | |
| Reference to a definition with arity 2 or more used as a value | A curried wrapper `a => b => f(a, b)` | |
| Lambda | `x => body`, always one parameter (curried) | A lambda whose pattern is not a variable becomes `x => match x { pat => body }`. |
| Function-typed value in the SDK | Curried type `(K) -> (V) -> Bool` | SDK shims accept curried closures and call `p(k)(v)`. This costs one closure allocation for each argument. |
| LetDefinition, no arguments | `let x = e` | |
| LetDefinition with arguments | A local `fn name(args) { ... }` | |
| LetRecursion, one binding | A local `fn` (a local fn can call itself) | A binding whose body is a lambda chain becomes parameters. |
| LetRecursion, mutual | `letrec f = (l : T) => ... and g = ...` | This worked for `let-recursion-mutual-test`. |
| Destructure | `let (a, b) = e`, or `match` for refutable patterns | |
| IfThenElse | `if c { a } else { b }` | |
| PatternMatch | `match` | Constructor and literal patterns map directly. MoonBit rejects partial matches at compile time by default (warning 0011 is an error), so the backend must add `_ => @rt.no_match("<fqname>")` when it cannot prove that the match is complete. |
| EmptyListPattern | `Empty` | |
| HeadTailPattern | `More(h, tail=t)`, nested for `a :: b :: []` | The core `List` has a `mut tail~` field, but pattern matching on it works. |
| AsPattern | `(p) as n`; for `_ as n`, only `n` | |
| WildcardPattern, TuplePattern, LiteralPattern, UnitPattern | `_`, `(a, b)`, `3L` / `"s"` / `true`, `()` | |
| Record type (closed) | One shared generic struct for each sorted set of field names, for example `Rec_name_number[A, B]`. A record alias becomes `pub type RecordType = Rec_name_number[String, Int64]` | This keeps structural typing. An anonymous record and its alias are the same MoonBit type. |
| Record literal | `@records_.Rec_name_number::{ name: ..., number: ... }` | |
| Field access | `r.name` | |
| FieldFunction `.name` | `r => r.name` | This needs the record type from the IR. |
| UpdateRecord | `{ ..r, name: "Soso" }` | |
| Extensible record `{ a \| name : String }` | **No clean mapping.** | MoonBit has no row polymorphism. Options: monomorphize for each use site, or use a trait with getters. |
| Empty record `{}` | `pub(all) struct Rec_ {}`, built with `Rec_::{}` | `{}` alone is a `Map` literal. |
| Tuple | MoonBit tuple | |
| Unit | `Unit` / `()` | |
| Maybe | `T?` (`Option`); `Just` becomes `Some`, `Nothing` becomes `None` | |
| Result | `Result[T, E]` | |
| List literal | `@list.List([a, b, c])` | `@list.from_array` is deprecated. |
| Dict | `@dict.Dict[K, V]`, an alias of `@immut/sorted_map.SortedMap[K, V]` | The key needs `Compare`. |
| Int | `Int64` with checked SDK operations (default); `@bigint.BigInt` is an option | Literals need an `L` suffix. Unconstrained literals (type variable `t8` in the fixture) default to `Int64`. |
| Float | `Double` | |
| String | `String` in value positions; `MString(String)` wherever order matters | See the String gap. |
| Char | `Char` (Unicode scalar value) | |
| `basics.equal` / `lessThan` / `and` | `==` / `<` / `&&` | The IR carries the concrete type at each reference, so the backend can select a monomorphic operator. |
| `basics.append` | `+` for String, `concat` for List | Selected by the instantiated type. |
| `basics.add` / `subtract` / `multiply` | `@basics.add(a, b)` and so on (checked shims) | This agrees with `morphir-runtime`, which uses `i64::checked_add`. |
| Untyped IR (hand-built tests, `ty: attr()`) | **Needs an inference pass** | MoonBit needs signatures on top-level functions. `local-count` worked only because its element type is free, so `fn[A]` was enough. |

The emitted code for all 12 model values, plus the SDK shims, was 347 lines of MoonBit.

## SDK mapping onto MoonBit core

| Morphir SDK | MoonBit core | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Basics.Int` + - * | `Int64` + - * | **Gap: overflow.** MoonBit wraps (`9223372036854775807L + 1L = -9223372036854775808`). `morphir-runtime` returns an error. A shim with overflow checks is necessary. |
| `Basics.//` (integer divide) | `Int64 /` | **Gap, and targets disagree.** Division by zero gives a trap on wasm-gc ("divide by zero"), a `PanicError` on js, and **returns 0 without an error on native**. Elm returns 0. A shim is necessary. |
| `Basics.modBy` | `%` truncates (`-7L % 2L = -1`) | **Gap.** Elm `modBy 2 -7 = 1` (floored). A shim is necessary. `remainderBy` maps to `%`. |
| Comparison, `compare`, `max`, `min` | `Compare` trait | Correct for numbers, Char, tuples and `@list.List` (lexicographic). **Wrong for String (shortlex).** |
| `Basics.Float` and math | `Double`, `@double`, `@math` | IEEE 754 on all targets. Not tested for each function. |
| `Basics.Bool`, `not`, `&&`, `\|\|` | `Bool` | Clean. |
| `String` | `String` (UTF-16 code units) | `length` counts UTF-16 units (`"😀".length() = 2`), the same as Elm in JavaScript. The Morphir spec must state this. **Ordering needs `MString`.** `fromInt` maps to `to_string`; `toInt` and `toFloat` map to `@strconv`. I did not check the full String API. |
| `Char` | `Char` | The type maps cleanly. I did not check the Unicode behavior of `toUpper`, `isAlpha` and similar functions. |
| `Maybe` | `Option` | `map`, `withDefault` and `andThen` need shims only to put the arguments in Morphir order. |
| `Result` | `Result` | Clean. |
| `List` | `@list.List` (immutable cons list) | `map`, `filter`, `fold`, `rev`, `zip`, `concat`, `take`, `drop`, `sort`, `repeat`, `intersperse`, `unzip`, `maximum` and `minimum` exist. `length` returns a 32-bit `Int` and needs a conversion. Shims are needed for `foldr`, `sortBy`, `sortWith`, `map2` to `map5`, `range` and `indexedMap` (for Int64). |
| `Dict` | `@immut/sorted_map` | `get`, `add` (insert), `remove`, `filter`, `map`, `fold`, `size` and `singleton` exist. **`merge` gives priority to the right map; Elm `union` gives priority to the left**, so the shim swaps the arguments. Shims are needed for `update`, `partition`, `diff`, `intersect`, `foldr` and `keys` (which returns an `Array`). |
| `Set` | `@immut/sorted_set` | This exists. I did not test it. It has the same String ordering issue. |
| `Tuple` | Tuples, `.0`, `.1` | Clean. |
| `Decimal` | **None in core** | **Gap.** Build it on `@bigint` (a scaled integer) or find a library. |
| `LocalDate`, `LocalTime`, `Month` | **None in core** | **Gap.** |
| `Regex` | **None in core** | **Gap.** |
| Arbitrary-precision `Int` (if the spec needs it) | `@bigint.BigInt` | This works on wasm-gc. The `fib` module with BigInt was 5,044 bytes; with Int64 it was 829 bytes. `fib 25 = 121393` took 17 ms in Node. |

## Build time and size

These were measured on an Apple Silicon Mac with a warm filesystem. "Cold" means that the project had no build output after `moon clean`. The core library is prebuilt when MoonBit is installed, so cold builds do not compile core.

| Target / mode | Cold build (22 packages) | Warm build (1 file touched) | No-op |
|---|---|---|---|
| wasm-gc debug | 0.35 to 0.48 s | 0.20 to 0.27 s | 0.02 s |
| wasm-gc release | 0.30 s | n/a | n/a |
| js debug / release | 0.27 s / 0.30 s | 0.15 s / 0.13 s | n/a |
| native debug (tcc) / release (cc) | 0.56 s / 1.31 s | 0.29 s / 1.01 s | n/a |

| Artifact (the harness `cmd/main` prints all results with `Debug`) | Size |
|---|---|
| wasm-gc release | 51,013 B (21,285 B gzip) |
| wasm-gc debug | 119,815 B, plus a `.wasm.map` file |
| wasm (linear memory) release | 69,280 B |
| js release | 154,622 B |
| native release | 390,056 B |
| wasm-gc release library, 2 scalar exports (arity + fib), no printing | **829 B** |
| The same library with BigInt Int | 5,044 B |

Most of the harness size comes from the `Debug` printing. The wasm-gc module imports only one function, `spectest.print_char`, and it validates with the default `wasm-tools` features. Wasmtime compiled the harness module in 26 ms.

For comparison, `morphir-runtime` tests compiled in 8.6 s with a cold target directory.

## moonc as WASM

| Form | What it is | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Installed `moonc` | A native Mach-O arm64 binary (35 MB) | This is the compiler that the spike used. |
| npm `@moonbit/moonc-worker` | A 5.5 MB CommonJS file made with **js_of_ocaml** (JavaScript, not WASM). The API is `check`, `buildPackage`, `linkCore` and `genTestInfo`. | **It works in Node in the same process.** Build took 0.13 to 0.15 s and link took 0.25 s after a 0.14 s load. The output wasm ran in Node and in moonrun and printed 34. **The worker version must match the core bundle exactly.** `0.1.202609203` failed with `Invalid_argument("Char.chr")` against core 0.10.6. `0.1.202608034` worked. The package has **no license field and no LICENSE file**. |
| GitHub `moonbitlang/moonbit-compiler` release `moonbit-wasm.tar.gz` (v0.10.14) | `moonc.js` + an 8.9 MB `.wasm` made with **wasm_of_ocaml** (wasm-gc) | It runs with Node (`node moonc.js -v` gave `v0.10.14+7d59c7ec9`). **It needs a JS host**: the module has 84 `bindings` imports plus `wasm:js-string`, `wasm:text-decoder` and `wasm:text-encoder`. It cannot run in wasmtime or Extism without a JS engine. |
| Browser playground | `@moonbit/moonpad-monaco` (Apache-2.0) wraps the worker | I did not test it. |

Summary: a MoonBit compiler in WASM or JS exists and works in JS hosts. It does not run directly in the Morphir WASM host (Extism).

## Licenses

| Component | License | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `moonc` (compiler) | **MoonBit Public Source License v1** (MPSL, 11 December 2024). It is not an OSI license. The README calls it "a relaxed SSPL". It is based on the GPL text and adds **section 14**: if you offer the program as a service "commercially or competitively", you must publish the Service Source Code of the whole service stack. The README also says that "modifications to the compiler are allowed for non-commercial purposes". | `moonbitlang/moonbit-compiler/LICENSE.TXT`, README |
| Compiler output | **Free of MPSL obligations.** An exception lets you convey embedded compiler portions in the output under MIT. The README says that "artifacts produced by the MoonBit compiler may be licensed by the user under any license of their choosing". | The same file, last section |
| `moon`, `moonrun` | **Apache-2.0 since 2026-09-11** (commit `2f23b930`, "relicense project under Apache-2.0"). **Before that it was AGPL-3.0.** The installed 0.1.20260803 was released under AGPL-3.0. | `moonbitlang/moon` history |
| `core` library | Apache-2.0. The NOTICE file lists fdlibm and V8 code (BSD-style). | `~/.moon/lib/core/LICENSE`, `moon.mod` |
| Bundled tools | binaryen Apache-2.0, tcc LGPL-2.1, simdutf MIT | `~/.moon/CREDITS.md` |
| `@moonbit/moonc-worker` (npm) | Not declared | The package metadata |
| `extism/moonbit-pdk` | Apache-2.0 | GitHub |

`docs/design/draft/extensions/distribution-and-acquisition.md:34-41` says that MoonBit's "implementation is AGPL-3.0". That sentence is out of date. The build tool and registry code (`moon`) was AGPL and is now Apache-2.0. The compiler was never AGPL; it uses MPSL.

**Effect on a Morphir extension:**

- **Generated code and the artifacts that users compile:** no problem. The compiler exception and the Apache-2.0 core cover them.
- **An extension that calls a `moonc` that the user installed**, as a separate process: this is running the unmodified program, and the license permits it without conditions. This is the recommended design.
- **An extension that bundles `moonc`** (the native binary, the npm worker or the wasm tarball): this conveys MPSL code. Each bundle must carry the license, and a non-OSI component is then in a FINOS distribution. This needs FINOS legal review. Do not do it before that review.
- **A hosted Morphir compile service** that runs `moonc` for third parties, commercially: section 14 can apply to the whole service stack. Vendors who host Morphir must know this.

This is not legal advice. The last two points need a legal review.

## Debuggability

| Case | moonrun (V8 + source map) | wasmtime 43 (the Extism engine) | js (Node) | native |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Failed pattern match, debug build | `RuntimeError: unreachable` with MoonBit frames and `file.mbt:line` | `wasm trap: unreachable` with mangled names only, for example `_M0FP47morphir2e03cmd11fail__match10head__only`. No file or line. | `$PanicError`, source-mapped. **One frame pointed to the wrong file** (`head_only` at `sdk/basics/basics.mbt:7:4`). | `PanicError` with `fail.mbt:line` |
| Failed pattern match, release build | `wasm-function[11]:0x4bb` only | `<wasm function 3>` only | n/a | n/a |
| `abort("Int overflow")` in the SDK | The trap and the stack show, **but the message is lost** | The same | The same | The message is printed |
| Division by zero | `RuntimeError: divide by zero` | Trap | `$PanicError` | **No error; the result is 0** |

Findings:

- Debug builds write a `.wasm.map` source map (176 KB for a 4.7 KB module) and add a `sourceMappingURL` section. moonrun and Node use it. Wasmtime does not use it, because wasmtime reads DWARF. A Morphir host can map offsets to source itself with the `.wasm.map` file.
- In `core/abort/abort.mbt`, `abort(msg)` executes `let _ = msg` on wasm, wasm-gc and js, so the message is lost. The Morphir SDK must send the error text to the host through an import before it traps, or it must use MoonBit `raise` errors at the MEP boundary.
- The backend should emit `_ => @rt.no_match("<fqname>")` for each match that it cannot prove complete. Then a failed match has a Morphir name in every build mode.

## Integration notes for E1 and E2

- Extism 1.30 (in the morphir-rust lock) turns on `wasm_gc`, `wasm_function_references` and `wasm_tail_call` in wasmtime 43. The spike's wasm-gc modules ran in wasmtime with those flags. The only import to supply is `spectest.print_char`. Programs that use `@env` need the MoonBit-specific `__moonbit_fs_unstable` imports.
- The official `extism/moonbit-pdk` builds with `--target wasm`, not wasm-gc. Decision 5 in the roadmap makes component-model hosts the target. The component model canonical ABI uses linear memory. Thus `--target wasm` is the practical target for MEP guests and components, and wasm-gc is for JS and browser hosts.
- To pass strings and records across the host boundary, the backend needs an ABI: JSON bytes through the Extism PDK, or the canonical ABI through `wit-bindgen`. Scalar exports worked without an ABI.

## Risks that would change the answer

1. **License (highest).** FINOS legal could decide that Morphir cannot depend on MPSL tools, even tools that the user installs. Or Morphir could need to bundle a compiler, or members could need to host compilation as a commercial service. In those cases, route 1 (Cranelift, Apache-2.0) becomes the answer.
2. **Toolchain churn before 1.0.** In this one spike: `derive(Show)` was deprecated, `@list.from_array` was deprecated, `min_value` changed to `MIN_VALUE`, the `moon.pkg` format changed, and the worker had to match the core bundle exactly. The backend must pin a toolchain version and test against it. If the MoonBit language changes faster than Morphir can follow, the cost of route 2 increases.
3. **Semantic gaps that need a Morphir-owned SDK.** These are String ordering, integer overflow, division by zero (native returns 0), `modBy`, `Dict.union` bias, lost abort messages, and missing Decimal, date/time and Regex types. If the Morphir spec needs arbitrary-precision `Int` everywhere, all arithmetic moves to BigInt, which is larger and slower.
4. **IR shape.** The backend needs typed IR. Untyped IR needs an inference pass. Extensible records have no clean mapping.

## Side effects

- `mise exec` in `ecosystem/morphir-moonbit` installed `bun@1.3.8` and `uv@0.12.19` into the global mise install directory, because that repository's mise config declares them. No repository file changed.
- `bd show` may have created `.beads.gate.lock` files in the umbrella and morphir-rust.
- The temp directory was deleted. The emitted MoonBit is not kept; the rule table above is enough to reproduce it.

design:
# Morphir Ecosystem Model and Roadmap Status: approved design (Damian, 2026-09-26). Each capability below gets its own design and plan when its turn comes; this document is what those designs argue from. ## 1. Purpose **Intent.** Turn the Morphir plans into small capabilities that a user can see, that ship on their own, and that are not tied to one another more than they must be. Free finos/morphir-rust from being the one place every extension is built, so each language ecosystem can be served on its own. **Who it is for.** Extension authors first, then Morphir CLI users, then contributors to a language ecosystem. **Success looks like.** - A contributor can build, test and release the Python extension from finos/morphir-python without touching morphir-rust. The same holds for every language repo. - A new ecosystem repo starts from one common layout. - A PR that touches only docs, or only one extension, runs only its own CI jobs. - The roadmap is a list of capabilities, each with a user-visible result and no more than one or two dependencies. - Any capability can be taken by another engineer, agent or machine. ## 2. The repository model ### 2.1 Two halves Every ecosystem repository has two halves and follows one layout. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph repo["finos/morphir-"] native["Native half
IR support and Morphir SDK
in the language itself"] rust["Extension half
the language's MEP extension
(Rust today; a component in the language later)"] docs["Docs"] end rust -->|"cargo add"| crates["Published core crates
(from morphir-rust)"] rust -->|"release: bundle + release.json"| bundle["Extension release
(installable by the CLI)"] umbrella["finos/morphir
CLI, specs, MCK"] -->|"pins by checksum or submodule"| bundle ``` - **Native half.** The language's own reading and writing of Morphir IR, and its Morphir SDK (the standard library a generated model runs against). - **Extension half.** The language's MEP extension: frontend, backend, workspace discovery. Written in Rust today against the published core crates. Later it can be a component written in the language itself, where the language compiles to WASM (TypeScript through jco componentize, MoonBit natively). - **Docs.** The repo's own docs site or docs folder. - A repo can have an empty extension half. finos/morphir-moonbit today and finos/morphir-scala after its restructure are native-only repos in the same layout. ### 2.2 finos/morphir-rust is the special case In morphir-rust both halves are Rust. Its native half is the Rust IR (`morphir-core`), the Rust SDK, and the core crates every other repo's extension half depends on: `morphir-extension-sdk`, `morphir-host`, `morphir-host-native`, `morphir-workspace`, `morphir-common`, `morphir-projection`. Its extension half is `morphir-rust-binding`, `morphir-elm-binding` until it moves (A6), and the Morphir Scheme reference extension (D1). What follows: the core crates are published from morphir-rust, and it is the one repo where a core change fans out to its own extensions. Everywhere else a core change arrives as a crate version bump. ### 2.3 finos/morphir holds the extensions with no language home The umbrella keeps the CLI (`crates/morphir`), the specs (`spec/`), and the MCK. It gains the format extensions: Avro and OpenAPI (A5) and the WIT backend (B1). They are extensions like any other, with bundle releases, but they live next to the CLI because no language repo owns them. ### 2.4 Built into the CLI, or installed A language is **built into the CLI** when the umbrella pins its ecosystem repo as a submodule and `crates/morphir` lists it as a built-in, depending on the extension crate by path through that pin. Gleam keeps this route after it moves (A3): `morphir compile` handles Gleam with no install, and the only coupling is the pin. Every other language is **installed**: `morphir extension install ` fetches the bundle from the language repo's release. Which languages are built in is an umbrella decision, and each language repo has its own pipeline either way. A built-in language still ships a bundle, so older CLIs and non-Rust hosts can install it. A project whose `morphir.toml` names a language the CLI does not have gets a clear message with the install command. ### 2.5 Published core crates The core crates are published to crates.io on each morphir-rust release. Versions are `0.x.y`, with prereleases such as `0.5.0-beta.1` allowed. Cargo treats `x` as the breaking number of a `0.x.y` version, so a breaking change bumps `x` and an additive change bumps `y`. No crate reaches 1.0 before Morphir 1.0.0. Until the first publish, an extension repo may use a git dependency on morphir-rust pinned to a tag, as a stopgap. ### 2.6 Packaging is a CLI command, not a script to copy Today the bundle packaging is Python under morphir-rust `scripts/extension_packaging`, and it needs `morphir-host-native` in the same workspace. It becomes a command of the CLI (for example `morphir extension bundle`), so an ecosystem repo needs only the released CLI to package, verify claims, and publish. The release workflow in the common layout calls that command. ### 2.7 Change-scoped CI Each repo builds only what a change affects: the native half, the extension half, or docs, and, in a repo with more than one extension, only the extensions touched. A core crate change is the only change that fans out, and only inside morphir-rust. The umbrella's `changes` filter gets one path set per extension it holds. Every repo pins its filters with a test, as the umbrella's `tests/ci` does today. Measure: a docs-only PR or a single-extension PR runs only its own jobs. ### 2.8 Incremental delivery per extension An extension ships with the capabilities it has, and its claim set tells the host. Each extension's roadmap is a ladder, and a repo can release at any rung: 1. types-only frontend 2. values in the frontend 3. backend 4. workspace discovery (`morphir compile` with no `morphir.toml`) 5. incremental and multi-document compile No rung waits for another extension, and no capability in the map requires a whole ladder. ### 2.9 Parallel work Every capability in the map is an independent unit of work with its own bead. The dependencies in the map are the only ordering. A capability can be claimed (`bd update --claim`) by any engineer, agent or machine. ## 3. Extension direction: WIT first, components first - **Target hosts** are component-model hosts: the Rust CLI through wasmtime, and JavaScript runtimes through jco. Elixir through Gleam is possible later, not a focus now. - **Contracts are WIT.** The extension contracts are written as WIT interfaces and worlds (`morphir:mep`, `morphir:host`), with WAC where composition helps. WIT is the source of truth for worlds and functions. The Gleam model in `spec/mep` stays the source of truth for the message types, and the WIT type package is generated from it by the WIT backend (B1). Until B1 exists, a hand-written type package is checked against the model by a test. - **WASM extensions are components**, not Extism plugins. Extism is maintained, not extended, so existing installs keep working; it may be retired as component-model support matures. - **Process and native extensions stay fully supported.** They are not the focus of this push. - **The runtime is different from extensions.** The evaluator keeps a core WASM target for browsers and hosts without component-model support (D3), next to its component target (D2). ## 4. The map Five tracks. Tracks run side by side; arrows are the only dependencies. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph T1["Track 1: repos and pipelines"] A1a["A1a crate publish proof (0.0.1)"] --> A1b["A1b core crates on crates.io"] A1b --> A2["A2 layout, packaging command, scoped CI"] A2 --> A3["A3 Gleam to morphir-gleam (built in by pin)"] A2 --> A10["A10 TypeScript extension in morphir-typescript"] A2 --> A4["A4 Python to morphir-python"] A2 --> A5["A5 Avro, OpenAPI to finos/morphir"] A3 --> A6["A6 Elm-native to morphir-elm"] A3 --> A9["A9 Scala restructure, scala-elm retired"] A2 --> A7["A7 MoonBit extension"] A2 --> A8["A8 .NET extension (C#, F#)"] A2 --> A11["A11 JVM extension (Java, Kotlin)"] end subgraph T2["Track 2: WIT contract and components"] B1["B1 WIT backend, types only"] --> B2["B2 MEP contract as WIT"] B2 --> B3["B3 component extensions end to end"] B3 --> B4["B4 host as a component, JS wrapper"] B3 --> B5["B5 MCK and itest adapters as components"] end subgraph T3["Track 3: MEP model follow-ups"] C1["C1 Rust MEP types from the model"] C2["C2 MEP conformance suite"] C3["C3 guest SDK (morphir-opua.2)"] end subgraph T4["Track 4: evaluation"] D1["D1 Morphir Scheme reference extension"] --> D2["D2 runtime as a component"] D1 --> D3["D3 runtime as core WASM"] D2 --> D4["D4 language-native runtime hosts"] end subgraph T5["Track 5: Morphir to WASM"] E0["E0 spike: MoonBit route"] --> E1["E1 Morphir to MoonBit backend"] E1 --> E2["E2 wasm, native and JS targets"] end A1b -.-> B3 B2 -.-> C2 A7 -.-> E1 E1 -.-> D2 ``` ### Track 1: repos and pipelines | Id | Capability | Repo | Depends on | User result | Wave | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | A1a | Publish one leaf crate (`morphir-common`) at `0.0.1` through `release.yml` to prove the pipeline, trusted publishing and organization secrets | morphir-rust | none | The publish job works end to end | now | | A1b | Publish `morphir-core`, `morphir-extension-sdk`, `morphir-workspace`, `morphir-projection` at `0.x.y` in dependency order; metadata, dry run in CI, bump rule in docs | morphir-rust | A1a | `cargo add morphir-extension-sdk` works outside the workspace | now | | A2 | The common layout: a documented repo layout and template with two halves, mise tasks, release workflow, change-scoped CI with a filter test, and `morphir extension bundle` replacing the Python packaging scripts | finos/morphir, morphir-rust | A1b | A contributor starts a language repo and releases an extension from it | 1 | | A3 | Gleam extension moves to finos/morphir-gleam; Output is a recommendation; everything built is thrown away | morphir-moonbit | none | Route decided | | E1 | Morphir-to-MoonBit backend (in the morphir-moonbit extension) | morphir-moonbit | E0, A7 | A model compiles to MoonBit | | E2 | wasm-gc, native (C, LLVM) and JavaScript targets through MoonBit's toolchain | morphir-moonbit | E1 | A model compiles to WASM, native or JS | Routes not chosen: route 0, direct emission with `wasm-encoder` (`morphir-wasm-binding`, kept as the Extism conformance guest); route 1, a Cranelift backend (the fallback if the spike fails). ## 5. Decisions | # | Decision | Date | |---|---|---| | 1 | Core crates are published to crates.io; git dependencies pinned to a tag are the stopgap | 2026-09-25 | | 2 | Crate versions are `0.x.y` with prereleases; no 1.0 before Morphir 1.0.0 | 2026-09-25 | | 3 | morphir-rust is core plus the Rust ecosystem repo, the special case of the model | 2026-09-25 | | 4 | Gleam stays built into the CLI through the umbrella's submodule pin; built in versus installed is an umbrella decision | 2026-09-25 | | 5 | Target hosts are component-model hosts; contracts are WIT; WASM extensions are components; Extism maintained, not extended; process and native fully supported | 2026-09-25 | | 6 | WIT is the source of truth for worlds and functions; the Gleam model for types; the WIT type package is generated by the WIT backend | 2026-09-25 | | 7 | Avro, OpenAPI and the WIT backend live in finos/morphir | 2026-09-25 | | 8 | Change-scoped CI is a rule of the model | 2026-09-25 | | 9 | Elm-native moves to morphir-elm in wave 2; the Morphir Scheme dialect is the reference extension in morphir-rust | 2026-09-25 | | 10 | Two Elm frontends: the TypeScript extension and Elm-native; `morphir-scala-elm` is decommissioned | 2026-09-25 | | 11 | Incremental delivery per extension, by claim set, is a rule of the model | 2026-09-26 | | 12 | The runtime targets components, core WASM and language-native hosts, as slices | 2026-09-26 | | 13 | Morphir to WASM goes through MoonBit as the main bet, proved by a spike; Cranelift is the fallback | 2026-09-26 | | 14 | A1 starts with a `0.0.1` publish of one leaf crate to prove the pipeline | 2026-09-26 | | 15 | MCK and itest adapters become WIT components (B5) | 2026-09-26 | ## 6. Not decided here Each of these belongs to its capability's own design: - The exact directory layout and template contents (A2). - The Morphir Scheme dialect's syntax, IR coverage and name (D1). - One provider or two for .NET (C#, F#) and for JVM (Java, Kotlin) (A8, A11). - The WIT rules for generics and recursive types, including the MEP `Json` type (B1). - The `morphir:mck/adapter` world (B5). - Whether `morphir-host` and `morphir-host-native` are published crates (A2). - Ordering inside Track 4. ## 7. How work proceeds - This spec is the design of the epic "Morphir ecosystem model and roadmap". Its five tracks are child epics, and each capability is a bead under its track. The existing epics `morphir-opua.1` (host library and MEP contract) and `morphir-opua.2` (guest SDK) are linked into Tracks 2 and 3, not moved. - Each capability gets its own design and plan, stored in beads (`bd-plan spec`, `bd-plan import`), and is executed from the rendered plan. - First three items, in parallel: A1a, B1, E0.

title: refactor(daemon)!: make morphir-daemon a client of morphir-host
description:
### Task 5: Delete the daemon's duplicates

Bead: `morphir-opua.1.1.6.5`.

**Files:**
- Delete from `crates/morphir-daemon/src/extensions/`: `registry.rs`, `registry/`, `session/` (controller, transport, validation, compatibility, extism, native, tests), `actor/`, `process.rs`, `process/`, `activation.rs`, `activation/`, `connected.rs`, `protocol.rs` (`ExtensionResponseExt`; move `MAX_MEP_PAYLOAD_BYTES` users to `morphir_host_native` or the SDK constant), `container.rs`, `host_functions.rs`.
- Modify: `crates/morphir-daemon/src/extensions/mod.rs:17-31`, `crates/morphir-daemon/src/lib.rs` (prelude at line 16 and the crate doc, which claims an HTTP server and build orchestration that do not exist), `crates/morphir-daemon/Cargo.toml` (drop `kameo`, `jsonrpsee`, `extism`, and any dependency `cargo machete` or a build shows unused), `crates/morphir-daemon/examples/mep-native-backend.rs` (delete, or move to `morphir-host-native/examples` if a test or task runs it; check `rg mep-native-backend`).
- Keep: `error.rs` (`DaemonError`, including `From<HostError>`), `loader.rs` (`ExtensionLoader`), `virtual_paths.rs`, `workspace.rs`.
- Modify: `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Guard test.** Add `crates/morphir-daemon/tests/public_surface.rs`:

```rust
//! morphir-daemon is a client of morphir-host: it has no MEP codec,
//! handshake, registry or session of its own.
#[test]
fn the_daemon_keeps_only_its_own_services() {
    let _: Option<morphir_daemon::DaemonError> = None;
    let _ = morphir_daemon::ExtensionLoader::new;
    let _ = std::mem::size_of::<morphir_daemon::VirtualPathConfig>();
}
```

and a check in the step below that `rg -n 'MepTransport|ExtensionRegistry|spawn_session|activate_transport|ExtensionResponseExt|ConnectedDaemonSession' crates` returns nothing.
- [ ] **Step 2: Delete** the files, fix `mod.rs`/`lib.rs`, drop the dependencies.
- [ ] **Step 3: Run** `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo test -p morphir-daemon`, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` (flakes: `--test-threads=1`), clippy `-D warnings`, `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-Dwarnings cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and the `rg` check.
- [ ] **Step 4: CHANGELOG** `[Unreleased]`:
  - `### Removed`: from `morphir-daemon`: `ExtensionRegistry` and its resolved types, the typestate `Session`, `MepTransport`, the session actor (`SessionHandle`, `spawn_session`), `ExtensionSession`, `SpawnedProcessSession`, `SpawnedProcessTransport`, `ExtismTransport`, `NativeMepTransport`, `activate_transport`, `ExtensionResponseExt`, `ConnectedDaemonSession`, `ProcessDescription`, and the `ExtensionContainer`/`MorphirHostFunctions` re-exports. Their replacements: `morphir_host::{Registry, Session, Pool}`, `morphir_host_native::{activate, describe, ProcessChannel, ExtismChannel, NativeChannel}`, `morphir_host_native::http::HttpChannel` (feature `http`).
  - `### Changed`: `CallError` variants (task 1), `Pool` idle eviction (task 2), the moved tests and mise tasks.
- [ ] **Step 5: Commit** `refactor(daemon)!: make morphir-daemon a client of morphir-host` with a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer naming the removed public items.

title: Gate: canonical form for comparing two claim sets (#921 Q1)
description: #921 open question 1: what canonical form two claim sets take before comparison (key order, number spelling). In practice the host compares parsed JSON values (morphir-distribution check_claims, ClaimsRecord::check_described), which is insensitive to key order and number spelling. Resolve by recording that rule in a Decision Record, or postpone formally with a reason.

title: Gate: whether publish probes WASM artifacts (#921 Q2)
description: #921 open question 2: does publish also probe WASM artifacts it can always run, and should that be required? Today no WASM artifact is probed; publish and install record claimCheck unchecked, and packaging instead reads the claims from the shipped guest bytes (extension-claims) and checks them against .github/extensions.toml. Resolve by recording that rule (or a change to it) in a Decision Record, or postpone formally.

title: Gate: claims under artifact provenance or signature (#921 Q3)
description: #921 open question 3: should the claim set be covered by the artifact's provenance or signature once publisher authenticity exists (distribution open question 4)? title: Gate: operating-system sandbox for process probes (#921 Q4)
description: #921 open question 4: can a process probe run in an OS sandbox where one is available (restricted profile on macOS, namespace on Linux)? title: Host library and MEP contract (finos/morphir#958)
description: The design is finos/morphir discussion 949, checkpoints 1-17. Tracking of this work now lives in beads, under this epic. The GitHub issues under finos/morphir#958 (phases #959-#962 and their sub-issues) stay open as mirrors and link back to their matching bead.
design:
# Morphir host library and MEP contract: design Status: design approved on 2026-09-23. This spec is waiting for review. Record: https://github.com/finos/morphir/discussions/949 (checkpoints 1 to 17). Beads: `morphir-opua` (extension SDK). This design is its host piece. Code blocks marked "sketch" show the shape of an idea. They are not the final API. ## 1. Goal Give every Morphir client one host library. The library finds the project, builds the MEP request, and talks to an extension guest. The same library serves the CLI, the desktop workbench, servers, and browsers. It also serves TypeScript and Python callers through the WASM component model. The MEP contract becomes a Morphir model. A Gleam module defines it. Morphir backends generate each binding and each language's types from it. Success looks like this: - `morphir compile`, `morphir generate`, and `morphir extension install` call `morphir-host`. The CLI no longer builds MEP requests or hardcodes `morphir-cli` as the peer name. - The web workbench uses the host pool. `crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/provider/sessions.rs` is gone. - `spec/mep/contract/mep.gleam` is the single source of the contract. CI fails when generated files drift. - A component guest and a process guest answer the same `Session::compile` call. - A TypeScript caller and a Python caller open a session through the host compiled to a component. They pass the same MEP conformance suite as the Rust host. ## 2. Terms - **Host library.** `morphir-host`. The in-process library that discovers a project, builds the guest request, and talks to the guest. - **CLI client.** The `morphir` command. It parses arguments, calls the host library, writes files, and prints diagnostics. - **Guest.** An extension that answers MEP calls: a native Rust guest, a process, or a WASM component. - **Session.** One live guest after the handshake. - **MEP.** The Morphir Extension Protocol, with its methods, capability statement, and version handshake. - **Binding.** One wire form of MEP: JSON-RPC, or a typed WIT world. ## 3. Scope In scope: - The host library in Rust (`morphir-host`) and its component form. - The MEP contract as a Gleam model, its bindings, and its versioning rule. - How the contract is published, downloaded, and checked. - The CLI, the workbench, and `morphir-daemon` as clients. - The TypeScript and Python host wrappers. Out of scope: - Moving the session host out of the CLI as its own project. - The public compile entry points in finos/morphir#897 (beads `morphir-t9cg`). This design gives those callers types they can use. - Moving the Elm package-name rule (kb `morphir-extensions` decision 0005) into the SDK. That is a later piece of `morphir-opua`. - The guest-authoring API. ## 4. Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph U["finos/morphir (umbrella)"] G["spec/mep/contract/mep.gleam"] -->|"morphir-gleam"| IR["MEP Library IR
(published model)"] K["spec/mep/mck
host and guest suites"] end IR -->|"backends"| B["Rust types, WIT morphir:mep, JSON Schema, TS, Python"] subgraph H["finos/morphir-rust: morphir-host"] CORE["sans-IO core: handshake, codec, version negotiation"] S["Session, one-shot helpers, Pool, Registry"] GC["GuestConnection: Native | JsonRpc over Channel | Component"] CORE --> S --> GC end B --> H CLI["morphir CLI"] --> S WB["web workbench"] --> S D["morphir-daemon"] --> S H -->|"morphir:host (async)"| TS["TypeScript wrapper (jco)"] H -->|"morphir:host-sync"| PY["Python wrapper (wasmtime-py)"] K -.->|"checks"| H K -.->|"checks"| TS K -.->|"checks"| PY ``` ### 4.1 The CLI and the host library (checkpoints 3 and 4) The host is a library linked into the `morphir` binary. There is no separate host program. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant CLI as CLI client participant HL as Host library participant G as Elm guest User->>CLI: morphir compile src/Foo.elm --package-name My.Package CLI->>CLI: check compile cache CLI->>HL: compile(files, language = elm, package = My.Package, peer) HL->>HL: discover project, normalize name to my/package HL->>G: initialize, then compile request G-->>HL: IR and diagnostics HL-->>CLI: result CLI->>CLI: write IR to output path, update cache CLI-->>User: print diagnostics ``` The work splits like this: | Operation | CLI client owns | Host library owns | | --- | --- | --- | | compile | output paths, compile cache, configuration warnings | project discovery, request building, frontend guest call | | generate | finding IR on disk, output directory, writing files | backend selection, backend guest call | | probe (install) | copying files, updating the catalog | handshake, `describe`, session fallback, `check_statement` | - The client passes its peer name and version. The library never hardcodes `morphir-cli`. - Compile, generate, and probe advertise one list of supported MEP versions. - `ConnectedDaemonSession` stays a way to reach an extension over HTTP. The CLI does not use it to reach the host library. ### 4.2 Layers (checkpoint 5) ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph clients["Clients"] CLI["morphir compile / generate / install"] WB["web workbench"] SRV["server"] BR["browser (WASM + JS)"] end subgraph HL["morphir-host"] OS["One-shot helpers
compile, generate, probe"] POOL["Pool (optional)
reuse per key, evict a stopped guest, retry once"] S["Session
handshake, capabilities, compile, generate, describe"] OS --> S POOL --> S end CLI --> OS WB --> POOL SRV --> POOL SRV --> S BR --> S ``` 1. **Session.** `open(guest, peer)` starts the guest, negotiates the version, and stores the capabilities. The client owns the session's lifetime. 2. **One-shot helpers.** These open a session, make one call, and close it. `morphir compile`, `morphir generate`, and install use them. Probe opens a session, reads the capabilities, checks the statement, and closes the session. 3. **Pool.** An optional helper on top of sessions. It keeps one guest for each key, removes a guest that stopped, and retries a request once on a new guest. This is the logic of `sessions.rs` today. The library keeps no hidden global state. The client decides pool size, idle time, and tenant limits. ```rust // sketch impl Session { pub async fn open(guest: GuestSource, peer: PeerInfo) -> Result; pub fn capabilities(&self) -> &Capabilities; pub async fn compile(&mut self, request: CompileRequest) -> Result; pub async fn generate(&mut self, request: GenerateRequest) -> Result; pub async fn describe(&mut self) -> Result; pub async fn close(self) -> Result<()>; } pub async fn compile_once(guest: GuestSource, peer: PeerInfo, request: CompileRequest) -> Result; impl Pool { pub async fn compile(&self, key: K, request: CompileRequest) -> Result; pub async fn generate(&self, key: K, request: GenerateRequest) -> Result; pub async fn abandon(&self, key: &K); } ``` ### 4.3 Crates (checkpoint 6) ```mermaid flowchart TB CLI["morphir CLI"] --> HN D["morphir-daemon"] --> HN JS["browser JS"] --> HW HN["native transports
(crate or feature)
process stdio, Extism, wasmtime"] --> H HW["morphir-host-wasm
(later)"] --> H H["morphir-host
portable core, compiles for wasm32"] H --> SDK["morphir-extension-sdk
protocol types, check_statement"] H --> WS["morphir-workspace
discover_with_identity"] ``` - `morphir-host` has no tokio process code and compiles for `wasm32`. It does not depend on any language binding. - Process stdio and Extism transports move out of `morphir-daemon` into a native crate or a feature. - `morphir-daemon` becomes one more client of `morphir-host`. - The name `morphir-runtime` stays reserved, because elsewhere in the ecosystem "runtime" means the IR evaluator. ### 4.4 Transport (checkpoint 10) ```mermaid flowchart TB S["Session and Pool"] --> C{"GuestConnection
typed calls"} C --> N["NativeConnection
in-process Rust guest"] C --> JR["JsonRpcConnection
MEP codec, written once"] C --> CM["ComponentConnection
WIT exports"] JR --> CH{"Channel
messages"} CH --> ST["process stdio"] CH --> HT["HTTP"] CH --> WW["Web Worker postMessage"] CM --> WT["wasmtime (native)"] CM --> JCO["jco (browser)"] HS["HostServices
log, progress, read-file"] -.->|"guest calls back"| C ``` ```rust // sketch #[cfg_attr(not(target_arch = "wasm32"), async_trait)] #[cfg_attr(target_arch = "wasm32", async_trait(?Send))] pub trait GuestConnection { async fn initialize(&mut self, params: InitializeParams) -> Result; async fn describe(&mut self) -> Result; async fn compile(&mut self, request: CompileRequest) -> Result; async fn generate(&mut self, request: GenerateRequest) -> Result; async fn close(&mut self) -> Result<()>; } #[cfg_attr(not(target_arch = "wasm32"), async_trait)] #[cfg_attr(target_arch = "wasm32", async_trait(?Send))] pub trait Channel { async fn send(&mut self, message: JsonRpcMessage) -> Result<()>; async fn receive(&mut self) -> Result; } pub trait HostServices { fn log(&self, level: LogLevel, message: &str); fn read_file(&self, path: &str) -> Result; } ``` - `JsonRpcConnection` owns the MEP codec. It matches request ids, maps RPC errors such as `-32014` to Rust errors, uses must-ignore readers, and normalizes legacy request shapes. - A `Channel` moves messages only. It contains no MEP method names. - `ComponentConnection` calls WIT exports with typed records and builds no JSON. - Each client supplies `HostServices`. The JSON-RPC connection routes guest requests to it. The component connection wires it as the WIT `host` imports. - `MepTransport` requires `Send`. The new traits drop `Send` on `wasm32`. ### 4.5 Registry (checkpoint 14) `morphir-host` defines `Registry` and `GuestSource`. Each client registers its own guests. ```rust // sketch: CLI let mut registry = Registry::new(); registry.register(GuestSource::native(gleam_guest()))?; if elm_requested { registry.register(GuestSource::native(elm_guest()))?; } for snapshot in catalog.installed() { registry.register(GuestSource::from_installed(snapshot))?; } ``` The CLI keeps today's rules from `crates/morphir/src/extensions.rs`. A browser client registers only component guests. When a second client needs the same default set, a small composition crate takes over the list at that time. ### 4.6 Sans-IO core and the component worlds (checkpoints 16 and 17) The protocol logic lives in a sans-IO core. An async shell and a sync world both drive it. ```rust // sketch pub enum Event { Opened, Received(JsonRpcMessage), Call(Request), Closed } pub enum Action { Send(JsonRpcMessage), Complete(RequestId, Response), Fail(RequestId, Error), Close } impl SessionCore { pub fn handle(&mut self, event: Event) -> Vec; } ``` ```mermaid flowchart TB CORE["SessionCore (sans-IO)"] CORE --> ASYNC["async shell
world morphir:host"] CORE --> SYNC["sync world
morphir:host-sync"] ASYNC --> RS["native Rust (Wasmtime 46+)"] ASYNC --> JS["Node and browsers (jco, JSPI)"] SYNC --> PY["Python (wasmtime-py)"] ``` - `morphir:host` exports `Session`, `Pool`, the one-shot calls, and `Registry` as `async func`. It imports async `send` and `receive`. - `morphir:host-sync` exports the core's `handle` function. The embedder runs the event loop. - The embedder supplies `Channel` and `HostServices` as imports, because a Wasm component cannot start processes. - The TypeScript wrapper uses `morphir:host` through jco. It falls back to `morphir:host-sync` if jco P3 is not stable enough for a release. - The Python wrapper uses `morphir:host-sync` with an asyncio loop. It moves to `morphir:host` when wasmtime-py supports component model async. - The WIT does not use `error-context`. Support as of 2026-09-23: | Embedder | Component model async | | --- | --- | | Native Rust, Wasmtime 46 or later | Supported, on by default | | Rust guest, wit-bindgen 0.62 | Supported | | Node and browsers, jco 1.34 | Experimental, uses JSPI (Chrome 137, Firefox 153, Safari 27) | | Python, wasmtime-py 49 | Not supported (bytecodealliance/wasmtime#13705) | ```ts // sketch: TypeScript wrapper import { Session } from "@finos/morphir-host"; using session = await Session.open(processGuest("morphir-elm"), peer); const result = await session.compile(request); ``` ## 5. The MEP contract ### 5.1 One contract, two bindings (checkpoint 7) ```mermaid flowchart TB M["MEP contract
methods, capabilities, handshake"] M --> J["JSON-RPC binding
stdio or HTTP"] M --> W["WIT binding
morphir:mep world"] ``` ```wit // sketch package morphir:mep@0.1.0; interface frontend { use types.{compile-request, compile-result, diagnostic}; compile: func(request: compile-request) -> result>; } interface host { log: func(level: log-level, message: string); read-file: func(path: string) -> result; } world frontend-guest { import host; export lifecycle; // initialize, describe export frontend; } ``` The envelope style of `morphir:ext@0.1.0` is not the component binding of MEP. ### 5.2 Versioning (checkpoint 8) Before 1.0.0: - A breaking change bumps the minor version (`0.2.x` to `0.3.0`). - An additive, backward-compatible change bumps the patch version. `@since` marks new WIT items. - The JSON-RPC handshake sends the canonical version, for example `"0.2"`. The WIT package carries the full version, for example `morphir:mep@0.2.3`. - `SUPPORTED_MEP_VERSIONS` lists canonical versions. - Published contracts carry no prerelease tags. The component model never splits a prerelease version, so each draft would need an exact match. After 1.0.0, MEP uses standard SemVer. ### 5.3 Source of truth (checkpoint 9) ```mermaid flowchart LR G["mep.gleam"] -->|"morphir-gleam frontend
works now"| IR["Morphir IR"] IR -->|"new backend"| WIT["WIT world"] IR -->|"morphir-openapi json-schema
needs fixes"| JS["JSON Schema"] IR -->|"morphir-rust, works now"| RS["Rust types"] IR -->|"backend to choose"| TS["TypeScript types"] IR -->|"morphir-python, needs List, Maybe, generics"| PY["Python types"] ``` ```gleam // sketch: mep.gleam import gleam/option.{type Option} pub type Diagnostic { Diagnostic(severity: Severity, message: String, path: Option(String)) } pub type CompileRequest { CompileRequest(language_id: String, sources: List(Source), package: CompilePackage) } pub type Frontend { Frontend(compile: fn(CompileRequest) -> Result(CompileResult, List(Diagnostic))) } ``` - Contract records use labelled fields. - WIT has no recursive types. The WIT backend rejects them, or encodes them the way `morphir:ir` `encoded-ast` does. - The generated files are committed, and CI checks them for drift. The contract never depends on a guest that it defines. ### 5.4 IR payloads (checkpoint 13) ```gleam // sketch pub type IrLayout { Classic DocumentTree } pub type IrPayload { IrPayload(media_type: String, layout: IrLayout, data: BitArray) } ``` - Guest capabilities list the IR formats the guest accepts and produces. - The host sends the format on disk when the guest accepts it. Otherwise the host converts the IR one time. - JSON-RPC carries JSON IR inline, Ion text as a string, and Ion binary as base64. WIT carries `list`. - `CompileResult.ir` and `GenerateRequest.ir` change from `serde_json::Value` to `IrPayload`. - This depends on the Ion codec work in finos/morphir-rust#233 and finos/morphir#951. ## 6. Where the contract lives and how it travels ### 6.1 Folder (checkpoints 11 and 15) ```text spec/mep/ README.md what MEP is, the versioning rule contract/ Gleam project, the source of truth gleam.toml src/mep.gleam generated/ committed, CI drift check in the umbrella mep.ir.json json-schema/ wit/morphir-mep/ mck/ host and guest conformance suites ``` The root `wit/` folder splits by subject: - `morphir:extension`, `morphir:frontend`, `morphir:backend`, `morphir:component`, and `morphir:vfs` get a README that marks them superseded. They are deleted when the first generated `morphir:mep` WIT lands. Their incremental, streaming, and vfs ideas become candidate capabilities for `mep.gleam` first. - `morphir:ir` moves to `spec/ir/wit/`. The kb mirror in morphir-scala updates its mapping. ### 6.2 Publishing (checkpoint 12) ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph U["finos/morphir"] C["mep.gleam"] -->|"compile"| IR["Library IR"] IR -->|"pack + publish (to build)"| REG[("model registry")] K["spec/mep/mck"] -->|"mck kit, suite mep"| KIT["conformance kit"] end REG -->|"morphir package resolve / restore"| LR["language repo
restored IR"] LR -->|"morphir generate"| T["types and bindings, committed"] KIT -->|"mck kit vendor"| LR2["language repo
MEP conformance tests"] ``` - The contract is a Morphir Library package, for example `finos.org/morphir/mep@0.2.3` with IR package `morphir/mep`. - Consumers derive WIT, JSON Schema, and language types from the IR. - The conformance cases travel as an MCK suite named `mep`. - Until `publish` exists, each language repo commits a copy of the IR from an exact umbrella commit, with source and digest. When `publish` exists, that copy becomes `morphir package restore`. Package format requirements that MEP adds: 1. A package can be a zip archive. 2. A package can carry document-tree IR. 3. A package supports Amazon Ion text and Ion binary. The default between them is still open. ## 7. Error handling - A failed handshake or version mismatch fails `Session::open` with the guest's supported versions and the host's list. - RPC errors map to typed Rust errors in `JsonRpcConnection`. `-32014` (lifecycle refusal) keeps its meaning. - The pool evicts a session whose guest stopped, opens a new one, and retries the request one time. A second loss fails the request and clears the pool entry. A guest rejection fails the request and keeps the session. These are the rules in `sessions.rs` today. - A guest that does not accept the IR format on disk and cannot take a conversion fails with a capability error before the call. - Probe keeps today's provenance rules: `statementSource` probed or declared, and `probeSource` describe or session fallback. ## 8. Testing - **Sans-IO core.** Feed events in and compare the actions that come out. No runtime. - **Session and pool.** Use a fake `GuestConnection` with typed values. Port the five `sessions.rs` tests: shared session, reuse across compile and generate, evict and retry once, a retry that also loses its session fails and clears the entry, and a rejection keeps the session. - **Codec.** Use a fake `Channel` with golden JSON messages, including the legacy `documents` shape. - **Contract.** CI compiles `mep.gleam` and fails on drift in `spec/mep/generated/`. - **Conformance.** The `mep` MCK suite has host cases (a scripted guest, the messages the host must send, and how it must react) and guest cases. The Rust host, the TypeScript wrapper, and the Python wrapper all run the host suite. - **Released guests.** Before merging a CLI change, run the CLI tests and the real released providers (Elm 0.3.1, scala-elm M08), as for the capability-statements work. ## 9. Work breakdown Each item is a candidate issue. Items in the same group can run in parallel. **A. Host library in the CLI (first slice)** 1. Create the `morphir-host` crate with the sans-IO `SessionCore`: handshake, version negotiation, client-supplied peer. (finos/morphir-rust) 2. Add `GuestConnection`, `Channel`, `HostServices`, `JsonRpcConnection`, a process stdio channel, and a native connection. Add `Session` and the one-shot helpers. (finos/morphir-rust) 3. Add `Registry` and `GuestSource`. (finos/morphir-rust) 4. Move CLI compile, generate, and probe onto `morphir-host`. Remove `host_initialize_params`. (finos/morphir) 5. Add `Pool`, and move the web workbench off `sessions.rs`. (finos/morphir-rust, finos/morphir) 6. Make `morphir-daemon` a client of `morphir-host`, and move the process and Extism transports out of it. (finos/morphir-rust) **B. The MEP contract as a model** 7. Create `spec/mep/` with `README.md` and `contract/mep.gleam`, modelled on today's Rust protocol types. Add the drift check. (finos/morphir) 8. Generate the Rust protocol types from the IR with `morphir-rust`, and commit the IR copy in finos/morphir-rust. (finos/morphir-rust) 9. Fix the JSON Schema backend: single-constructor types as plain objects, and generic declarations. (finos/morphir-rust) 10. Add a Morphir to WIT backend. (finos/morphir-rust) 11. Close the Python backend gaps: `List`, `Maybe`, and generics. (finos/morphir-rust) 12. Add `BitArray` or an SDK `Bytes` type to the Gleam frontend. (finos/morphir-rust) 13. Add the `mep` MCK suite, with host cases and guest cases. (finos/morphir) 14. Split the root `wit/` folder and list the candidate capabilities. (finos/morphir) **C. Formats and packages** 15. Add `IrPayload` and IR format capabilities to MEP. Depends on the Ion codec. (finos/morphir, finos/morphir-rust) 16. Package format: zip archive, document-tree IR, and Ion. Link to the existing package work (`morphir-uhk3`). (finos/morphir) 17. Publish the MEP contract as a model package when `pack` and `publish` exist. (finos/morphir) **D. Component model and ports** 18. Add `ComponentConnection` over Wasmtime. (finos/morphir-rust) 19. Compile `morphir-host` to a component with the `morphir:host` and `morphir:host-sync` worlds. (finos/morphir-rust) 20. Add the TypeScript host wrapper with jco. (finos/morphir-typescript) 21. Add the Python host wrapper with wasmtime-py. (finos/morphir-python) ## 10. Risks and open items - jco P3 is experimental. The TypeScript wrapper may start on `morphir:host-sync`. - wasmtime-py has no async. Python stays on `morphir:host-sync` until it does. - No `pack` or `publish` command exists yet. The IR copy bridges the gap. - The Gleam frontend has no `BitArray` today. - The default Ion form, text or binary, is still open. - No TypeScript types backend exists in the new toolchain. Item 20 needs a choice of generator.

## Status and how to continue (2026-09-25)

**Goal.** One extension SDK for guests and hosts across runtimes. This epic builds the portable host library (`morphir-host`, wasm32-clean, with `morphir-host-native` for processes, Extism and HTTP) and the MEP contract as a Morphir model, then ports the host to the component model with TypeScript and Python wrappers.

**Done.**
- Phase A, host library in the CLI (`morphir-opua.1.1`, finos/morphir#959): finos/morphir-rust#252, #263, #271, #275 and finos/morphir#982, #989, #995, #998. `morphir-daemon` is now a client of `morphir-host`.
- Phase B first step, MEP contract model (`morphir-opua.1.2.1`, #964): finos/morphir#1005. `spec/mep/contract/src/mep.gleam`, committed IR `spec/mep/generated/mep.ir.json`, drift check in the CLI test job.
- Tracking moved to beads; plan discussions #976, #983, #992 are closed. Design record: discussion #949.

**Next.** Phase B (`morphir-opua.1.2`, #960). Ready: `.1.2.2` generate the Rust MEP protocol types from `mep.ir.json` (finos/morphir-rust#241; suggested next, the README wire mapping and integer widths feed it), `.1.2.7` MEP conformance suite (#965), `.1.2.3` JSON Schema fixes (#242), `.1.2.4` WIT backend (#243), `.1.2.5` Python backend gaps (#244), `.1.2.6` Gleam BitArray (#245). Then Phase C (`morphir-opua.1.3`) and Phase D (`morphir-opua.1.4`, including `HostServices`, `morphir-opua.1.4.5`).

**Where things are.**
- Specs: design of `morphir-opua` (cross-language SDK) and of `morphir-opua.1` (host library). Render: `mise run beads:plan -- spec <id> --render`.
- Plans: plan epics `morphir-opua.1.1.7` to `.1.1.10` (Phase A parts 1-4) and `morphir-opua.1.2.1.1` (MEP contract). Render: `mise run beads:plan -- render <plan-epic>`. Ledgers are comments on each plan epic.
- Deferred items recorded in the part 4 ledger: split pool open failures further only if a client needs it; Pool retry policy for decode failures is done (`Invalid`); idle eviction is `Pool::tick`/`evict_idle`.

**How to continue.**
1. `bd show morphir-opua.1 --long`, `bd list --parent morphir-opua.1.2 --all`, `bd ready`.
2. Write the plan with superpowers writing-plans, store it with `mise run beads:plan -- import <plan.md> --parent <bead> --spec morphir-opua.1`, execute subagent-driven from the rendered file, log with `bd-plan ledger` (AGENTS.md, "Superpowers artifacts live in beads").
3. Work rules: umbrella PRs target `main` unless a milestone branch is named; finos/morphir-rust PRs target `main`; merges need Damian's per-PR approval (`main` needs `--admin`); monitor PRs and address every review comment before merging; do not watch main CI after a merge unless asked.
4. Sync after beads changes: `bd dolt commit && bd dolt push`, `mise run beads:publish`, `git push origin beads-sync`.

title: Design portable V3/V4 node addresses, index, and URIs
description: Define a typed semantic NodeAddress and version-aware node index for addressable V3 and V4 IR nodes. Specify a portable Morphir URI serialization independent of JSON, YAML, document-tree layout, and host. Support convenient unpinned URIs that resolve against a supplied current artifact with explicit stale or ambiguous target diagnostics, plus optional revision-pinned permalinks that resolve only against the identified immutable artifact revision. Browser URLs derive from the Morphir URI. Reconcile legacy V3 decorator NodeIDs and existing V4 document URIs/cursors without inheriting their gaps. Keep exact wire syntax in draft until reviewed; this task defines the shared address contract needed by V3/V4 sidecars and later native metadata.
design: Draft design in finos/morphir#957: typed semantic address and V3/V4 indexes; portable URI independent of serialization; unpinned current-artifact resolution with explicit stale/ambiguous outcomes; optional exact immutable revision pin; derived browser links. Pending review of artifact/revision namespace, guarded positional steps, URI grammar, and legacy key translation before implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Reviewed artifact scope, root node kind/name, typed child path, IR version and optional revision model; URI parse/render and resolver contract; fixed V3/V4 positive and negative fixtures for nested nodes, JSON/YAML/tree layouts, escaping, stale and ambiguous targets, revision/version mismatch and sidecar key compatibility; index proves target existence and uniqueness with no silent retargeting; browser-link derivation specified; V4 native metadata migration boundary remains open.
notes:
Expanded finos/morphir#957 with a V4 type/field excerpt, typed NodeAddress and candidate URI snippets, V3 NodeID translation, node-kind and serialization-layout tables, and current-versus-pinned resolution cases. URI spelling and digest/guard algorithms remain draft pending design review.
finos/morphir#957 now shows proposed same-file versioned V3 and V4 sidecar JSON, seven V3 NodeID-to-semantic-URI cases, and an explicit shape-aware migration algorithm. Historical fixture /type and /value spellings are handled as tested compatibility inputs; all-or-nothing migration, collisions and invalid targets are covered. Draft envelope and URI grammar await review.
Draft spec and 49 reference-only cases are in finos/morphir#973 (branch feat/ir-node-addresses-957). Independent review corrected the canonical V4 Public wrapper and V3 TypeID custom-type exception. Issue #957 now links the PR. Open before closing: exhaustive V3/V4 child-role grammar and cases, custom constructor argument mapping, canonical guard/revision digest vectors, and executable adapter/index roundtrips. PR remains draft; no MCK compatibility claim.
Decision 2026-09-24: unpinned indexed URIs use a semantic node fingerprint of each ordered-step role, index, and selected child, not a whole-artifact revision guard. Unrelated artifact edits and later sibling appends retain the link; changed selected children or shifted indexed lineage become stale when distinguishable. Recorded in #957 and draft PR #973 with three new reference cases (52 total). Canonical cross-format digest encoding and vectors remain open.

title: Add golden file and span assertions to morphir itest
description: Extend the existing real-CLI scenario driver with golden-style assertions for complete file contents and selected spans. Support both notebook and Markdown authoring, fixed expected fixtures or inline expected text, useful mismatch diagnostics, and existing Rego/native evaluator architecture. Decide span selection and authoring contract before implementation, then drive it with failing integration scenarios and regression checks.
design: Proposed first increment: first-class golden assertions shared by Markdown and notebooks, with authored expected text kept on disk or supplied inline. Exact UTF-8 whole-file comparison by default; optional explicit line-range or marker-delimited selection, pending user preference. Preserve whitespace and final-newline significance; any line-ending normalization must be explicit. Load expected content before CLI commands and capture actual output immediately after its referenced command. Missing files, invalid/out-of-range spans and missing/ambiguous markers fail. Render unified diffs with source path/selected range; keep artifacts under --keep-temp. Preserve the existing real-CLI and morphir eval provider boundary, lowering golden equality into the same evaluator request rather than introducing a second external runner. Alternatives considered: raw Rego comparisons are already possible but require boilerplate and lack focused diagnostics; separate snapshot runner duplicates the scenario pipeline. No automatic blessing/update mode in the first increment. Add red/green CLI regressions for both formats, adopted golden example, developer/KB/skill documentation. Authoring syntax and span-selection scope are awaiting design review; no implementation edits yet.
acceptance_criteria: Both scenario formats can compare full generated files and selected spans against authored expectations. Mismatches fail with readable diffs; missing files, invalid selectors and ambiguous marker matches cannot pass. Expected content is independent of generated output. Existing assertions remain compatible. Documentation, example coverage and local skill explain authoring and diagnostics.
notes:

title: Design the full Library lock and registry-record contract
description: Develop an approved worked two-Library morphir.lock and local registry-record contract using the existing eligibility and loan-rules fixtures. Explore context, settle scope, compare approaches, review design sections, write an ignored working design, self-review it, obtain user review, then prepare an implementation plan.
