notes:
Approved scope: published Libraries in a local-directory registry first; snapshots and Git/HTTPS are follow-up profiles. Next proposed boundary, not yet approved: keep exact graph/digests and pinned registry provenance portable in morphir.lock; machine-local registry roots and trusted keys live in explicit configuration. A local binding locates bytes and must not itself confer package authority. Compare this with embedding absolute paths or using a content-only lock; preserve signed release verification and offline replay without version selection.
User approved the portable-lock/document boundary: release manifest owns package/IR identity, requirements, exports and content declarations; registry record owns release metadata, location and signed release statement; morphir.lock owns exact graph/bindings/digests/pinned provenance and evidence; explicit local configuration supplies filesystem roots and trusted authorities/keys. Location does not grant authority; evidence does not authorize itself. Next proposed section remains unapproved: content-digest-pinned immutable registry snapshots, explicit resolve/update versus exact offline replay, replay under current caller trust policy without claiming latest revocation knowledge.
User approved immutable registry snapshot and exact replay behavior. Registry snapshots are index revisions, not deferred unpublished package snapshots. Digest-pinned authenticated snapshots supply resolution metadata/status; explicit updates may choose a newer snapshot. Ordinary replay preserves selections and lock bytes, requires exact local metadata/signatures/content, and never substitutes another release. Current caller trust policy applies known revocations; unavailable required freshness fails with a specific diagnostic and no implicit network access. Next proposed section, not yet approved: unpacked local bundles, immutable digest-addressed metadata/content, and publication of a new snapshot only after full validation and staging; serialize writers and check expected current revision; identical republication is idempotent without clearing status, conflicting content is rejected.
User approved local storage/publication section: unpacked bundles first; immutable digest-addressed content and metadata; release records carry exact release/IR identity, requirements, manifest/content digests, signed release statement and typed registry-relative location. Duplicated metadata must match the verified manifest. Mutable status belongs to snapshots. Stage/validate content, store immutable objects, construct/sign snapshot, then atomically advance current revision with serialized writers and an expected-revision check. Identical verified republication is idempotent, conflicting content rejected, and republication never clears yank/revocation. Next proposed verification/MCK section remains unapproved: phase-ordered lock/metadata/trust checks, safe copying and hashing of exact bytes into private staging, IR identity/binding validation, atomic per-bundle publication and graph-level success only after all nodes verify. Distinct structured failures; no hooks, network fallback, version substitution, or claim of public-specification compatibility.
User approved verification and MCK boundary: validate exact lock/capabilities, authenticate metadata and release statements under caller policy, copy/hash exact declared bytes in private staging with path/link/entry/resource checks, verify manifest/content/IR identity/exports/bindings, atomically publish verified bundles, and report graph readiness only when all required nodes pass. Failed dependencies never cause version substitution or incomplete graph exposure. Cache path names are not integrity evidence. Fixed shared-MCK cases include real temporary-directory filesystem tests and interrupted/concurrent/conflicting publication; TypeScript owns the runner and Rust uses its adapter. Integrity/authorization does not claim public-specification or behavioral compatibility. Next proposed shape remains unapproved: a versioned morphir.lock envelope retains draft.2 LockedGraph unchanged, adds policy identification, logical registry snapshot pins, one acquisition entry per exact graph release, and digest-pinned verifiable evidence references. Keep timestamps and machine-specific verification reports outside the lock; every reference must resolve to available verified metadata for offline replay.
User approved full-lock section shape: versioned envelope with resolution, unchanged draft.2 graph, registries, acquisitions, evidence. One acquisition per graph release, exact identity/digest agreement, digest-referenced metadata must be available locally for offline replay. Machine paths, credentials and verification timestamps stay outside the lock; separate reports, no authoritative verified flag. Consolidated approved sections into ignored .dev/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-17-package-lock-registry-design.md. Wire details remain unfinished. Must reconcile registry snapshot mapping, publication authority, signed package statements and offline historical-evidence/expiry semantics before calling this implementation-ready.

Updated local working design to distinguish the approved direction from proposed mapping: TUF targets authenticate package records/statements and signed status; snapshot plus targets form the logical registry revision, not a second custom signed index; timestamp handles refresh freshness. Lock pins exact metadata digests. Explicit out-of-band PackagePath namespace authorization must accompany repository trust, with component-wise prefix matching. Separate publisher-signed package statements remain required. TUF freshness/rollback checks cannot be bypassed by presenting old lock evidence. These mapping details remain for review; no implementation started.
User approved concrete TUF role mapping and namespace-scoped authority. Working design now distinguishes that approved mapping from proposed DSSE/Ed25519 release statements and offline authorization policy. Recommendation: fresh TUF metadata for new resolution/update/first restore; durable local security authorization can permit continued exact offline reuse after metadata expiry, subject to current trust policy and known revocations. Such authorization is not a portable lock flag or disposable report/cache entry. Newer fresh metadata may authorize the same locked release without changing graph/provenance. DSSE keyid is only a hint, publisher key authorization is namespace-scoped and separate from TUF roles. These proposals remain unapproved; do not disable TUF expiry/rollback checks. Source review used DSSE 1.0.2 and TUF 1.0.36.
User approved DSSE/Ed25519 package release statements and offline policy. Self-review clarified: TUF timestamp publication is the final registry commit point, pinned historical evidence is not a fresh TUF load, and verification reports are not durable security authorization. Full signed two-Library fixture and normative field/security-state schemas remain required before runtime implementation.

title: Design ecosystem-wide Morphir package distribution
description: Synthesize the package research and designs in finos/morphir and morphir-scala, compare relevant ecosystem package systems, and define a coherent package format, identity, dependency resolution, repository, transport, trust, workspace, and CLI design for Morphir model packages. This design prepares the vertical slice tracked by morphir-uhk3.
acceptance_criteria: The reviewed design defines canonical domain terms and invariants; reconciles existing umbrella and Scala proposals; evaluates 2-3 architectural approaches; specifies package identity, immutable content, manifests, dependency constraints and locks, source descriptors, repository/index behavior, trust and integrity, offline and workspace flows, CLI operations, interoperability, migrations, errors, testing, and staged delivery; records unresolved choices explicitly; and stays local under .dev until approved for publication.
notes:
Context mapped. User decisions: (1) model packages, executable extensions, and installable tools remain distinct artifact domains, with semantic reuse only; (2) published model packages are IR-first, with canonical versioned Morphir IR and optional source/provenance. Root CONTEXT.md now distinguishes Morphir package from immutable package release. Identity research: the earlier PURL-vs-PackagePath question was premature. JSR/Deno separates scoped package release from exported entrypoint; Gleam separates package dependency from imported module and supports registry/path/pinned-Git sources; Go uses authority-bearing module paths, package subpaths, one version per module path, /vN identity for incompatible majors, and replace for source redirection; Cargo fully qualifies packages by source+name+version and lets code use aliases/crate/module names, allowing multiple versions and sources. PURL standardizes cross-ecosystem package coordinates and physical subpaths but does not define name ownership, dependency solving, public exports, source substitution, or version coexistence. PackagePath+SemVer is sufficient for a release only after package-path ownership is defined; the system still needs PackageRequirement, ModuleReference, SourceDescriptor, digest/provenance, and coexistence rules. Teaching reference written locally at .dev/.sdlc/morphir-package-identity/. Next decision: global, authority-bearing, or repository-qualified package-name ownership.
Distribution history added from finos/morphir discussions. #55 says Distribution was introduced above Package to carry the package name, was expected to encompass multiple versioned packages, and deliberately deferred version semantics to package management. #146 frames publishing/versioning/reuse of Morphir IR as package-manager user stories. #160 distinguishes unresolved Library references from loading/linking the transitive implementation closure and raises version-conflict handling. #211 proposes Bundle as a fat IR; its discussion reframes that as Library versus bottom-of-graph Application and explicitly raises multiple-version support. #218 supersedes Bundle with standalone Application plus entry points, full dependency definitions, SDK inclusion/tree shaking, and equivalence/compatibility. #203/#214/#289 distinguish the semantic distribution from its single-file or granular document-tree serialization and treat a distribution as a virtual tree with one or many files. Proposed reconciliation: package release is repository identity/lifecycle; Distribution is typed IR content (Library/Specs/Application); encoding/layout is storage representation; package bundle/archive is the transport envelope. A reusable release requires a normative Library distribution; Specs is a projection; Application is a linked build/deployment artifact. Manifest requirements and lock entries remain distinct from dependency specs/definitions embedded in IR, with consistency validation between them.
Approved distribution boundary after reviewing finos/morphir discussions #55, #88, #146, #160, #203, #211, #214, #218, and #289. A reusable Morphir package release has one normative Library distribution; Specs is a projection sharing the release identity; Application is a versioned linked standalone IR artifact that may be stored/distributed but is not a dependency. Distribution is semantic IR independent of single-file/document-tree encoding. Package bundle is the physical transport envelope. Manifest requirements, lock entries, and embedded distribution dependency snapshots are distinct but must agree. CONTEXT.md updated with these terms.
Approved package identity: canonical PackageReleaseId = authority-bearing PackagePath + exact SemVer. The authority prefix establishes namespace ownership; registry, mirror, workspace, Git, and vendored locations remain SourceDescriptors and do not alter identity. Local dependency/import aliases are non-canonical. PURL may be an external representation after Morphir type registration, not the domain identity model itself. CONTEXT.md updated with Package path and Package release ID.
Version-coexistence research: MoonBit main at 94521dbd (2026-09-04) avoids Go /vN paths. Its MVS groups one module name into compatibility sets: all versions below 2.0 form one set, and each major >=2 is a separate set. It selects one version per set and retains multiple incompatible versions of the same module simultaneously. The resolved graph identifies nodes by ModuleSource (name+version+source), gives each a ModuleId, and binds each dependent edge to an exact node. PackageFQN internally contains ModuleSource/version although display/import syntax omits it; imports support local aliases. This is strong precedent for contextual, edge-scoped resolution. For Morphir, source should remain outside canonical identity per the approved model, so graph nodes would use PackageReleaseId (PackagePath+SemVer), with SourceDescriptor/digest in the lock. Supporting this requires Application distributions and downstream traversal to key definitions/references by release instance or graph context; current PackagePath-keyed dependency maps are insufficient. MoonBit currently has no dependency graph lockfile; .moon-lock is an operation mutex, so Morphir should not copy that omission.
Approved coexistence model: no Go-style major version suffixes. Keep PackagePath stable across majors; unify compatible requirements where possible; allow incompatible PackageReleaseIds for the same path to coexist as exact nodes in the resolved graph; require distinct dependency slots/aliases when one package directly uses multiple versions. Published Library IR resolves references through its owning release dependency slots; the lock binds slots to exact ReleaseIds; Application distributions carry the exact graph and implementations. This requires evolving current PackagePath-keyed distribution dependency structures. CONTEXT.md updated with Dependency slot and Resolved dependency edge.
Approved requirement and selection semantics: PackageRequirement uses an explicit SemVer constraint; prereleases require explicit admission. Normal builds consume the exact complete PackageLock. Initial resolution and intentional update prefer the highest stable version satisfying applicable constraints, unifying overlapping requirements where possible and retaining separate release nodes for disjoint constraints. CONTEXT.md updated with revised Package requirement and Package lock.
Approved module exposure model: convention-generated export paths by default, derived canonically from public Morphir ModulePaths rather than physical filesystem layout. Packages may exclude convention exports and add aliases, or select explicit mode for a curated surface. Publication validates and expands configuration into a complete immutable PackageExportTable carried by the release and Library/Specs metadata; consumers never regenerate it. Direct filesystem/module conventions are not repository identity. CONTEXT.md updated with Package export path/table.
Approved physical packaging model: define one canonical logical PackageBundle containing manifest, exact build lock, normative Library distribution, optional Specs/source/provenance/SBOM/attestations, and integrity metadata. Permit directory, deterministic archive, OCI, and repository-specific transport encodings. PackageContentDigest hashes a canonical sorted content manifest/file digests and stays stable across repacking; TransportDigest verifies a particular archive/blob. No transport technology becomes package semantics. CONTEXT.md updated.
Approved repository architecture: RegistryIndex metadata is separate from package content and supports list-versions/read-release/source-descriptor capabilities. Resolver works through that capability rather than storage-specific APIs. Initial reference backends are local directory plus static Git/HTTPS per-package histories; OCI and hosted APIs are adapters over the same model. Content acquisition verifies package and transport digests. PackageCatalog search is separate and non-authoritative. CONTEXT.md updated with Registry index, Package registry, and Package catalog.
Approved authority/trust discovery: authority-bearing prefix may expose a well-known HTTPS metadata document; signed versioned delegations bind namespace prefixes to registry indexes and publication keys. Explicit configuration can pin authority metadata and redirect to approved mirrors. Mirrors may serve identical metadata/content but cannot create valid releases. Locks retain delegation digest, index snapshot, content digest, and exact source for offline reproduction. CONTEXT.md updated with Package authority, Authority delegation, and Package mirror.
Approved release lifecycle: PackagePath+version is permanently bound to one PackageContentDigest; republishing different content is rejected. Mutable signed status is separate: yank excludes from new range resolution while locks/exact requirements may remain eligible; revocation can warn or block even locked use under policy; tombstone durably records exceptional unavailability and prevents identity reuse. Mutable channels point to immutable releases. CONTEXT.md updated with lifecycle terms.
Approved development overrides: path/workspace/modified-vendor/pinned-Git inputs compile into explicit immutable IR-first UnpublishedPackageSnapshots with declared PackagePath, source/tree revision, compiler provenance, and content digest. They do not claim a published PackageReleaseId. Overrides are root-only policy and never propagate. Branch selectors resolve to commits in locks. Byte-identical vendored published bundles remain published releases with alternate SourceDescriptors. Applications may link snapshots with provenance; publishing a reusable Library release requires all dependency edges to resolve to published releases. CONTEXT.md updated.
Approved document boundary: existing morphir.toml/morphir.yaml configuration remains the sole human-authored package intent and may include non-publishable workspace/task/toolchain/source/credential settings; morphir.lock is resolver-generated complete exact graph; publication emits a normalized immutable machine-facing PackageReleaseManifest containing only portable identity, requirements, expanded exports, content references, compatibility, and integrity metadata. Package consumers never evaluate authoring configuration. CONTEXT.md updated.
Approved publication-time SemVer enforcement for stable releases. Patch/minor publication must pass structural backward-compatibility analysis over normalized export tables and Specs distributions; major releases may break. Implementation-only changes may be patch releases. Publisher emits a machine-readable PackageCompatibilityReport stored by the registry with comparison provenance. Behavioral equivalence is not generally provable and remains attested/additional analysis. Indeterminate structural results fail by default or require an authority-approved exception. CONTEXT.md updated.
Approved name and release refinement: use ContractRelease rather than InterfaceRelease. LibraryRelease has normative Library distribution plus derived Specs; ContractRelease has normative Specs and no Morphir implementation claim. Runtime/extension providers bind to exact Contract PackageReleaseId and Specs digest. This is operationally analogous to .NET contract/reference assemblies and semantically analogous to ML module signatures, while avoiding overloaded signature/reference/interface terminology. CONTEXT.md updated.
Approved application/binding boundary: ApplicationDistribution is portable and contains the exact model graph, Library implementations, ContractRelease requirements, and entry points. Target-specific ApplicationBinding separately maps every required ContractReleaseId+SpecsDigest to a compatible executable provider/artifact digest. Execution requires a complete binding; analysis/codegen may consume the portable Application. Changing platform bindings does not change model identity, and provider artifacts remain outside the model package graph. CONTEXT.md updated.
Approved trust policy: public/private registry publication requires a PackageReleaseStatement signed by a key authorized through the PackageAuthority delegation chain, covering exact ReleaseId, normalized manifest, and PackageContentDigest. RegistryStatusStatements separately sign snapshots and yank/revoke/tombstone state. Optional build/SBOM provenance attestations are evidence, not publication authority. Transport TLS/digests do not substitute for release signatures; mirrors need no publishing keys. Unsigned snapshots are permitted only by explicit local-development policy and are marked in locks. Reuse standard TUF-style delegation and DSSE/in-toto-style statement machinery where semantics fit, with domain-specific manifests. CONTEXT.md updated.
Approved CLI boundary: model packages use morphir package lifecycle commands distinct from morphir extension and morphir tool. Shared internals are limited to acquisition/cache/verification/trust semantics. Package workflow covers add/remove, explicit resolve/update, sync, tree/why, build snapshot, check, pack, verify, publish, vendor, inspect, yank, revoke. Ordinary builds validate and consume an existing lock, fetch missing content, and never silently re-resolve; missing/invalid locks require explicit resolution. Higher-level build orchestration delegates to this lifecycle.
Approved migration model: package-layer format evolves independently from Morphir IR format. New bundles may carry supported legacy Library IR with explicit payload format metadata. Legacy versionless distributions become UnpublishedPackageSnapshots; non-authority names remain migration metadata until explicitly mapped; localDependencies become workspace overrides; generated slots/exports adapt what is representable. No authority/version is invented and legacy IR is not silently rewritten. Graph-aware features such as multiversion Application linking, Contract releases, and binding metadata declare capabilities and produce clear errors in unsupported consumers. A package migrate workflow emits config plus a migration/capability report. CONTEXT.md updated with Legacy package adapter.
Approved PURL role: native PackageReleaseId remains normative domain identity. A future registered morphir PURL type is the reversible standardized external representation of an exact release for SBOM/provenance/catalog/vulnerability/generic repository interop. PURL does not represent ranges, dependency slots, exports, graph edges, sources, or unpublished snapshots; subpath is physical content and must not encode logical exports. Package manager v1 does not block on registration; define/test proposed mapping now, register upstream after a working format/registry, emit as standardized metadata only after registration. CONTEXT.md updated.
Approved diagnostics contract: define a stable versioned PackageDiagnostic ADT/schema with code, severity, operation, subject, dependency path, structured details, causal diagnostics, and guidance. Share codes/payloads across CLI JSON, WIT, daemon APIs, and language libraries while allowing local human renderers. Cover identity/authority, solving, lock state, legacy capability, exports/slots, contract bindings, acquisition/offline, digests/signatures, immutable collision, compatibility, and archive safety. Integrity/authority errors fail closed; authorized mirrors may be retried for availability but never trigger silent trust fallback or re-resolution. CONTEXT.md updated.
Approved normative PackageConformanceCorpus alongside schemas/specification. Language-neutral cases define inputs, normalized values, serialized outputs, digests, diagnostics, and capability requirements for identity/SemVer/PURL, exports, manifests/content hashes, solver/locks, contracts/bindings, compatibility, trust/signing, mirrors/offline/corruption, archive attacks/case collisions, and legacy adaptation. All implementations run the same corpus; no implementation is normative. Property/fuzz/performance tests remain supplemental. CONTEXT.md updated.
Approved staged delivery: Stage 0 specification foundation; Stage 1 local Library steel thread; Stage 2 signed distributed registry; Stage 3 graph-aware packages, contracts, applications, and bindings; Stage 4 ecosystem adoption and interoperability. Consolidated design published for ecosystem review as finos/morphir#800, labeled enhancement/spec/draft. The issue preserves all 16 open Stage 0 decisions.

title: kb containment is lexical: Windows separators and symlinks still escape
description: Follow-up review on #107 (merged). The containment guards added there split on '/' only and are purely lexical, so two escapes remain. (1) On Windows, roots/groups such as '..\\victim' or 'C:\\victim' contain no '/' and pass validation; PathBuf::push then interprets backslashes and drive prefixes, so pull --prune can still delete outside the bundle and new-bundle can still scaffold outside kb/bundles. We ship x86_64-pc-windows-msvc and aarch64-pc-windows-msvc, so this is reachable. (2) A symlinked component (sources -> ../../../victim, or kb/bundles/shared symlinked out) passes the lexical check on every platform while reads, writes and deletes follow the link. Fix by inspecting Path::components and rejecting ParentDir/CurDir/RootDir/Prefix, and by verifying the resolved destination stays beneath the bundle.

title: Make YAML the primary migrate output format
description: Specify and implement YAML as a native persisted serialization of the concrete Morphir IR, with v4 as the primary target and v3 compatibility where the concrete model permits it. YAML is an equal IR storage format, not a frontend language, generated projection, or documentation view. The migrate command should default v3-to-v4 output to YAML, infer single-file encoding from the destination extension, support document-tree output, and convert stored IR bidirectionally between JSON and YAML. Update v4 so JSON Schema is clearly a bootstrap definition mechanism rather than a restriction of IR storage to JSON.
acceptance_criteria:
EARS acceptance requirements:
AC-01 ubiquitous: The IR codec system shall provide an explicit YAML representation for every valid concrete v3 and v4 IR node.
AC-02 event-driven: When the YAML decoder reads an explicit or preferred readable form, it shall normalize that form into exactly one versioned semantic IR value.
AC-03 event-driven: When the YAML encoder writes an IR value, it shall emit the specified deterministic readable form where one exists and the explicit structural form otherwise.
AC-04 event-driven: When JSON is converted to YAML to JSON without a version transform, the result shall be semantically equal to the original IR.
AC-05 event-driven: When YAML is converted to JSON to YAML without a version transform, the result shall be semantically equal to the original IR.
AC-06 ubiquitous: The codec system shall retain JSON input and output support for every previously supported IR version.
AC-07 unwanted: If YAML contains ambiguous shorthand, duplicate keys, unsupported tags, unsafe aliases, lossy numbers, or invalid coercions, then the decoder shall reject it with a located diagnostic.
AC-08 event-driven: When v3 is migrated to v4 without a selected format or recognized output extension, the command shall emit canonical YAML.
AC-09 event-driven: When resolving single-file output, the command shall apply explicit output format, recognized extension, then YAML default.
AC-10 unwanted: If output format conflicts with a recognized extension, then the command shall diagnose the conflict and shall not publish.
AC-11 event-driven: When resolving single-file input, the command shall apply explicit input format, recognized extension, then bounded JSON-first detection.
AC-12 event-driven: When --json is used without an output path, the command shall write migrated JSON IR to stdout.
AC-13 event-driven: When --json is used with an output path, the command shall write the artifact and emit JSON status and diagnostics to stdout.
AC-14 event-driven: When writing a YAML document tree, the command shall use manifest.yaml, module.yaml, *.type.yaml, and *.value.yaml.
AC-15 ubiquitous: A generated document tree shall use one serialization profile.
AC-16 unwanted: If discovery finds multiple supported manifests, then the reader shall diagnose ambiguity and shall not choose implicitly.
AC-17 event-driven: When a single file is converted to a document tree and back without version change, the result shall be semantically equal.
AC-18 event-driven: When a JSON document tree is converted to YAML and back, the result shall be semantically equal.
AC-19 ubiquitous: Each transform shall declare event, definition, module, or distribution retention.
AC-20 state-driven: While all transforms are event-local, definition-local, or module-local, the pipeline shall retain no more than the largest declared scope plus bounded codec buffers.
AC-21 unwanted: If a transform needs a whole distribution, then the pipeline shall report that requirement before processing.
AC-22 event-driven: When LCR v3 is migrated to v4 YAML as a file or tree, the pipeline shall use its streaming path without retaining the complete distribution.
AC-23 ubiquitous: The pipeline shall carry semantic IR events rather than JSON or YAML value trees.
AC-24 ubiquitous: Public codec options shall keep IR version, layout, format, vocabulary, normalization, and publication independent.
AC-25 event-driven: When a new codec is registered, existing migration transforms and codec callers shall compile unchanged.
AC-26 optional: Where YAML style selection is later exposed, the system shall use existing codec options without changing the semantic model.
AC-27 unwanted: If any pipeline or publication stage fails, then existing output shall remain unchanged.
AC-28 optional: Where --allow-partial is enabled, migration shall recover only through target-version incompleteness constructs.
AC-29 unwanted: If serialization would drop, coerce, or ambiguously reinterpret IR, then --allow-partial shall not permit publication.
AC-30 ubiquitous: Each diagnostic shall include stable code, stage, severity, cursor, guidance, and source location when available.
AC-31 ubiquitous: The v4 specification shall separate the semantic model, JSON profile, YAML profile, and document-tree layout.
AC-32 ubiquitous: The v4 specification shall define logical document identities without physical serialization extensions.
AC-33 event-driven: When a normative YAML example round-trips through normalized IR and JSON, the result shall be semantically equal.
notes:
Design approved and written locally at .dev/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-28-native-yaml-ir-storage-design.md. Native YAML and JSON normalize to versioned semantic IR. Semantic equivalence defines losslessness. Canonical YAML uses deterministic readable shorthand with explicit structural fallback. Current CLI phase adds --input-format and --output-format for JSON/YAML; YAML style selection remains a compatible follow-up. Output resolution is explicit flag, known extension, then YAML default. Input uses explicit flag, known extension, then bounded JSON-first detection. Preserve the legacy context-dependent --json behavior. Homogeneous document trees default to YAML and use manifest.yaml, module.yaml, *.type.yaml, and *.value.yaml. Approved pipeline uses semantic cursor events, composable transforms, declared event/definition/module/distribution buffering, format encoders, layout sinks, and atomic publication. Open codec identifiers leave room for TOML, Markdown, Jupyter, and other adapters without implementing them now. Approved strict diagnostics keep --allow-partial from weakening serialization correctness. Approved v4 spec split: serialization-neutral semantic model, JSON profile, YAML profile, and document-tree profile. JSON Schema remains a bootstrap definition for JSON, not a persistence restriction. Logical identities omit physical extensions; resolve format versus manifest in favor of manifest. V3 semantics remain stable with complete explicit YAML coverage; v4 schema changes are allowed with documented migration behavior. Verification uses TDD, local quality gates, real morphir-elm and morphir-scala fixtures, semantic round-trips, single-file and document-tree acceptance paths, and instrumented bounded-scope LCR streaming. Implementation will use small commits pushed at completed sectional boundaries.

title: Design validated typestate MEP sessions
description: Separate untrusted MEP wire DTOs from validated application state, then assess a generic typestate session controller shared by Extism, spawned-process, and connected-daemon transports. The current session enum prevents some field combinations but still admits identity and capability drift, duplicate capability kinds, stringly typed operation calls, invalid JSON-RPC response envelopes, and uncertain lifecycle outcomes after cancellation or transport failure.
design: Recommended direction from the dedicated review: define an object-safe MepTransport that only exchanges wire requests and responses; put validation and lifecycle rules in Session<T, Loaded|Ready|Indeterminate|Stopped>; expose typed compile, generate, validate, and transform operations on Ready; use a ManagedSession enum only where registries or actors need runtime state erasure. Keep wire::InitializeResult deserializable even when peers disagree, then validate it into NegotiatedSession. Do not silently merge discovery and initialization claims.
acceptance_criteria: Document wire DTO versus validated domain boundaries; decide identity and capability drift policy; cover response JSON-RPC version, request ID correlation, and exactly-one-of-result-or-error validation; represent uncertain lifecycle outcomes explicitly; provide compile-fail tests for invalid state transitions; define migration from the object-safe ExtensionSession API without duplicating state machines across transports.
notes:
Rebased PR #93 onto connected-daemon main commit 6351b3e. New head 294991c integrates ConnectedDaemonTransport with MepTransport and migrates real HTTP conformance, 64 MiB payload, refusal, and timeout tests to Session typestates. Refusal and request timeout now retain Indeterminate because HTTP cannot prove remote state; acknowledged shutdown proves Stopped. Local connected/process/Extism/unit/doc/clippy checks pass. Replacement CI pending.
PR #93 head eee6cf2 boxes the state-bearing Session values in FailedSession, with a concrete ConnectedDaemonTransport size regression capped at 128 bytes. Replacement morphir-rust CI run 33122001751 passed every job, including integration, native process, connected daemon, WASM/Extism, lint, docs, coverage, and EasyCLA. Umbrella PR #707 commit 89481932 pins this head; its replacement run 33122067259 passed the previously failing morphir CLI consumer job plus all aggregate checks. PR #93 is CLEAN and MERGEABLE, all five review threads are resolved, and a final Codex review of eee6cf2 is pending. Final Codex review of head eee6cf2 posted two P2 findings: Session::loaded can wrap a SpawnedProcessSession already advanced through the compatibility API and reset lifecycle/request IDs; failure abort can still wait the full request timeout while collecting a stderr pipe inherited by a descendant. Both were assigned to the dedicated typestate worktree for TDD fixes. PR #93 remains open and must rerun morphir-rust and umbrella consumer verification after its head changes.
PR #93 head fcb9364 addresses the two final-review P2s. description: Turn the morphir-scala Package URL and MoonBit registry research and the approved ecosystem package design in finos/morphir#800 into a working Morphir IR-first model-package vertical slice. Establish the MCK package-suite specification foundation, then implement a pinned Git-file index and local-directory backend, exact resolution and locks, verified materialization, workspace overlays, and an Elm acceptance fixture with transitive unpublished dependencies.
design: Follow the IR-first model-package design in finos/morphir#800 and kb/bundles/morphir/morphir-package-system/package-system-design.md. MCK is the shared compatibility brand with domain-specific suites and versioned protocol/report integration. title: [UPDATED] Implement DirectRuntime for direct execution mode
description:
Implement DirectRuntime in morphir-ext for direct execution without actors or IPC, supporting CLI, Morphir-Live, and browser/WASM environments.

## PREREQUISITE: Gherkin Acceptance Tests Required

**BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION**: Prepare comprehensive Gherkin acceptance tests and present to user for approval/iteration. Implementation may NOT proceed without user verification of tests.

Gherkin tests must cover:
- DirectRuntime construction with ExtismRuntime
- execute() method with various function names and envelopes
- TEA lifecycle: init(), update(), subscriptions()
- Design-time operations: backend_generate(), frontend_compile()
- Error handling (WASM errors, envelope errors, missing functions)
- No dependency on Kameo or daemon infrastructure
- Works in WASM context (no_std compatible if needed)

## Background
DirectRuntime provides in-process extension execution without daemon/actor overhead. All clients (CLI, Morphir-Live, browser/WASM) can use DirectRuntime for embedded execution.

## Architecture

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     Client Layer                           │
│  (CLI, Morphir-Live, Browser/WASM, IDE)                   │
└──────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                       │
                       │ Choice: Direct or Daemon
                       │
            ┌──────────┴──────────┐
            │                     │
            ▼                     ▼
  ┌──────────────────┐   ┌─────────────────┐
  │  DirectRuntime   │   │  DaemonClient   │
  │  (morphir-ext)   │   │  (morphir-ext)  │
  └────────┬─────────┘   └────────┬────────┘
           │                      │
           │ No IPC               │ IPC (JSON-RPC)
           │                      │
           ▼                      ▼
  ┌──────────────────┐   ┌─────────────────┐
  │ ExtismRuntime    │   │  Daemon Service │
  │ (morphir-ext)    │   │  with actors    │
  └────────┬─────────┘   └─────────────────┘
           │
           │ Loads WASM
           ▼
  ┌──────────────────┐
  │  Extension       │
  │  (WASM module)   │
  └──────────────────┘

DirectRuntime Flow:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Client
  │
  └─> DirectRuntime::new(ExtismRuntime)
        │
        └─> execute("backend_generate", envelope)
              │
              └─> ExtismRuntime::call_envelope()
                    │
                    └─> Extism loads WASM
                          │
                          └─> Calls backend_generate()
                                │
                                └─> Returns envelope
```

- **Depends on**: `morphir-ext/src/runtime.rs` (ExtensionRuntime trait)

title: Morphir x WebAssembly Component Model Interactive Guide
description:
Build an interactive, self-guided tutorial that explains the WebAssembly Component Model ABI (canonical ABI, lifting/lowering) while being extremely aware of Morphir IR.

## Goals
1. Map Morphir IR programs and types to WebAssembly (core Wasm level)
2. Evaluate whether Morphir IR could serve as a practical replacement for WIT
3. Identify gaps preventing this substitution (semantic/ABI/tooling mismatches)
4. Determine how Morphir could be enhanced to support this use case

## Modules (Progressive)
- Core Wasm boundary constraints (i32/i64/f32/f64, linear memory)
- Canonical ABI: lifting and lowering
- Scalars (bool/int/float)
- Strings and byte sequences (ptr/len, encoding)
- Lists, records/structs, tuples
- Variants/enums, option/result
- Functions, multi-arg/multi-return, flattening rules
- Resources/handles (ownership, borrowing patterns)
- Error handling and traps vs typed errors
- Versioning and evolution patterns
- Performance considerations (copies, allocations, alignment)

## Deliverables per Module
- Conceptual explanation with ASCII diagrams
- Code snippets in F#, Scala, Go
- Morphir IR examples (types + functions)
- Core Wasm function signature and memory layout
- WIT replacement check (what Morphir has, what's missing, candidate enhancements)
- Confidence check questions

## Key Questions
- Can Morphir IR act as an IDL/interface definition layer analogous to WIT?
- Can we derive canonical ABI lowering/lifting rules from Morphir IR types?
- What semantics does WIT have that Morphir IR lacks?
- What additions would make Morphir IR more suitable?

title: Create reusable TUI framework for interactive morphir commands
description:
Build a shared TUI framework that provides consistent interactive experiences across morphir commands.

## Overview
Create a reusable TUI component in `cmd/morphir/internal/tui` that can be used by:
- `morphir` (main interactive mode)
- `morphir validate --tui`
- Future commands like `morphir explore`, `morphir inspect`, etc.

## Architecture
```
cmd/morphir/internal/tui/
├── app.go           # Main TUI application shell
├── layout.go        # Flexible layout manager (sidebar + main)
├── components/
│   ├── sidebar.go   # Collapsible sidebar with tree/list
│   ├── viewer.go    # Markdown/content viewer with paging
│   ├── statusbar.go # Bottom status/help bar
│   └── searchbar.go # Search/filter input
├── styles/
│   └── theme.go     # Consistent lipgloss styling
└── keymap/
    └── vim.go       # Vim-style keybindings
```

## Core Components

### AppShell
Main application container that manages:
- Layout (sidebar width, visibility)
- Focus management between panels
- Global keybindings (quit, help, toggle sidebar)
- Resize handling

### SidebarPanel
- Tree view for hierarchical content
- List view for flat content  
- Collapsible (toggle with `b` or `Ctrl+b`)
- Filterable

### ViewerPanel
- Glamour-rendered markdown
- Viewport with vim navigation (j/k, gg/G, Ctrl+d/u)
- Search within content (/)
- Line numbers (optional)

### StatusBar
- Current mode indicator
- Keybinding hints
- File/position info

## Usage Pattern
```go
// In validate command
app := tui.NewApp(
    tui.WithSidebar(fileList),
    tui.WithViewer(markdownContent),
    tui.WithTitle("Validation Report"),
)
return app.Run()

// In main morphir command
app := tui.NewApp(
    tui.WithSidebar(commandList),
    tui.WithViewer(welcomeContent),
    tui.WithTitle("Morphir"),
)
return app.Run()
```

## Keybindings (Vim-style)
| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| j/k | Scroll down/up |
| h/l | Switch panels |
| gg/G | Go to top/bottom |
| Ctrl+d/u | Page down/up |
| / | Search |
| n/N | Next/prev search result |
| b | Toggle sidebar |
| q | Quit |
| ? | Show help |

## Libraries
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` - TUI framework
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles` - Components
- `github.com/charmbracelet/glamour` - Markdown
- `github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss` - Styling

## Blocked By
None - this is a foundational component

## Blocks
- morphir-tol (TUI validate command)

title: Bound Ion capability claims by node and IR version
description: Protocol v2 currently treats profiles, nodes, and IR versions as a Cartesian product. Refine the exact 2.0.0-draft.1 capability response with explicit per-profile limits, have the runner skip unsupported combinations, and advertise Ion only with truthful limits. Keep numeric v1 JSON/YAML unchanged. Expand the limits as Ion operations gain coverage. This allows Task 5 primitive proofs without claiming unimplemented Ion operations.

title: MEP Contract as a Gleam Model Implementation Plan
description:
# MEP Contract as a Gleam Model Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Add `spec/mep/`, where `contract/src/mep.gleam` models today's MEP protocol types, `generated/mep.ir.json` is the committed Morphir IR of that model, and CI fails when the two drift.

**Architecture:** The contract is a small Gleam project that the umbrella CLI compiles with its built-in Gleam frontend (`--ir-version 4 --types-only`); no `gleam` binary is needed. A mise task refreshes the committed IR. A Rust test in `crates/morphir/tests/` compiles the contract into a temporary directory, checks that every protocol type is present, and compares the result with the committed file byte for byte; the existing `morphir CLI (test + integration)` job runs it once `spec/mep/**` is in its path filter.

**Tech Stack:** Gleam (source language only), Morphir CLI (`crates/morphir`), the Gleam frontend in `ecosystem/morphir-rust/crates/morphir-gleam-binding`, Rust integration tests, mise, GitHub Actions.

**Spec:** beads `morphir-opua.1` design (render with `mise run beads:plan -- spec morphir-opua.1 --render`), sections for checkpoints 8, 9, 11 and 12, and work item B7. Issue finos/morphir#964, bead `morphir-opua.1.2.1`.

## Scope

In this plan: the handshake, capabilities, claims, compile, diagnostics and generate types that `morphir-extension-sdk` defines today (`ecosystem/morphir-rust/crates/morphir-extension-sdk/src/protocol.rs`, `src/types.rs`, `src/claims/`), the method names and error codes, the README with the versioning rule and the wire mapping, the committed IR and its drift check.

Not in this plan (existing beads): Rust types generated from the IR (`morphir-opua.1.2.2`), JSON Schema fixes (`.1.2.3`), the WIT backend and `generated/wit/` (`.1.2.4`), Python backend gaps (`.1.2.5`), `BitArray` in the Gleam frontend (`.1.2.6`), the MEP conformance suite and `spec/mep/mck/` content (`.1.2.7`), the typed IR payload (`morphir-opua.1.3.1`). Also out: workspace discovery payloads (they live in `morphir_workspace`, not the SDK), validate and transform payloads, and the JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope itself (a standard, not MEP).

## Decisions this plan makes inside the spec

1. **Arbitrary JSON is a recursive `Json` type** in the model (`JsonNull`, `JsonBool`, `JsonInt`, `JsonFloat`, `JsonString`, `JsonArray`, `JsonObject`). The Gleam frontend has no `Dynamic`, and a placeholder would hide what the wire carries. The WIT backend (`.1.2.4`) will need a non-recursive mapping for it (checkpoint 9 notes WIT rejects recursion); that bead records the choice.
2. **Flattened extra members are an explicit `extra: Dict(String, Json)` field** on `ExtensionCapabilities` and `CompileOptions`, with a doc comment saying they sit beside the named members on the wire. Reserved and legacy key rejection stays a codec rule, documented, not modelled.
3. **Labels are snake_case in Gleam and lowerCamelCase on the wire by default.** Every exception is written in the doc comment of its type and in the README's wire mapping table: `ExtensionInfo` keeps snake_case (`min_sdk_version`), enum spellings (`cli`, `frontend`, `error`, `compiled`), `PeerKind`'s fallback to `Unspecified`, `multiDocument` written only when true, `exposedModules` absent versus empty. A later codec bead generates the mapping; this plan only states it.
4. **Constructor names are unique across the module** and never shadow the prelude: severities are `ErrorSeverity`, `WarningSeverity`, `InfoSeverity`, `HintSeverity`; extension types are `FrontendExtension`, `BackendExtension`, `TransformExtension`, `ValidatorExtension`, `WorkspaceExtension`.
5. **One source file**, `contract/src/mep.gleam`, grouped by section comments, as checkpoint 11 lays out. The IR package is `morphir/mep` (checkpoint 12).
6. **The drift check is a Rust test, not a new CI job.** The committed file is a copy of `.morphir/out/compile.dest/morphir-ir.json`; `morphir compile -o spec/mep/generated` is not used because install refuses to overwrite a file it has no ledger entry for on a fresh checkout.

## Global Constraints

- Records use labelled fields (checkpoint 9: positional fields become `arg-1`).
- Compile with `--ir-version 4 --types-only` and an explicit `--config spec/mep/contract/morphir.toml`.
- Do not add Gleam to `[tools]` or CI; the built-in frontend is self-contained.
- The README states the pre-1.0 rule verbatim in meaning: before 1.0.0, a breaking change bumps the minor version and an additive or backward-compatible change bumps the patch version; published contracts carry no prerelease tags. The handshake sends the canonical `MAJOR.MINOR` form (today `"0.1"`). The claims format version (`0.1.0-draft.2`) is separate.
- Commits: Conventional Commits, no AI attribution, no `Co-Authored-By`, plain English, no em dashes.
- Track progress in beads with `mise run beads:plan -- ledger <plan-epic> "<line>"`.

## Review Focus

1. **A type or field the SDK sends that the model lacks.** Pinned by the task 1 to 3 coverage tests, which list every expected type and, for the records most likely to drift, every field label.
2. **A committed IR that does not match a fresh compile on another machine.** Pinned by task 4's byte comparison running in CI on Linux, with config discovery isolated from the user's environment.
3. **A wire spelling that the model silently changes.** Pinned by the README table in task 4 and a test that every type with a non-default wire rule names it in its doc comment.
4. **A constructor that shadows the prelude or collides with another.** Pinned by the compile itself in each task (the frontend rejects duplicates) and by Decision 4.
5. **CI not running the check when only `spec/mep/**` changes.** Pinned by task 4's filter change and a `tests/ci` check if the repo tests its filters.

---

## File map

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `spec/mep/README.md` | What MEP is, versioning rule, wire mapping, scope, how to regenerate |
| `spec/mep/contract/morphir.toml` | Morphir project: name `morphir/mep`, `source_directory = "src"`, `[frontend] language = "gleam"` |
| `spec/mep/contract/gleam.toml` | Gleam project for editors and optional real type-checking |
| `spec/mep/contract/.gitignore` | `/build/`, `/.morphir/` |
| `spec/mep/contract/src/mep.gleam` | The contract |
| `spec/mep/generated/mep.ir.json` | Committed IR |
| `crates/morphir/tests/mep_contract.rs` | Coverage and drift tests |
| `.config/mise/config.toml` | `spec:mep` and `spec:mep-check` tasks; `check` aggregate |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | `spec/mep/**` in the path filter that selects the CLI test job |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | `[Unreleased]` entry |

## Branch and pull request

One umbrella branch, `feat/mep-spec-contract`, from `origin/main`. One PR to `main` after the whole-branch review. Refers to #964 and #960.

---

title: Morphir Host Phase A, Part 4 Implementation Plan
description:
# Morphir Host Phase A, Part 4 Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Finish Phase A. `morphir-daemon` becomes a client of `morphir-host` with no MEP handshake, codec, registry or session actor of its own, and the three items deferred from part 3 land in `morphir-host`.

**Architecture:** The last duplicates in `morphir-daemon` are deleted after their behaviour tests move to `morphir-host-native`, where the real implementations already live. HTTP stays a way to reach an extension, as an `HttpChannel` behind a feature of `morphir-host-native`. `CallError` separates connect, handshake and decode failures. `Pool` gains a clock-free idle eviction. The umbrella CLI then drops the workarounds it carries for those gaps.

**Tech Stack:** Rust 2024, tokio, async-trait, async-lock, jsonrpsee 0.26 (HTTP client and test server only), Extism, cargo, mise.

**Spec:** `.dev/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-23-morphir-host-library-design.md` (with `.dev/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-23-cross-language-extension-sdk.md`). Part 3 ledger: `.dev/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-24-morphir-host-phase-a-part-3.ledger.md`.

**Tracking:** beads, not GitHub discussions. Epic `morphir-opua.1.1` (Phase A, finos/morphir#959). This plan closes `morphir-opua.1.1.2` (finos/morphir-rust#237) and `morphir-opua.1.1.6` (finos/morphir-rust#240). Each task below has its own bead under those two; the GitHub issues stay open as mirrors until the work merges.

## Scope of this plan

In part 4:

- `CallError` gets `Connect`, `Handshake` and `Invalid` in place of `Open`. `Pool` does not retry a decode failure.
- `Pool::tick` and `Pool::evict_idle` give idle eviction without a clock, so `morphir-host` stays wasm32-clean.
- `HttpChannel` in `morphir-host-native` (feature `http`) replaces `ConnectedDaemonSession`.
- The daemon's real-extension tests move to `morphir-host-native`, on `activate` and `Session`.
- `morphir-daemon` keeps only `DaemonError`, `ExtensionLoader`, `VirtualPathConfig`, `FileSandbox` and `workspace`. Everything else in `extensions/` is deleted, with the `kameo`, `jsonrpsee` and `extism` dependencies.
- The #237 close-out: one test that a process guest and a native guest answer the same `Session::compile`.
- Umbrella: pin move, the new `CallError` arms, the start-failure side channel removed, the idle sweep on `Pool::evict_idle`.

Out of scope, recorded as beads elsewhere:

- `HostServices` (guest calls back to the host). No JSON-RPC guest calls the host today, and part 1 moved it next to the component imports. It becomes a Phase D bead under `morphir-opua.1.4`, linked from #237.
- A `NativeConnection` that skips JSON. `InvocationMode::NativeDirect` already gives the CLI typed calls with no JSON; `NativeChannel` covers the protocol path.
- Legacy top-level `documents` normalization. Since 0.4.0-beta.6 the SDK requires `sources` and ignores a top-level `documents`, pinned by `crates/morphir-extension-sdk/tests/compile_request.rs` (`top_level_documents_without_sources_reports_missing_sources`, `sources_ignores_unknown_top_level_documents`). #237's item is superseded by that decision.

## Decisions this plan makes inside the spec

1. **#240 "daemon tests pass unchanged" is met by moving the tests, not by keeping the API.** The daemon tests drive `activate_transport`, `InvokeOutcome` and `Session<T, Loaded>`, which are the duplicates #240 removes. Every behaviour they pin is kept by a ported test with the same name in `morphir-host-native`. No compatibility shims.
2. **`CallError` variants** (pre-1.0, so a breaking change is a minor bump of the crate):

   ```rust
   #[non_exhaustive]
   pub enum CallError {
       Rejected(HostError),  // the guest or host refused; session still ready
       Failed(HostError),    // the session broke; the connection closed its channel
       Invalid(HostError),   // the guest answered, the result did not decode or failed the host checks; session closed in order
       Connect(HostError),   // Pool only: `open` failed, no guest was started or reached
       Handshake(HostError), // Pool only: the guest started but the MEP handshake failed
   }
   ```

   `Invalid` is not retried by `Pool`: the same guest build gives the same bad answer. `CheckedConnection` reports a failed result check as `Invalid` too (part 4 ruling R1).
3. **Idle eviction counts ticks, not time.** `std::time::Instant` panics on `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, and `morphir-host` takes no clock dependency. The caller calls `Pool::tick` on its own timer and `Pool::evict_idle(n)` evicts every slot unused for at least `n` ticks. A slot is in use while its lock is held, so eviction skips it with `try_lock`, and an evicted session is always closed in order.
4. **`HttpChannel` is native and feature-gated.** jsonrpsee is not wasm-portable. Feature `http` of `morphir-host-native`, off by default, so the CLI build does not pull the HTTP client.

## Global Constraints

- `morphir-host` must pass `cargo check -p morphir-host --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` and must not depend on tokio (except dev), `morphir-daemon`, `morphir-host-native`, `morphir-distribution`, or any language binding.
- `morphir-host-native` must not depend on `morphir-daemon`.
- Every trait a browser client implements keeps `MaybeSend` plus the paired `cfg_attr(async_trait)` attributes.
- Wire sequences unchanged. Existing CLI error texts unchanged except where a task names the change and the CHANGELOG records it.
- Commits: Conventional Commits. No AI attribution, no `Co-Authored-By`. Plain English docs, no em dashes.
- Local process tests flake in parallel on this machine; judge real-process failures with `--test-threads=1`.

## Review Focus

1. **A retry that repeats a bad answer, or no retry for a lost guest.** Pinned by the task 1 pool tests: `Invalid` is returned once with one open; `Failed` still reopens once.
2. **An idle sweep that closes a guest in use, or never closes one.** Pinned by task 2 tests: a slot whose lock is held is skipped; a slot unused for `n` ticks is closed in order; a call after eviction opens a fresh guest.
3. **A lost behaviour when the daemon tests move.** Pinned by task 4: every `#[test]`/`#[tokio::test]` name in the moved files exists in the new files (a name-diff check in the step), and the mise tasks run the new locations.
4. **HTTP failures reported as the wrong state.** Pinned by task 3: a refused connection and a timeout are `Indeterminate` with cause `Transport`; a JSON-RPC error reply is an error response, not a channel failure.
5. **A CLI text change nobody recorded.** Pinned by task 7: the playground start and handshake texts keep their current exact wording without the side channel.

---

## File map

finos/morphir-rust (`ecosystem/morphir-rust/`):

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/morphir-host/src/connection.rs` | `CallError` variants |
| `crates/morphir-host/src/session.rs` | `Session::call` returns `Invalid` |
| `crates/morphir-host/src/pool.rs` | Connect/handshake split, no retry on decode, `tick`, `evict_idle` |
| `crates/morphir-host/tests/{session,pool}.rs` | Tests for the above |
| `crates/morphir-host-native/src/http.rs` | `HttpChannel` (feature `http`) |
| `crates/morphir-host-native/examples/mep-http-backend.rs` | Moved test server |
| `crates/morphir-host-native/tests/*_extension.rs`, `tests/process_describe.rs`, `tests/fixtures/` | Moved real-extension tests and fixtures |
| `crates/morphir-daemon/src/**` | Duplicates deleted |
| `crates/morphir-elm-binding/tests/{frontend,acceptance,wasm}.rs` | Fixture paths |
| `.mise/tasks/{test/daemon,test/process,test/extism,extension/artifact/*}`, `.github/ci-impact.toml` | New test locations |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | Removed/Changed entries |

finos/morphir (umbrella):

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/morphir/src/extensions/guest.rs`, `commands/ui/provider/extension.rs` | New `CallError` arms |
| `crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/provider/pool.rs` | Side channel removed; sweep on `Pool::evict_idle` |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | Pin move and any text change |

## Branches and pull requests

1. Tasks 1 to 6: one finos/morphir-rust branch from `origin/main` (`feat/morphir-host-phase-a-close`). One PR after a whole-branch review. Refers to finos/morphir-rust#237 and #240.
2. Task 7: one umbrella branch after that PR merges, based on `milestone/v0.4.0-beta.9` and updated with `origin/main`; the PR targets `milestone/v0.4.0-beta.9`. Pin the submodule to the merge commit. (finos/morphir-rust has no milestone branch, so the tasks 1-6 PR targets its `main`.)

description:
### Task 6: Workbench through `Pool`

**Files:**
- Create: `crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/provider/pool.rs` (`PooledInvoker`)
- Delete: `crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/provider/sessions.rs`
- Modify: `crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/provider/playground.rs`, `ui/provider/mod.rs`, `crates/morphir/src/extensions.rs` (delete `open_frontend_session`, `open_backend_session`, `open_loaded`, `installed_loaded`, `session_failure`, `failed_session_message`)

title: morphir-host Phase A, part 3: Registry, Pool, and the CLI off the daemon session Implementation Plan
description:
# morphir-host Phase A, part 3: Registry, Pool, and the CLI off the daemon session Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Resolve providers with a portable `morphir_host::Registry`, reuse workbench guests with a portable `morphir_host::Pool`, keep the daemon's error texts across channels, and move every remaining CLI extension path off `morphir-daemon`'s registry, typestate session, and actor.

**Architecture:** `morphir-host` gains `Registry`, the `GuestSource` trait, `Resolved`, and `Pool<K>` (checkpoints 5, 14, 19). It depends on `morphir-core` for IR version matching and stays wasm32-clean. `morphir-host-native` gains `NativeSource` (next to `NativeChannel`) and `InstalledSource`. `ChannelError` gains a `cause`, so a transport failure that began as an I/O or JSON error keeps its text at the daemon boundary (part 2 ruling R8). The umbrella CLI builds a `morphir_host::Registry`, calls resolved sources, and serves the workbench through `Pool`. After this plan the CLI depends on `morphir-daemon` only for `DaemonError` text mapping; part 4 removes the daemon's registry, typestate session, actor, and transport copies.

**Tech Stack:** Rust 2024 (`rust-version = "1.98"`), `async-trait` 0.1, `async-lock` 3 (portable async mutex), `morphir-core` (format versions), `morphir-distribution`, `morphir-common`, `morphir-extension-sdk`, tokio (tests and native only).

**Spec:** discussion 949, checkpoints 5, 10, 14, 18, 19 (local `.dev/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-23-morphir-host-library-design.md`). Part 1 plan #976, part 2 plan #983 and their closing checkpoints. Tracking: epic #958, Phase A #959, finos/morphir-rust#238 (Registry), finos/morphir-rust#239 (Pool), #963 (rest).

---

## Scope of this plan

In part 3:

- `ChannelError` and `HostError::Channel` carry a `cause` so I/O and JSON texts survive (part 2 R8).
- `Registry`, `GuestSource`, `Resolved`, `ProviderMetadata`, `ProviderOrigin`, `InvocationPolicy`, `InvocationMode`, `CapabilityMetadataScope` in `morphir-host`, ported from the daemon with the same rules and texts.
- `NativeSource` and `InstalledSource` in `morphir-host-native`. `NativeSource` stays native because in-process guests run on a blocking worker (`spawn_blocking`), as `NativeChannel` does.
- `Pool<K>` in `morphir-host`, with the 8 behaviours of the workbench's `SessionReuseInvoker`.
- CLI: registry, compile, generate, `extension list`, playground catalog, workbench invoker, and the UI workspace provider move to the host crates. `builtin_provider`, `open_*_session`, `open_loaded`, `installed_loaded`, `session_failure`, `failed_session_message`, and `ui/provider/sessions.rs` are deleted.
- The two missing CLI tests from part 2 (UI installed workspace provider; installed provider rejected-call text).

Part 4 gets its own plan: delete the daemon's `ExtensionRegistry`, typestate `Session`, kameo actor, `ExtensionSession`/`SpawnedProcessSession`/`SpawnedProcessTransport`, `ExtismTransport`, `NativeMepTransport`, `activate_transport`, `ExtensionResponseExt`, and move `ConnectedDaemonSession` to an HTTP `Channel`. Those are now used only inside `morphir-daemon` and its tests.

## Decisions this plan makes inside the spec

1. `GuestSource` is a trait with one `connect` method that returns a boxed `GuestConnection`. The registry never activates anything itself.
2. `Pool` is keyed by provider id and stores a fingerprint (`"{id}@{version}:{origin:?}:{mode:?}"`, as today). A `CallError::Failed` plays the role of the daemon's `SessionLost`: evict, reopen once, retry once. `CallError::Rejected` keeps the session.
3. Registry errors are `HostError::Invalid(text)` with the daemon's texts. At the CLI boundary they pass through `DaemonError::from`, so the `Extension error: ` prefix stays (part 2 R6).
4. `ChannelCause::{Transport, Io, Json}`. `From<HostError> for DaemonError` maps a `Channel` error with cause `Io` or `Json` to `DaemonError::Other(anyhow!(message))`, whose display is the message unchanged, so the CLI prints `IO error: ...` again instead of `Extension error: IO error: ...`.

## Global Constraints

- `morphir-host` must pass `cargo check -p morphir-host --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` and must not depend on tokio (except dev), `morphir-daemon`, `morphir-host-native`, `morphir-distribution`, or any language binding. It may depend on `morphir-core` (checkpoint 19) and a portable async mutex (`async-lock`).
- `morphir-host-native` must not depend on `morphir-daemon`.
- Every trait a browser client implements keeps `MaybeSend` plus the paired `cfg_attr(async_trait)` attributes.
- Resolution rules and texts are unchanged: language or target filter, advertised IR version normalization, installed over built-in, ambiguity and no-match texts, duplicate-id text, invocation policy.
- Wire sequences unchanged. Existing CLI error texts unchanged, now including the `IO error: ...` / `JSON error: ...` texts part 2 R8 changed.
- The workbench keeps: one guest per provider id reused across compile and generate, evict and retry once on a lost session, keep the session on a rejection, `abandon` after a timeout, replacement when the provider fingerprint changes, one-shot calls for direct (native typed) providers, the 120 s invocation timeout.
- Commits: Conventional Commits. No AI attribution, no `Co-Authored-By`. Plain English docs, no em dashes.
- Local process tests flake in parallel on this machine; judge real-process failures with `--test-threads=1`.

## Review Focus

1. **Resolution drift.** A provider that resolved before must resolve the same way (same provider, same mode, same texts). Pinned by porting all 20 daemon `provider_registry` tests to `morphir-host` in task 2.
2. **A pool that keeps a dead guest or drops a live one.** Pinned by the 8 ported workbench behaviours in task 4 and the CLI playground tests in task 7.
3. **Lost I/O text again.** Pinned by the task 1 test that an I/O-rooted channel failure displays `IO error: ...` through `DaemonError::from`.
4. **Weaker validation for installed providers.** `InstalledSource::connect` must return the same `CheckedConnection` as `activate`. Pinned by the task 3 parity test and the traversal test in the umbrella.
5. **Held locks across await points in `Pool`** that block unrelated providers. Pinned by the task 4 test `a_slow_provider_does_not_block_another`.

---

## File map

finos/morphir-rust (`ecosystem/morphir-rust/`):

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/morphir-host/src/channel.rs`, `src/error.rs` | `ChannelCause`, `cause` on `ChannelError` and `HostError::Channel` |
| `crates/morphir-host/src/registry.rs`, `src/registry/types.rs` | `Registry`, `GuestSource`, `Resolved`, metadata and policy types |
| `crates/morphir-host/src/pool.rs` | `Pool<K>` |
| `crates/morphir-host/tests/registry.rs`, `tests/pool.rs` | Ported behaviour tests |
| `crates/morphir-host-native/src/installed.rs`, `src/native.rs` | `InstalledSource`, `NativeSource` |
| `crates/morphir-daemon/src/error.rs` | `From<HostError>` keeps I/O and JSON texts |

finos/morphir (umbrella):

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/morphir/src/extensions.rs`, `src/extensions/guest.rs` | Registry built from host sources; calls through `Resolved` |
| `crates/morphir/src/commands/{compile.rs, compile/prepare.rs, generate.rs, extension.rs}` | Use `morphir_host` registry types |
| `crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/provider/playground.rs` | Catalog and invoker on host types |
| `crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/provider/pool.rs` | New `PooledInvoker` (replaces `sessions.rs`) |
| `crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/provider/extension.rs` | Installed workspace provider through `InstalledSource`, with a test |

## Branches and pull requests

1. Tasks 1 to 4: one finos/morphir-rust branch from `origin/main` (`feat/morphir-host-registry-pool`). One PR after a whole-branch review. Refers to #238, #239.
2. Tasks 5 to 7: one umbrella branch from `origin/main` after that PR merges. Pin the submodule to the merge commit. Refers to #963, #959.

title: Task 1: Keep the cause of a channel failure
description:
### Task 1: Keep the cause of a channel failure

**Files:**
- Modify: `crates/morphir-host/src/channel.rs`, `src/error.rs`, `src/jsonrpc.rs`, `src/testing.rs`, `src/probe.rs` (any `ChannelError`/`HostError::Channel` construction)
- Modify: `crates/morphir-host-native/src/{native.rs, extism/channel.rs, process/channel.rs, process/child.rs}` and tests constructing `ChannelError`
- Modify: `crates/morphir-daemon/src/error.rs`, `src/extensions/process/describe.rs`
- Test: `crates/morphir-host/tests/connection.rs`, `crates/morphir-daemon/src/error.rs` (unit)

**Interfaces:**
- Produces:
  ```rust
  /// What a transport failure began as.
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
  pub enum ChannelCause {
      /// The transport itself failed: a timeout, a closed pipe the host detected, a stopped guest.
      #[default]
      Transport,
      /// An I/O error. The message starts with `IO error: `.
      Io,
      /// A JSON encoding or decoding error. The message starts with `JSON error: `.
      Json,
  }
  pub struct ChannelError { pub message: String, pub state: ChannelState, pub cause: ChannelCause }
  HostError::Channel { message: String, state: ChannelState, cause: ChannelCause }
  impl ChannelCause { pub fn of(error: &HostError) -> Self } // Io -> Io, Json -> Json, Channel{cause} -> cause, else Transport
  ```
- `From<ChannelError> for HostError` copies `cause`. Every place that turns a `HostError` into a `ChannelError` (for example `ProcessChannel::fail`, `ExtismChannel`'s `indeterminate`) sets `cause: ChannelCause::of(&error)`. Combined messages (`"; process cleanup also failed"`, `"; transport abort also failed"`) keep the first error's cause.
- `From<HostError> for DaemonError`: `Json -> Json`, `Io -> Io`, `Channel { cause: Io | Json, message, .. } -> DaemonError::Other(anyhow::anyhow!(message))`, else `Extension(text)`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**
  - Host (`tests/connection.rs`): a `MemoryChannel` that fails `receive` with `ChannelError { message: "IO error: broken pipe".into(), state: ChannelState::Stopped, cause: ChannelCause::Io }`; the call fails with `CallError::Failed(HostError::Channel { cause: ChannelCause::Io, .. })`.
  - Daemon (`src/error.rs` unit test): `DaemonError::from(HostError::Channel { message: "IO error: broken pipe".into(), state: ChannelState::Stopped, cause: ChannelCause::Io }).to_string() == "IO error: broken pipe"`; with `cause: ChannelCause::Transport` the text is `"Extension error: IO error: broken pipe"` (unchanged behaviour for transport causes); a JSON cause keeps `"JSON error: ..."`.
  - Host-native (`src/process/channel.rs` unit test, unix): a `ProcessChannel` whose guest exits at once; `send` of a request fails and the error's `cause` is `Io` when the write hit `EPIPE` (skip-assert the cause if the race yields "closed stdout before a response frame", which is a `Transport` cause; assert one of the two outcomes with its matching cause).
- [ ] **Step 2: Run them and see them fail** (`cargo test -p morphir-host -p morphir-host-native -p morphir-daemon --lib --tests`): compile errors on `cause`.
- [ ] **Step 3: Implement** the type, the `of` helper, every construction site (list them with `rg -n 'ChannelError \{|HostError::Channel \{' crates`), and the daemon mapping. `MemoryChannel::fail` keeps taking a `ChannelError`. Daemon `anyhow` is already a dependency.
- [ ] **Step 4: Run** `cargo test -p morphir-host -p morphir-host-native`, `cargo test -p morphir-daemon --lib --tests -- --test-threads=1`, clippy on the three crates with `--all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, the wasm32 check, fmt.
- [ ] **Step 5: Commit** `feat(host): keep what a transport failure began as`.

/// A checked MEP connection to one provider, ready to open.
pub(crate) type ProviderConnection =
    morphir_host_native::CheckedConnection<morphir_host::JsonRpcConnection<Box<dyn morphir_host::Channel>, morphir_host::ExpectedChecks>>;

/// Open a connection to a configured process provider.
pub(crate) async fn configured(launch: ProcessLaunch, provider: &str) -> Result<ProviderConnection, CliError>;

/// Open a connection to a resolved provider that speaks MEP
/// (`NativeMep`, `ProcessMep` or `WasmMep`).
pub(crate) async fn resolved(
    home: &MorphirHome,
    workspace: &Path,
    provider: &str,
    mode: InvocationMode,
    native: Option<&NativeExtension>,
    installed: Option<&InstalledExtensionSnapshot>,
) -> Result<ProviderConnection, CliError>;

/// Open, make one call, close. Errors keep the CLI's texts.
pub(crate) async fn call_once<P: Serialize, R: DeserializeOwned>(
    connection: ProviderConnection,
    provider: &str,
    method: &str,
    request: P,
) -> Result<R, CliError>;

/// Open and read what the provider negotiated, then close.
pub(crate) async fn negotiate(connection: ProviderConnection, provider: &str) -> Result<NegotiatedProvider, CliError>;
