title: morphir-host Phase A, part 2: native channels, probe, and CLI one-shot calls Implementation Plan
description:
# morphir-host Phase A, part 2: native channels, probe, and CLI one-shot calls Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Put the process, Extism, and in-process native transports behind `morphir_host::Channel` in a new crate `morphir-host-native`, move the describe probe and the negotiation checks into `morphir-host`, and run every CLI one-shot extension call (compile, generate, workspace discovery, install probe, publish describe, configured providers) through `morphir_host::Session`.

**Architecture:** `morphir-host` stays portable. It gains `Channel::abort`, `ExpectedChecks` (the daemon's full negotiation rules, moved), and `describe` (the install probe with session fallback, moved). The new crate `morphir-host-native` owns everything that needs tokio processes, Extism, or non-portable validation crates: `ProcessLaunch`, framing, staging, `ProcessChannel`, `ExtismChannel`, `NativeChannel`, result validation, and `activate`. `morphir-daemon` keeps its public API and delegates to both crates. The umbrella CLI then drops its typestate one-shot paths. The workbench session pool and the provider registry stay on the daemon until part 3.

**Tech Stack:** Rust 2024 (`rust-version = "1.98"`), tokio (`process`, `io-util`, `time`, `rt`), `extism` 1, `tempfile` 3, `semver` 1, `async-trait` 0.1, `morphir-extension-sdk`, `morphir-core`, `morphir-distribution`, `morphir-workspace`.

**Spec:** design record https://github.com/finos/morphir/discussions/949, checkpoints 5, 6, 10, 14 and 18 (local `.dev/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-23-morphir-host-library-design.md`). Part 1 plan and its rulings: https://github.com/finos/morphir/discussions/976. Tracking: epic #958, Phase A #959, finos/morphir-rust#237 (rest), finos/morphir-rust#240 (transports part), #963 (rest).

---

## Scope of this plan

In part 2:

- `morphir-host`: `Channel::abort`, `impl Channel for Box<C>`, `ExpectedChecks` and the expectation types, and `describe`.
- New crate `morphir-host-native` (checkpoint 18): process launch, framing and staging, `ProcessChannel`, `NativeChannel`, `ExtismChannel` with the Extism container, result validation, `CheckedConnection`, and `activate`.
- `morphir-daemon` delegates to the moved code. Its public API does not change.
- Umbrella CLI: install probe, publish describe, configured providers, installed providers (`ProcessMep`, `WasmMep`), native MEP providers, and the workbench workspace provider run through `morphir_host::Session`.

Part 3 gets its own plan:

- `Registry` and `GuestSource`, and provider resolution out of `ExtensionRegistry` (#238).
- `Pool`, and the workbench leaves `sessions.rs` and `SessionHandle` (#239).
- `morphir-daemon` drops its typestate session and actor, and removes `ExtensionResponseExt` (#240 rest).

## Decisions this plan makes inside the spec

1. `Channel` gains `abort` with a default that calls `close`. Part 1 used `close` for both an orderly close after `exit` and an abort after a protocol failure. A process channel must kill its child on abort, but wait for it on close. Waiting after a failure would hang for the full request timeout.
2. `describe` lives in portable `morphir-host`, not in `morphir-host-native`. It needs only the SDK and `semver`, so a browser host can probe too.
3. Method-result validation (compile IR checks, generated artifact paths) moves to `morphir-host-native`, because it needs `morphir-core` and `morphir-distribution`. `CheckedConnection` wraps any `GuestConnection` and applies it. A validation failure closes the session in order, the same way a decode failure does (part 1 ruling R6). The daemon aborted instead. Both end the session and report the error.
4. The daemon's Extism host functions (`MorphirHostFunctions`) are stubs today. They move unchanged. This plan does not implement them.
5. The CLI keeps `NativeDirect` calls (typed Rust calls on built-in providers) as they are. They are not MEP sessions.

## Global Constraints

- Crates: `ecosystem/morphir-rust/crates/morphir-host` (portable) and `ecosystem/morphir-rust/crates/morphir-host-native` (new). Workspace members are `crates/*`. Add `morphir-host-native` to root `default-members`, to the README crate table, and to every `.github/ci-impact.toml` `crates` list that names `morphir-daemon` (part 1 lesson: `classify.py` only tests `default-members`).
- `morphir-host` must still pass `cargo check -p morphir-host --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` and must not depend on tokio (except as a dev-dependency), `morphir-daemon`, `morphir-host-native`, `morphir-distribution`, `morphir-core`, or any language binding.
- `morphir-host-native` must not depend on `morphir-daemon`. `morphir-daemon` depends on `morphir-host-native`.
- Every trait a browser client implements keeps the `MaybeSend` plus paired `cfg_attr(async_trait)` pattern.
- The wire sequence to released guests does not change:
  - Session: `morphir.initialize` (id 1), calls (ids 2, 3, ...), `morphir.shutdown`, `morphir.exit`.
  - Probe: `morphir.extension.describe` (id 1). Fallback: `morphir.initialize` (id 2), `morphir.initialized` notification, `morphir.extension.capabilities` (id 3), `morphir.shutdown` (id 4), then `morphir.exit`.
  - Frames: `Content-Length: {len}\r\n\r\n{json}`.
- Existing error texts stay byte-identical. The daemon and CLI tests match them.
- The CLI's own message formats stay: `Provider '{provider}' rejected '{method}': {error}`, `Provider '{provider}' failed during {operation}: {error}`, `Failed to start provider '{provider}': {error}`.
- Commits: Conventional Commits. No AI attribution, no `Co-Authored-By`.
- Doc comments in plain English. No em dashes.
- Local process tests are flaky in parallel on this machine (100 ms timeouts). Run real-process suites with `--test-threads=1` when judging a failure.

## Review Focus

1. **An abort that waits.** After a protocol failure a process channel must kill the child promptly, not wait up to 30 s. Pinned by the task 1 test `a_protocol_failure_aborts_rather_than_closes` and the task 5 test `abort_kills_the_child_without_waiting`.
2. **A second `exit`.** The daemon's process `terminate` sent `morphir.exit` itself. `JsonRpcConnection::close` now sends it through `send`, so `ProcessChannel::close` must not send another. Pinned by the task 5 test `close_after_exit_waits_without_a_second_exit`.
3. **Probe wire sequence drift.** Released guests (Elm 0.3.1, scala-elm) fall back to the session path with exact ids. Pinned by the task 3 test `fallback_uses_the_released_ids_and_order` and by the host compatibility suite in task 9.
4. **Weaker validation after the move.** Installed providers must still get discovery locks, legacy backend rules, and artifact path checks. Pinned by the moved daemon tests in tasks 2 and 7 and by the task 9 test that generates through an installed provider with a traversal artifact (`generate_rejects_traversal_from_an_installed_provider_without_writing`, already in the umbrella).
5. **Staging leaks.** Verified bytes are staged in private temp directories. A channel must keep the staging directory alive until the child exits, and remove it after. Pinned by the moved test `verified_bytes_stage_under_the_explicit_managed_directory` and the umbrella test `staging_is_private_under_home_and_removed_after_success_or_failure`.

---

## File map

finos/morphir-rust (`ecosystem/morphir-rust/`):

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/morphir-host/src/channel.rs` | `Channel::abort`, `impl Channel for Box<C>` |
| `crates/morphir-host/src/jsonrpc.rs` | Use `abort` on failure |
| `crates/morphir-host/src/testing.rs` | `MemoryChannel` counts aborts |
| `crates/morphir-host/src/expected.rs` | `ExpectedExtension`, `PersistedExtensionCapabilities`, `CapabilityExpectation`, `ExpectedChecks`, `validate_negotiation` (moved) |
| `crates/morphir-host/src/probe.rs` | `describe`, `Description`, `DescriptionSource`, `permits_fallback`, `check_capability_kinds` (moved) |
| `crates/morphir-host-native/Cargo.toml` | New crate |
| `crates/morphir-host-native/src/lib.rs` | Exports |
| `crates/morphir-host-native/src/process/{mod.rs,launch.rs,frame.rs,stage.rs,child.rs,channel.rs}` | Launch, framing, staging, child, `ProcessChannel` |
| `crates/morphir-host-native/src/native.rs` | `NativeChannel` |
| `crates/morphir-host-native/src/extism/{mod.rs,container.rs,host_functions.rs,channel.rs}` | Extism container (moved), `ExtismChannel` |
| `crates/morphir-host-native/src/results.rs` | Result validation (moved), `CheckedConnection` |
| `crates/morphir-host-native/src/activate.rs` | `activate`, `ActivatedGuest` |
| `crates/morphir-daemon/src/extensions/**` | Delegate to the two crates, keep the public API |

finos/morphir (umbrella):

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/morphir/Cargo.toml` | Add `morphir-host-native` |
| `crates/morphir/src/extensions.rs` | One-shot calls through `morphir_host::Session` |
| `crates/morphir/src/extensions/guest.rs` | New: open a checked connection for a resolved or configured provider, map errors to `CliError` |
| `crates/morphir/src/commands/extension/probe.rs`, `commands/extension.rs` | `describe` through `ProcessChannel` |
| `crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/provider/extension.rs` | Workspace provider through a session |
| `crates/morphir/tests/support/process_bundle.rs` | `describe` through `ProcessChannel` |

## Branches and pull requests

1. Tasks 1 to 7: one branch of finos/morphir-rust from `origin/main` in the submodule checkout (`git -C ecosystem/morphir-rust switch -c feat/morphir-host-native origin/main`). One PR after a whole-branch review. It refers to #237 and #240.
2. Tasks 8 and 9: one umbrella branch from `origin/main` after that PR merges and main CI passes on the merge commit. Pin the submodule to the merge commit. The PR refers to #963 and #959.

title: morphir-host Phase A, part 1: portable session core Implementation Plan
description:
# morphir-host Phase A, part 1: portable session core Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Create the portable `morphir-host` crate with a sans-IO MEP session core. Run the daemon's existing session controller on top of that core without changing its behaviour. Make every CLI path offer one host identity and one version list.

**Architecture:** `morphir-host` holds the MEP handshake as a synchronous state machine (`SessionCore`): an event goes in and one action comes out. Two async shells drive the core. The first is the existing typestate `Session<T, S>` in `morphir-daemon`, which keeps its public API, so the CLI and the daemon's 60+ session tests become the regression suite for the core. The second is a new portable `JsonRpcConnection` over a `Channel` trait. It has no tokio code and compiles for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`. The CLI then takes its peer name and version list from one `HostConfig`.

**Tech Stack:** Rust 2024 (workspace `rust-version = "1.98"`), `serde`/`serde_json`, `thiserror` 2, `async-trait` 0.1, `tokio` (tests only in `morphir-host`), `morphir-extension-sdk`, `morphir-workspace`.

**Spec:** the design record is https://github.com/finos/morphir/discussions/949 (checkpoints 1 to 17). It is also in the local notes: `.dev/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-23-morphir-host-library-design.md`. Tracking: epic finos/morphir#958, Phase A finos/morphir#959. This plan covers finos/morphir-rust#236, part of finos/morphir-rust#237, and the host-identity part of finos/morphir#963.

---

## Scope of this plan

Phase A is too large for one plan. This plan is part 1. Part 1 alone produces software that works and is tested.

In part 1:

- `morphir-host` crate with `HostConfig`, `HostError`, `Negotiated`, envelope validation, `SessionChecks`, `SessionCore`, `Channel`, `GuestConnection`, `JsonRpcConnection`, `Session`, the one-shot helpers, and a `MemoryChannel` test double.
- `morphir-daemon`'s typestate controller runs on `SessionCore`. Its public API does not change.
- The CLI uses one `host_config()` for every `initialize` and `describe`.

Part 2 gets its own plan after part 1 merges:

- Move the process stdio, Extism, and native transports out of `morphir-daemon` and behind `Channel` (#240).
- Move `describe` with session fallback (the install probe) into `morphir-host`.
- `Registry` and `GuestSource`, and the move of provider resolution out of `ExtensionRegistry` (#238).
- Move CLI compile and generate onto `morphir-host` sessions (the rest of #963).
- `Pool`, and the workbench leaves `sessions.rs` (#239).

## Decisions this plan makes inside the spec

Check these during review. Each one narrows the spec. None of them changes a checkpoint.

1. `SessionCore::handle` returns one `Action`, not a `Vec<Action>`. MEP sessions have one request in flight, so every event produces exactly one action.
2. `GuestConnection` has a generic `call(method, params)`. `Session` provides the typed `compile` and `generate`. A later `ComponentConnection` maps method names to WIT exports.
3. `HostServices` is not in part 1. No MEP guest calls the host over JSON-RPC today, so a `HostServices` trait would have no caller. It arrives with the component imports in Phase D.
4. The core does not send `morphir.initialized` in a normal session. The daemon does not send it today, and released guests were tested without it. Only the describe fallback sends it, and that code stays in the daemon in part 1.
5. Method-result validation (compile IR checks, generated artifact paths) stays in `morphir-daemon`. It depends on `morphir-core` and `morphir-distribution`, which are not proven portable. `SessionCore` validates the envelope and the negotiation only.

## Global Constraints

- Crate location: `ecosystem/morphir-rust/crates/morphir-host` (finos/morphir-rust). Workspace members are `crates/*`, so no workspace edit is needed.
- `morphir-host` must pass `cargo check -p morphir-host --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. It must not depend on tokio (except as a dev-dependency), `morphir-daemon`, `morphir-distribution`, `morphir-core`, or any language binding.
- Traits that a browser client implements use `MaybeSend` (it means `Send` on native targets and nothing on `wasm32`), with `#[cfg_attr(not(target_arch = "wasm32"), async_trait)]` and `#[cfg_attr(target_arch = "wasm32", async_trait(?Send))]`.
- MEP versions: offer `SUPPORTED_MEP_VERSIONS` from `morphir-extension-sdk` (currently `["0.1"]`). Never hardcode `"0.1"` outside tests.
- The client supplies the peer. The only `"morphir-cli"` literal in `crates/morphir/src` after task 7 is the one in `host_config()`.
- Error texts that exist today stay byte-identical. Examples: `RPC error {code}: {message}`, `Extension selected protocol version '{v}' that the host did not offer`, `Extension response ID {a} did not match request ID {b}`.
- The wire sequence to released guests stays identical: `morphir.initialize` (id 1), calls (ids 2, 3, ...), `morphir.shutdown`, then `morphir.exit` from the transport.
- Commits: Conventional Commits. No AI attribution, no `Co-Authored-By` lines (EasyCLA).
- Code style: match surrounding code. Doc comments in plain English. No em dashes.

## Review Focus

These failure modes follow from the spec, but ordinary unit tests would miss them. Each line names the task whose test pins it.

1. **Released guests see a different wire sequence.** Examples: an extra `morphir.initialized`, or ids that no longer start at 1. Elm 0.3.1, scala-elm M08, and the published WASM backends would then break. Pinned by the task 4 test `a_session_numbers_requests_in_the_released_order` and by the host compatibility suite in task 7.
2. **Error text changes break CLI tests and user scripts that match messages.** Pinned by exact-string asserts in task 2 (envelope), task 3 (guards), and the unchanged daemon suite in task 4.
3. **A guest RPC error ends the session.** The workbench keeps one guest across clicks, so a rejection must keep the session ready. Pinned by the task 3 test `a_guest_rpc_error_rejects_the_call_and_keeps_the_session` and the daemon actor test `a_rejected_invocation_keeps_the_session_usable`.
4. **A transport failure reports the wrong proven state.** `Indeterminate` must not become `Stopped`, and a failed channel must not be closed a second time. Pinned by the daemon test `retains_an_indeterminate_state_after_an_uncertain_exchange_failure` (task 4) and the task 5 test `a_transport_failure_does_not_close_the_channel_again`.
5. **A later change pulls tokio or a native-only crate into `morphir-host`.** The browser build then breaks without anyone noticing. Pinned by the CI wasm32 check added in task 1.

---

## File map

| `crates/morphir-host/src/session_core.rs` | `SessionChecks`, `BasicChecks`, `Event`, `Action`, `SessionCore` |
| `crates/morphir-host/src/channel.rs` | `Channel`, `Outgoing`, `ChannelError` |

| `crates/morphir-daemon/src/extensions/session/validation.rs` | `DaemonChecks`; remove `validate_response`, `ResponseFailure` |

## Branches and pull requests

1. Tasks 1 to 6 go on a branch of finos/morphir-rust. Create it in the submodule checkout:

title: feat(host-native): reach an extension over HTTP with HttpChannel
description:
### Task 3: `HttpChannel` replaces `ConnectedDaemonSession`

Bead: `morphir-opua.1.1.6.3`.

**Files:**
- Create: `crates/morphir-host-native/src/http.rs`
- Modify: `crates/morphir-host-native/Cargo.toml` (feature `http = ["dep:jsonrpsee"]`, `jsonrpsee = { version = "0.26", features = ["http-client"], optional = true }`; dev-dependency `jsonrpsee` with `server`, `macros`), `crates/morphir-host-native/src/lib.rs` (`#[cfg(feature = "http")] pub mod http;`)
- Move: `crates/morphir-daemon/examples/mep-http-backend.rs` (and its `examples/support/` if used) to `crates/morphir-host-native/examples/`, with `required-features = ["http"]`
- Move and port: `crates/morphir-daemon/tests/connected_daemon_extension.rs` to `crates/morphir-host-native/tests/http_channel.rs`
- Modify: `.mise/tasks/test/daemon` (rename to `.mise/tasks/test/http`, build the example from `morphir-host-native --features http`, run `--test http_channel -- --ignored`)

**Interfaces:**
- Produces: `morphir_host_native::http::{HttpChannel, HttpEndpoint}`:

```rust
pub struct HttpEndpoint {
    pub id: String,
    pub url: String,
    pub request_timeout: Duration, // default 30 s, as ConnectedDaemonSession
}

impl HttpChannel {
    /// Validate the endpoint (non-empty id, parseable URL) and build the client.
    pub fn connect(endpoint: HttpEndpoint) -> Result<Self, HostError>;
    /// A checked connection expecting extension `endpoint.id`.
    pub fn connection(self) -> CheckedConnection<JsonRpcConnection<Box<dyn Channel>, ExpectedChecks>>;
}
```

Channel behaviour (copy the contract of `crates/morphir-daemon/src/extensions/connected.rs:101-155`):
- `send(Outgoing::Request)`: POST the method with the params object, buffer the reply for `receive`, re-stamp the caller's id on it. Non-object params: buffer an `invalid_params` error response, send nothing.
- `send(Outgoing::Notification)`: ignored (no `morphir.exit` over HTTP, as today).
- A JSON-RPC error reply (`ClientError::Call`): buffered as `ExtensionResponse::error(code, message)`.
- Any other client error: `ChannelError { state: Indeterminate, cause: ChannelCause::Transport, message }`.
- `close()`: `Stopped` when the last buffered reply answered `morphir.shutdown` successfully, otherwise `Indeterminate`.
- `abort()`: no-op.

- [ ] **Step 1: Port the tests first.** Copy the 4 `#[ignore]` tests from `connected_daemon_extension.rs` into `tests/http_channel.rs`, rewritten over `Session::open(HttpChannel::connect(endpoint)?.connection(), &config)` and `session.compile(...)`. Keep their names. Add two non-ignored unit tests in `http.rs` with a local `jsonrpsee` server on `127.0.0.1:0`: a JSON-RPC error reply becomes an error response (`CallError::Rejected` at the session), and a closed port gives `ChannelError { state: Indeterminate, cause: Transport }`.
- [ ] **Step 2: Run to verify they fail** (`cargo test -p morphir-host-native --features http`): unresolved `http` module.
- [ ] **Step 3: Implement** `http.rs` as specified.
- [ ] **Step 4: Run** `cargo test -p morphir-host-native --features http`, then `mise run test:http`. Expected: PASS, including the 4 ignored tests through the mise task.
- [ ] **Step 5: Commit** `feat(host-native): reach an extension over HTTP with HttpChannel`.

---

Done when the wrapper passes the MEP host suite.

title: feat: add the TypeScript host wrapper over the morphir-host component (finos/morphir-typescript#35)
description: Wrap the morphir-host component for Node and browsers with jco, supplying a child-process Channel for Node and a Web Worker Channel for browsers, using morphir:host where component model async and JSPI support allow it and falling back to morphir:host-sync otherwise, plus choosing a generator for the TypeScript protocol types. Done when the wrapper passes the MEP host suite in Node.

title: feat(host): compile morphir-host to a component with async and sync worlds (finos/morphir-rust#247)
description: Compile morphir-host to a WASM component with two worlds: morphir:host, exposing Session, Pool, one-shot calls and Registry as async functions with async send and receive imports, and morphir:host-sync, exporting the sans-IO handle function for embedders without component model async. Done when Wasmtime runs morphir:host and passes the MEP host suite, and morphir:host-sync passes the same suite through a sync driver.

title: feat(host): add ComponentConnection for component guests (finos/morphir-rust#246)
description: Add a GuestConnection that calls the exports of a component guest built against the generated morphir:mep world, using Wasmtime 46 or later, with guest calls to the host going through HostServices as WIT imports and IR moving as bytes with no JSON round trip. Done when a component guest and a process guest pass the same Session tests.

title: feat(spec): publish the MEP contract as a Morphir model package (finos/morphir#969)
description: Publish the MEP model as a Library package, for example finos.org/morphir/mep@0.2.3 with IR package morphir/mep, once pack and publish exist, so language repos can replace their vendored IR copy with morphir package restore. Done when a language repo restores the MEP package and regenerates its types with no diff.

title: feat(package): zip archives, document-tree IR and Amazon Ion in model packages (finos/morphir#968)
description: Extend the library contract, which today only allows an unpacked directory with one classic JSON IR v4 payload, to also allow a package as a single zip archive, document-tree IR, and Amazon Ion text and binary, keeping per-file digests inside archives and widening content path rules for the new file names. Done when the library contract and schemas describe all three and resolve and restore accept a zip package in a local registry test.

title: feat(mep): carry IR as a typed payload with a media type (finos/morphir#967)
description: Change MEP so IR travels as IrPayload with media_type, layout and data fields, with guest capabilities listing the IR formats each guest accepts and produces; the host sends the on-disk format when the guest accepts it and converts once otherwise, keeping JSON as an accepted format. Done when a JSON-only guest keeps working and an Ion-capable guest receives IR with no conversion.

title: chore(wit): split the root wit folder by subject (finos/morphir#966)
description: Mark wit/morphir-extension, wit/morphir-frontend, wit/morphir-backend, wit/morphir-component and wit/morphir-vfs as superseded by the generated morphir:mep world, record their incremental, streaming and vfs ideas as candidate capabilities first, then delete them and move wit/morphir-ir to spec/ir/wit/. Done when the candidate capability list is recorded and wit/ no longer exists at the repo root.

title: feat(mck): add the MEP conformance suite (finos/morphir#965)
description: Add spec/mep/mck with host cases (a scripted guest plus the messages the host must send and how it must react) and guest cases (a request and its required response shape), delivered through morphir mck kit vendor as suite mep. Done when the suite vendoring command produces a locked snapshot and morphir-host passes the host suite in CI.

title: feat(gleam): support BitArray or an SDK Bytes type in the Gleam frontend (finos/morphir-rust#245)
description: IrPayload (planned in Phase C, morphir-opua.1.3.1) carries IR bytes as a BitArray field, which the Gleam frontend does not support today; add BitArray support or an SDK Bytes type, mapped to WIT list<u8> and JSON base64. The MEP contract model (spec/mep/contract/src/mep.gleam) has no IrPayload yet, so this work comes before IrPayload is added to it. Done when a Gleam record with a bytes field compiles to IR.

title: feat(python): support List and Maybe in the Python backend (finos/morphir-rust#244)
description: The Python backend rejects List and Maybe (it accepts only scalar, local reference or fixed tuple fields), and the MEP contract uses both, so add support for them. Generic declarations moved to their own lower-priority bead, because the MEP model declares no generic types. Done when the MEP model (spec/mep/contract/src/mep.gleam) generates importable Python types.

title: feat: add a Morphir IR to WIT backend (finos/morphir-rust#243)
description: Add a backend that turns Morphir IR types into a WIT package, mapping records, custom types, Maybe, Result, List and Dict to WIT equivalents, rejecting or encoding recursive types since WIT has none, and taking the package name and version from the model. Done when the MEP model produces a WIT package that wasm-tools component wit accepts and a recursive type gets a clear diagnostic or documented encoding.

title: fix(openapi): JSON Schema for single-constructor records (finos/morphir-rust#242)
description: Fix the morphir-openapi JSON Schema backend so a single-constructor custom type writes as a plain object instead of a oneOf with a kind discriminator. This is the part the MEP contract needs: every MEP record is a single-constructor type. Generic declarations (JSC003) moved to their own lower-priority bead, because the MEP model declares no generic types. Done when a Gleam record type produces a plain object schema and spec/mep can generate JSON Schema for its records.

title: feat(sdk): generate MEP protocol types from the MEP model IR (finos/morphir-rust#241)
description: Vendor a copy of the MEP IR from an exact finos/morphir spec/mep commit with its source and digest, then generate the Rust protocol types in morphir-extension-sdk from it with the morphir-rust backend, replacing the hand-written types. Done when the wire format is unchanged and CI fails when the generated Rust does not match the vendored IR.

title: refactor(daemon): make morphir-daemon a client of morphir-host (finos/morphir-rust#240)
description: Move the process stdio and Extism transports out of morphir-daemon into morphir-host, so morphir-daemon opens guests through morphir-host like any other client while ConnectedDaemonSession keeps its HTTP path. Done when morphir-daemon has no MEP handshake or codec of its own and daemon tests pass unchanged.

title: Kit: Ion reference encoding, spelling/semantic cases, round trip, diffs, HTML, CI summary
description:
### Task 7: Complete the Ion reference kit and baselines

Owns `morphir-1qhu.7`. Move the remaining cases according to an explicit list of spelling rules by profile, leaving semantic cases in Ion. Run both adapters, record new transcript exchanges under the append-only baseline rule, and verify report schema, kit grammar, HTML, CLI, and CI gates. Close this bead only when the spec's acceptance criteria hold and `morphir-vvgi.9` is unblocked.
notes:
START BRIEF (handoff 2026-09-26). Epic-level state, rules and gates: bd show morphir-1qhu (notes).

SPEC: docs/design/draft/testing/mck-ion-reference.md. Read Design (Profiles, Two kinds of case, How the runner checks a semantic case, Failures, Diffs, Grammar checks, Report and HTML, CI, Frozen baselines), Testing and Open questions.

FIRST STEP: this bead is too big for one PR. Brainstorm the slicing with the user, draft a plan in .dev/docs/superpowers/plans/, then `bd-plan import <plan.md> --parent morphir-1qhu --spec morphir-1qhu --link <N>=morphir-1qhu.7` (AGENTS.md "Superpowers artifacts live in beads").

SUGGESTED SLICES (a proposal, not agreed):
1. Unified diffs for every canonical mismatch (replace first-line-only check_canonical, crates/morphir-mck/src/ir/compare.rs:37-46), optional `diff` + `check` members on report records, size cap. Needs a line-diff crate (e.g. `similar`; none in workspace). No protocol change; lands alone.
2. Canonical Ion text writer settings (spacing, symbol quoting, struct order) written into docs/design/draft/ir/ion.md. Spec open question; must be settled before any `ion canonical` fence is frozen. Coordinate with epic morphir-vvgi (Ion codec lives in ecosystem/morphir-rust, morphir-common IrCodec, FormatId ion).
3. Protocol contractVersion 2: Profile = ion|json|yaml (crates/morphir-mck/src/transport/protocol.rs, protocol schema), capabilities request carries contractVersion, adapters list ion only for v2 drivers. Rust adapter declares ion (morphir-rust PR + pin move).
4. @spelling/@semantic cases: runner transcoding with morphir-common codecs, round-trip byte compare in Ion, failure kinds (kit-error / answer-not-readable / diff / skipped), grammar checks in mck check. HOW TO START IN A NEW WORKTREE
  git worktree add ../morphir-<topic> -b feat/<topic> origin/main
  cd ../morphir-<topic> && git submodule update --init ecosystem/morphir-rust
  bd prime; bd show morphir-1qhu; bd show morphir-1qhu.7; bd update morphir-1qhu.7 --claim
Superpowers specs/plans go through bd-plan (AGENTS.md "Superpowers artifacts live in beads"); drafts stay in .dev/.

WORKING RULES THE USER SET
- One thing at a time. One PR at a time, no parallel builds or agents fighting over cargo.
- Scoped gates while iterating (cargo test -p <crate> --test <name>, clippy -p morphir); keep build output short (grep test result / error).
- Push branches and open PRs without asking. Blanket squash+admin merge for morphir-1qhu PRs once CI is green and every review comment has a reply. Merge by hand, not gh auto-merge.
- Watch every PR you open in the background until merged; restart the watcher after each push.
- Codex comments: react eyes, verify, reply; thumbs-up only for real issues.
- No AI attribution in commits/PRs (EasyCLA). Commit trailer: Refs https://github.com/finos/morphir/issues/946
- Nested .claude/worktrees: pre-push fmt hook fails on cargo metadata; push with MORPHIR_SKIP_HOOKS=1 after running cargo fmt --check yourself.
- After closing beads: mise run beads:publish && git push origin beads-sync.

GATES THAT MATTER HERE
- Kit: cargo test -p morphir-mck; cargo test -p morphir --test mck_run --test mck_convert --test mck_command --test mck_report; morphir mck check spec/ir/mck; morphir mck convert --check (run after any spec/ir/mck/*.md edit; twins must stay in step).
- itest: cargo test -p morphir --lib commands::itest; --test itest --test eval; morphir itest examples --tag suite:offline -> 18 passed; 0 failed; 8 not selected.
- CLI flag changes: mise run docs:cli, commit completions/ docs/cli docs/man.

title: Unified extension SDK for guest and host sides across runtimes (Rust, TypeScript, Python)
description: Follow-up from the single-file synthesis work (finos/morphir#915, #917). Today the portable workspace discovery rules (selection confinement, duplicate rejection, name-required, empty language) live only in Rust (morphir-workspace). The morphir-elm MEP extension (TypeScript, vnext) gets a minimal hand port of the ad-hoc subset so it can synthesize, which duplicates those rules. Build one SDK covering both the guest side (extension authors) and the host side (protocol types, discovery validation, compile envelope) for several runtimes, early targets Rust, TypeScript and Python, so providers stop re-porting protocol rules. Retire the TS hand port once the TS SDK exists.
design:
# Cross-language extension SDK Local working notes. Decided checkpoints are published at https://github.com/finos/morphir/discussions/949. This file is gitignored. A session is one live guest after the handshake. Opening a session starts the guest, negotiates the protocol version, and stores the guest's capabilities. The session exposes compile, generate, and describe. The client owns the session's lifetime and closes it. A client can hold many sessions at the same time, one for each guest. A server can keep a few sessions for the same guest and use them like workers. The host library opens every guest. Guests do not connect back to the host. The host library has three layers. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph clients["Clients"] CLI["morphir compile / generate / install"] WB["web workbench"] SRV["server"] BR["browser (WASM + JS)"] end subgraph HL["Host library"] OS["One-shot helpers

(later decision)"] ``` 1. **Session.** The core. `open(guest, peer)` returns a session. The peer name and version still come from the client. 2. **One-shot helpers.** Compile, generate, and probe each open a session, make one call, and close it. `morphir compile`, `morphir generate`, and install use these helpers. Probe opens a session, reads the capabilities, checks the statement, and closes the session. 3. **Pool.** An optional helper built on sessions. It keeps one guest for each key, removes a guest that stopped, and retries a request once on a new guest. This is the logic in `crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/provider/sessions.rs` today. The web workbench uses the pool instead of its own cache. A server can use the pool or build its own. ```rust // sketch pub struct Session { /* negotiated version, capabilities, transport */ } impl Session { pub async fn open(guest: GuestSpec, peer: PeerInfo) -> Result; pub fn capabilities(&self) -> &Capabilities; pub async fn compile(&mut self, request: CompileRequest) -> Result; pub async fn generate(&mut self, request: GenerateRequest) -> Result; pub async fn describe(&mut self) -> Result; pub async fn close(self) -> Result<()>; } // One-shot helper: open, call, close. pub async fn compile_once(guest: GuestSpec, peer: PeerInfo, request: CompileRequest) -> Result { let mut session = Session::open(guest, peer).await?; let result = session.compile(request).await; session.close().await?; result } // Optional pool. The client picks the key and the limits. pub struct Pool { /* K -> Session */ } impl Pool { pub async fn compile(&self, key: K, request: CompileRequest) -> Result; pub async fn generate(&self, key: K, request: GenerateRequest) -> Result; pub async fn abandon(&self, key: &K); } ``` Two playground clicks through the pool: ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant WB as Web workbench participant P as Pool participant S as Session participant G as Elm guest User->>WB: click Compile WB->>P: compile(key = elm, request) P->>S: open (no session yet for key) S->>G: start, initialize P->>S: compile S->>G: compile G-->>WB: IR User->>WB: click Generate WB->>P: generate(key = elm, request) P->>S: generate (same session, no start) S->>G: generate G-->>WB: files Note over P,G: if the guest stopped: evict, open a new session, retry once ``` The host library keeps no hidden global state. The client decides pool size, idle time, and tenant limits. Reason: the host library must serve the CLI, desktop and server clients, and browser clients through WASM with JS glue. A hidden pool needs global state and timers, and `wasm32` does not supply threads for them. A session handle maps to a JS object that the caller frees. It also gives a server control of concurrency and isolation. ```ts // sketch: browser client through a wasm-bindgen adapter using session = await Session.open(guest, { name: "morphir-web", version }); const result = await session.compile(request); // `using` calls session[Symbol.dispose]() here, which frees the guest. ``` Consequence: the session must not depend on one transport. Process stdio, Extism, HTTP, and a browser worker or in-page WASM guest must all fit behind the same session. MEP versioning before 1.0.0 MEP uses the minor-bump rule until it reaches 1.0.0. Published contracts carry no prerelease tags. - A breaking change bumps the minor version: `0.2.x` to `0.3.0`. - An additive, backward-compatible change bumps the patch version: `0.2.1` to `0.2.2`. `@since(version = 0.2.2)` marks the new WIT items. - The JSON-RPC handshake sends the canonical version, for example `"0.2"`. The WIT package carries the full version, for example `morphir:mep@0.2.3`. - `SUPPORTED_MEP_VERSIONS` lists canonical versions, for example `["0.1", "0.2"]`. `MEP_VERSION = "0.1"` in `morphir-extension-sdk/src/protocol.rs` is already in this form. Reason: WIT accepts full SemVer 2.0, prerelease included. The component model Explainer turns each version into a canonical version, and a host matches imports on that string. A version with a prerelease tag is never split, so each draft is a separate contract that needs an exact match. ```text 0.2.6 -> 0.2 (0.x: split after minor) 1.2.3 -> 1 (>= 1: split after major) 0.2.0-draft.1 -> 0.2.0-draft.1 (prerelease: never split) ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph A["minor-bump rule"] g1["guest imports morphir:mep@0.2.6"] -->|"canonical 0.2"| h1["host provides morphir:mep@0.2.1"] end subgraph B["prerelease tags"] g2["guest imports 0.2.0-draft.2"] -.-x|"no match"| h2["host provides 0.2.0-draft.1"] end ``` With the minor-bump rule, the JSON-RPC and WIT bindings negotiate and link the same way. After 1.0.0, MEP uses standard SemVer, and the canonical version is the major version. ## Checkpoint 9. The digest rules keep working for each file inside the archive. The content path rules must allow the file names that document-tree IR and Ion need. ## Checkpoint 13. IR in MEP messages is a typed payload with a media type MEP carries IR as a typed payload. The payload names its media type and its layout. Each guest states which IR formats it accepts and which it produces. ```gleam // sketch: mep.gleam pub type IrLayout { Classic DocumentTree } pub type IrPayload { IrPayload(media_type: String, layout: IrLayout, data: BitArray) } // media_type: "application/ion", "application/ion+text", "application/json" ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR D["IR on disk
Ion binary"] --> H["host library"] H -->|"guest accepts Ion: send as is"| G1["backend guest A"] H -->|"guest accepts JSON only: convert once"| G2["backend guest B"] ``` Rules: - The guest's capabilities list the IR formats it accepts and the formats it produces. The host sends the IR in its format on disk when the guest accepts that format. When the guest does not, the host converts the IR one time. - The JSON-RPC binding carries JSON IR inline and Ion text as a string. It carries Ion binary as base64. - The WIT binding carries `data` as `list` with no extra encoding. This is the `encoded-ast` shape from checkpoint 7. - JSON stays an accepted format. Guests that accept only JSON keep working. - Today `CompileResult.ir` and `GenerateRequest.ir` in `morphir-extension-sdk` are `serde_json::Value`. They become `IrPayload`. Open gap: the Gleam frontend does not support `BitArray` today. The contract needs that support, or a `Bytes` type from the SDK. This decision depends on the Amazon Ion IR codec work in finos/morphir-rust#233 and finos/morphir#951.## Checkpoint 14. Each client registers its own guests `morphir-host` defines `Registry` and `GuestSource`. It does not depend on `morphir-gleam-binding`, `morphir-elm-binding`, or any other language binding. Each client registers the guests it needs. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph H["morphir-host (no language bindings)"] R["Registry"] GS["GuestSource: Native | Process | Component"] end CLI["CLI"] -->|"Gleam, Elm when requested (native)
+ installed catalog"| R BR["browser client"] -->|"component guests"| R SRV["server"] -->|"its own set"| R ``` ```rust // sketch let mut registry = Registry::new(); registry.register(GuestSource::native(gleam_guest()))?; if elm_requested { registry.register(GuestSource::native(elm_guest()))?; } for snapshot in catalog.installed() { registry.register(GuestSource::from_installed(snapshot))?; } ``` - A native guest is one more `GuestConnection` from checkpoint 10. It runs in the same process, with no channel and no JSON. - The CLI keeps today's rules from `crates/morphir/src/extensions.rs`. Gleam is always registered. Elm is registered only when requested. Installed guests come from the CLI's extension catalog. That code moves to the new API. - A browser client registers only component guests, so its bundle holds no native bindings. - If a second client needs the same default set, a small composition crate takes over that list at that time. ## Checkpoint 15. The root `wit/` folder splits by subject The root `wit/` folder holds six hand-written packages at `@0.4.0`. No code, CI job, or generator reads them. The folder splits by subject. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph now["wit/ today (hand-written @0.4.0)"] E["extension, frontend, backend,
component, vfs"] I["morphir-ir"] end E -->|"replaced by"| M["spec/mep/generated/wit
morphir:mep (generated)"] E -.->|"ideas: incremental, streaming, vfs"| G["mep.gleam"] I -->|"moves to"| S["spec/ir/wit/"] ``` - `morphir:extension`, `morphir:frontend`, `morphir:backend`, `morphir:component`, and `morphir:vfs` describe the same protocol as the generated `morphir:mep` world. They get a README that marks them superseded. They are deleted when the first generated `morphir:mep` WIT lands. - Before deletion, the ideas in `incremental.wit`, `streaming.wit`, and the `vfs` reader and writer become a list of candidate capabilities for `mep.gleam`. - `morphir:ir` describes the IR, not MEP. It moves to `spec/ir/wit/` under the rule from checkpoint 11 that specs live under `spec/`. The kb mirror in morphir-scala (`kb/bundles/morphir/morphir-upstream/sync.yaml`, mapping `wit/morphir-ir/**`) updates its path. ## Checkpoint 16. TypeScript and Python host ports wrap one core compiled to a component There is one host implementation, `morphir-host` in Rust. The TypeScript and Python host ports are thin wrappers around that core compiled to a WASM component. ```mermaid flowchart TB C1["morphir-host
compiled to a component
world morphir:host"] --> TS1["TypeScript wrapper
(jco)"] C1 --> PY1["Python wrapper
(wasmtime-py)"] TS1 -.->|"imports: Channel, HostServices"| C1 PY1 -.->|"imports: Channel, HostServices"| C1 K["spec/mep/mck
host suite"] -->|"checks"| C1 K -->|"checks"| TS1 K -->|"checks"| PY1 ``` - The component exports a `morphir:host` world: `Session`, `Pool`, the one-shot calls, and `Registry`. - The embedding language supplies `Channel` and `HostServices` as imports, because a Wasm component cannot start processes. The layer split from checkpoint 10 makes this possible. - The TypeScript wrapper uses `jco`. The Python wrapper uses `wasmtime-py`. Each wrapper adds idiomatic names and process channels, and nothing else. - Every language uses the same handshake, codec, and pool, so the ports cannot drift apart. - The MCK host suite in `spec/mep/mck` still checks the core and each wrapper. ```ts // sketch: TypeScript wrapper import { Session } from "@finos/morphir-host"; using session = await Session.open(processGuest("morphir-elm"), peer); const result = await session.compile(request); ``` Costs: the core must not block on I/O across the component boundary. It needs component model async, or a core that takes messages in and returns actions (sans-IO). Python users need the `wasmtime` package. The choice between async and sans-IO is the next decision. ## Checkpoint 17. Component model async first, with a sans-IO fallback The target is component model async (WASI 0.3). The `morphir:host` world exports `async func` calls and imports async `send` and `receive`. When an embedder cannot run component model async, it uses a sync world that is driven from a sans-IO core. Python falls back today. Support as of 2026-09-23: | Embedder | Component model async | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | | Native Rust, Wasmtime 46 or later | Supported, on by default | Wasmtime 46.0.0 (2026-06-22) enables WASI 0.3 and `component-model-async` by default. Latest is 49.0.0. The Rust API (`bindgen!` async, `func_wrap_concurrent`, `run_concurrent`) is complete. | | Rust guest, wit-bindgen 0.62 | Supported | The `async` feature is on by default. `wasm32-wasip2` with that feature builds 0.3 components. `wasm32-wasip3` is Tier 2 from Rust 1.100.0. | | Node and browsers, jco 1.34 | Experimental | P3 transpiles and runs. The generated glue uses JSPI where a call can suspend. JSPI ships in Chrome 137, Firefox 153, and Safari 27. Node 24 or later may need `--experimental-wasm-jspi`. | | Python, wasmtime-py 49 | Not supported | Only sync component calls. `stream` and `future` values raise `NotImplementedError`. The Wasmtime C API has no async yet (bytecodealliance/wasmtime#13705). | WASI 0.3.0 was ratified on 2026-06-11, and 0.3.1 followed on 2026-08-11. ```mermaid flowchart TB CORE["SessionCore (sans-IO)
handle(event) -> actions"] CORE --> ASYNC["async shell
world morphir:host
async func exports, async imports"] CORE --> SYNC["sync world
morphir:host-sync
handle(event) exported as is"] ASYNC --> RS["native Rust (Wasmtime)"] ASYNC --> JS["Node and browsers (jco, JSPI)"] SYNC --> PY["Python (wasmtime-py)
asyncio driver loop"] ``` ```rust // sketch: the sans-IO core under both worlds pub enum Event { Opened, Received(JsonRpcMessage), Call(Request), Closed } pub enum Action { Send(JsonRpcMessage), Complete(RequestId, Response), Fail(RequestId, Error), Close } impl SessionCore { pub fn handle(&mut self, event: Event) -> Vec; } ``` Rules: - The protocol logic (handshake, codec, id matching, pool bookkeeping) lives in the sans-IO core one time. The async shell and the sync world both drive it. - The async traits from checkpoint 10 are the Rust shell API and the `morphir:host` export. - The Python wrapper drives `morphir:host-sync` with an asyncio loop. When wasmtime-py supports component model async, Python moves to `morphir:host`. - The TypeScript wrapper uses `morphir:host` through jco. If jco P3 is not stable enough for a release, the TypeScript wrapper uses `morphir:host-sync` until it is. - The WIT does not use `error-context`. Wasmtime keeps it off by default, and jco and wasmtime-py do not fully support it. - Delivery confirmation goes in the WIT when it is needed. jco stream backpressure does not confirm that the other side processed a chunk. ## Tracking The design in checkpoints 1 to 17 is approved. The work is tracked in #958. - Phase A, host library in the CLI: #959 - Phase B, MEP contract as a Morphir model: #960 - Phase C, IR formats and model packages: #961 - Phase D, component model and language ports: #962 The work issues are sub-issues of the phase issues. They live in finos/morphir, finos/morphir-rust, finos/morphir-typescript, and finos/morphir-python, and they carry "blocked by" links. ## Checkpoint 18. Native transports live in `morphir-host-native` The process stdio, Extism, and in-process native transports become `Channel` implementations in a new crate, `morphir-host-native`, in finos/morphir-rust. The describe probe with session fallback moves there too. ```mermaid flowchart LR H["morphir-host
portable, no native deps"] --- N["morphir-host-native
ProcessChannel, ExtismChannel,
NativeChannel, probe"] N --> D["morphir-daemon"] N --> C["morphir CLI"] H -.->|"later"| W["morphir-host-wasm
browser adapter"] ``` - `morphir-host` keeps zero native dependencies. Its wasm32 check does not depend on anyone remembering a feature flag. - `morphir-host-native` depends on `morphir-host`, tokio, `extism`, and `morphir-distribution`. - The daemon and the CLI depend on `morphir-host-native`. The browser adapter sits beside it later, the way `morphir-workspace-wasm` sits beside `morphir-workspace`. This settles the open choice in checkpoint 6 ("a native crate or behind a feature"). ## Checkpoint 19. `Registry` lives in portable `morphir-host` Provider resolution moves out of the daemon's `ExtensionRegistry` into `morphir-host`. `morphir-host` takes a dependency on `morphir-core` for IR version matching. `morphir-core` passes `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. ```mermaid flowchart LR H["morphir-host
Registry, GuestSource trait, Pool
+ morphir-core (IR version matching)"] N["morphir-host-native
installed GuestSource
(morphir-distribution)"] C["CLI, workbench, browser, TS/Python wrappers"] N --> H C --> H C --> N ``` - A browser client and the TypeScript and Python wrappers resolve providers with the same rules as the CLI: - the language or target filter - IR version matching - installed providers winning over built-ins - the same ambiguity and no-match texts - `GuestSource` is portable. A built-in `NativeExtension` is a source in `morphir-host`. An installed snapshot is a source in `morphir-host-native`, because it needs `morphir-distribution`. - `Pool` also lives in `morphir-host`. - Cost: the browser build is larger, and `morphir-host` users get `morphir-core`'s `serde_json` features (`preserve_order`, `arbitrary_precision`). Workspace builds already have these through the daemon. ```rust // sketch pub trait GuestSource: MaybeSend + Sync { fn info(&self) -> &ExtensionInfo; fn capabilities(&self) -> &ExtensionCapabilities; fn origin(&self) -> ProviderOrigin; // Builtin | Installed fn native(&self) -> Option<&NativeExtension>; // typed direct calls async fn connect(&self, workspace: &Path) -> Result, HostError>; } let mut registry = Registry::new(); registry.register(Arc::new(NativeSource::new(gleam)))?; registry.register(Arc::new(InstalledSource::new(home, snapshot)))?; // morphir-host-native let resolved = registry.resolve_frontend("elm", "4.0.0", InvocationPolicy::PreferDirect)?; ``` ## Open Phase A is complete (finos/morphir-rust#252, #263, #271, #275; finos/morphir#982, #989, #995, #998). Ledgers: `.dev/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-2*-morphir-host-phase-a-part-*.ledger.md`. Tracking is in beads: epic `morphir-opua.1`; next is Phase B `morphir-opua.1.2` (MEP contract as a Morphir model, first bead `morphir-opua.1.2.1`, finos/morphir#964). HostServices is `morphir-opua.1.4.5` in Phase D.

title: Windows: morphir CLI needs MSVC Spectre-mitigated CRT libs to build (GH #886)
description:
cargo build -p morphir fails on a Windows host whose Visual Studio install lacks the Spectre-mitigated CRT libs, blocking build, test and clippy for the whole crate.

Chain: morphir -> morphir-opa -> regorus (std feature) -> msvc_spectre_libs with features = ["error"], whose build script panics rather than warns when the libs are absent. Introduced by 826f47c0, which added regorus and morphir-opa. Linux CI is unaffected, so only Windows contributors hit it.

Options: document the required VS component; raise it with regorus upstream (the "error" feature is opt-in, a warning is the crate default); make morphir-opa optional behind a feature.

Found while verifying GH #885 locally. Full analysis in GH #886.

comments.text: Decision 2026-09-18 (Damian Reeves): two contracts, two owners. (1) 'My extension works with the released CLI' belongs to the extension repo (finos/morphir-rust#172). Replace them with a consumer check that downloads published bundles at tags pinned in a file and runs python_extension, rust_extension, generate_extension and generate_openapi_extension with the CLI built from the PR. title: Support Morphir IR v3 in the Python frontend and backend
description: Extend the Rust Python extension to compile and generate the supported Python modeling subset through classic Morphir IR v3 as well as v4. Reuse shared IR contracts, preserve multi-module privacy and supported value semantics, reject lossy conversions, advertise both versions, and verify native, WASM, packaged CLI paths with documentation.
design: Use one Python language mapping in v4 and concrete morphir-core classic types for v3 encoding. Decode v3 through shared typed migration, check inferred annotations against supported expression types before erasing them for Python generation, and reject collisions or lossy conversion. Readers honor supported minor intervals; writers request baseline 3 or 4. CLI selection is explicit flag then selected project ir.format_version then v4; v3 JSON/YAML single-file artifacts retain version metadata for generation and workspace loading.
acceptance_criteria: Both frontend and backend advertise IR 3 and 4; compile chooses the requested version; v3 ADTs, tuples, conditionals, imports and private modules roundtrip; independent classic IR input works; unsupported or lossy input produces diagnostics; README, release metadata and packaged tests match actual support.

title: morphir-rust YAML stage: Literal::Float must carry its lexeme; Document numbers through serde_saphyr
description: The YAML profile page requires lexeme-preserving numbers. morphir-core's Literal::Float(f64) re-renders (1.0e2 becomes 100.0), which no JSON kit case pins today but the YAML profile stage will. Carry float text the way Literal::Decimal does (or a lexeme alongside the f64). Also: with serde_json's arbitrary_precision enabled workspace-wide, a Literal::Document number is a private Number struct that serde_saphyr cannot serialize; the stage-1 fix wave converts it in the YAML encoder, and the YAML stage must keep that path (or a raw-number type) under test.
close_reason: Shipped by the Rust mirror stage 2 (YAML profile): finos/morphir-rust#153 (squash 6baae7eb) and finos/morphir#819 (squash 5152a96d). Literal::Float carries its lexeme (FloatLiteral); document numbers go through the core YAML writer from the lexeme (PlainValue removed); a guard test fails when a non-serde_json serializer enters a crate outside the allow-list. Residuals in .59 and .60.

comments.author: Damian Reeves
comments.text: Also: morphir-common/src/ir_transport/yaml/plain.rs falls back to a YAML string for a document number outside u64/i64/f64 range (no test); the YAML stage must carry such numbers as bare lexemes.

comments.author: Damian Reeves
comments.text: Also for the YAML stage: the parent CLI's YAML path decodes through the v4 JSON codec, so the YAML profile's explicit structural vocabulary (for example packageName spelled as a nested array in crates/morphir-common/tests/fixtures/yaml/v4-explicit.yaml) is refused; the Rust adapter declares no yaml capability yet, so the kit cannot see it. Decide whether the explicit vocabulary stays a MUST on the profile page or the reader table is amended, then implement it in the Rust YAML reader.

design:
# IR ingestion contract audit

Follow-up to #790.

## Purpose

Run one deliberate, read-only review of every supported or specified Morphir IR
ingestion route through the normalized UI AST and the Insight and XRay views.
The review must produce one complete support matrix and one consolidated
findings report. It must not fix findings or trigger another PR-bot review.

This corrects a gap in the XRay review process. The implementation reviews were
organized around small commit ranges and individual acceptance slices. The
exhaustive semantic fixture covered V3, while the V4 smoke project exercised
only a few expanded forms. As a result, the reviews proved renderer coverage
and a narrow V4 happy path, but not representation parity across the V4 schema
or across storage layouts.

## Prior review history and mandatory regression anchors

The audit must retain and independently re-prove every prior PR #790 review
finding. A finding marked fixed is a regression anchor, not a row to skip:

- Codex review `5103345835`, inline comment `3925698261`: a fresh clone could
  not run the documented mise setup before trusting `.config/mise/config.toml`.
  Addressed by parent commits `ef584982` and `41db85f4`. This is outside the IR
  semantic matrix but remains a checkout/setup precondition for the audit.
- Codex review `5103916579`: nested tuple patterns and subjects produced
  misaligned Insight decision-table columns. Addressed in morphir-ui commits
  `887d95c`, `050322f`, `e822422`, and `8b785e7`, vendored by parent commit
  `298e00ce`. Re-prove recursive, opaque, opposing, and arity-mismatch cases.
- Codex review `5104505026`: exact baseline release string `4.0.0` was rejected,
  and schema-valid flattened V4 access wrappers failed definition extraction.
  Addressed in morphir-ui commits `d7487d3`, `bdab4a4`, and `28c5558`, vendored
  by parent commit `d121e9bd`. Re-prove all schema-listed access spellings and
  wrapper forms, attributes/doc preservation, map boundaries, exact release
  dispatch, and accurate diagnostics.
- Codex review `5105072844`: compact V4 `Variable`, `Reference`, `Constructor`,
  `Tuple`, `List`, and `Literal` wrapper payloads degraded to unknown nodes.
  Addressed in morphir-ui commits `06da156` and `21116b5`, vendored by parent
  commit `b2eb5615`. Re-prove every compact and expanded form, scalar literal
  inference, non-finite rejection, and own-data-property behavior.

Preserve these deliberate exclusions and unresolved contexts:

- Do not silently expand decoder support from the baseline `4.0.0` release to
  `4.1.0`. The current exact-release policy recognizes later release strings
  but rejects unsupported releases accurately. Report any conflict between
  that policy and the schema as a contract/capability decision, not as an
  automatic parser fix.
- The published books-and-records fixture still contains retired
  `product-(i-d)` name syntax. That fixture issue is tracked separately as
  #793; do not weaken canonical name parsing to make it pass.
- The latest compact-value fix intentionally received no further external bot
  review. Its local tests and CI are evidence, but this audit must re-evaluate
  it independently.
- YAML single-file and JSON/YAML document-tree routes do not currently all
  reach a normalized library in the UI. Record each missing route explicitly
  rather than treating a manifest-only load as end-to-end support.

## Scope

Audit these input profiles:

1. V3 single-file JSON
2. V3 single-file YAML
3. V4 single-file JSON
4. V4 single-file YAML
5. V4 JSON document tree/VFS
6. V4 YAML document tree/VFS

For each applicable profile, follow both entry paths:

- browser file or folder loading;
- connected `morphir live` workspace loading.

Trace each route through parsing/loading, normalization into the shared AST,
definition selection, Insight transformation/rendering, and XRay
projection/rendering. A route that is specified but not implemented is a
product capability gap, not automatically a decoder defect.

The audit covers every schema-defined type expression, pattern, literal, and
value expression, including accepted compact and expanded spellings, access
wrappers, documentation, attributes, recursive nesting, and malformed or
future-compatible fallback behavior. V3/V4 semantic equivalents must normalize
to equivalent ASTs. JSON/YAML and single-file/document-tree storage choices
must not change the rendered semantic result.

The audit excludes unrelated CLI serving, deployment, performance,
observability, and multi-user production hardening.

## Normative sources and implementation boundaries

Treat these as normative or contract-defining inputs:

- `website/static/schemas/morphir-ir-v3.json`
- `website/static/schemas/morphir-ir-v4.json`
- `website/static/schemas/morphir-ir-v4-document-tree-files.json`
- `docs/spec/ir/schemas/v4/json-profile.md`
- `docs/spec/ir/schemas/v4/yaml-profile.md`
- `docs/spec/ir/schemas/v4/document-tree-files.md`
- `crates/morphir/src/commands/migrate.rs`

Inspect at least these implementation boundaries:

- `crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/`
- `ecosystem/morphir-ui/apps/morphir-web/src/workspace/browser-provider.ts`
- `ecosystem/morphir-ui/apps/morphir-web/src/connected/connected-provider.ts`
- `ecosystem/morphir-ui/packages/morphir-ir/src/decode.ts`
- `ecosystem/morphir-ui/packages/morphir-ir/src/ast-decode.ts`
- `ecosystem/morphir-ui/packages/morphir-ir/src/names.ts`
- `ecosystem/morphir-ui/packages/morphir-ir/src/ast.ts`
- `ecosystem/morphir-ui/packages/morphir-insight/src/`
- `ecosystem/morphir-ui/packages/morphir-ui/src/views/insight/`

Use existing tests and fixtures as evidence, but do not treat their existence or
green status as proof that a schema alternative is covered.

## Deliverables and stop rule

Produce:

1. A representation matrix with a row for every schema-defined alternative and
   columns for all applicable input profiles and entry paths. Each cell must be
   `supported`, `rejected with diagnostic`, `degrades to unknown`, `not
   implemented`, or `not applicable`, with evidence.
2. One ranked findings report. Every finding must cite the schema/contract,
   source location, minimal reproduction, observed result, expected result, and
   affected matrix cells.
3. A short gap summary grouped as code defect, missing product capability,
   fixture/spec inconsistency, or test-only gap.
4. A proposed issue breakdown that keeps delivery blockers separate from
   optional hardening.

Do not edit source, add tests, create fix commits, request GitHub reviews, or
stop after the first valid finding. Complete the matrix and report all findings
in one pass. Implementation begins only after maintainers review and prioritize
the consolidated report.

## Reusable review prompt

```text
Perform a deliberate, read-only contract audit of Morphir IR ingestion through
the web UI. This is not a diff review and not a request to fix code. Review the
whole contract boundary once, then return one consolidated report. Do not stop
after the first finding and do not request another reviewer.

Goal
Prove whether semantically equivalent Morphir IR reaches equivalent normalized
ASTs and remains usable in both Insight and XRay across:

- V3 single-file JSON
- V3 single-file YAML
- V4 single-file JSON
- V4 single-file YAML
- V4 JSON document tree/VFS
- V4 YAML document tree/VFS

Exercise both browser file/folder loading and connected `morphir live`
workspace loading wherever applicable. Document-tree layouts are V4-only.

Sources of truth
Read the relevant AGENTS.md files first. Then use:

- website/static/schemas/morphir-ir-v3.json
- website/static/schemas/morphir-ir-v4.json
- website/static/schemas/morphir-ir-v4-document-tree-files.json
- docs/spec/ir/schemas/v4/json-profile.md
- docs/spec/ir/schemas/v4/yaml-profile.md
- docs/spec/ir/schemas/v4/document-tree-files.md
- crates/morphir/src/commands/migrate.rs

Trace the implementation through:

- crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/
- ecosystem/morphir-ui/apps/morphir-web/src/workspace/browser-provider.ts
- ecosystem/morphir-ui/apps/morphir-web/src/connected/connected-provider.ts
- ecosystem/morphir-ui/packages/morphir-ir/src/{decode,ast-decode,names,ast}.ts
- ecosystem/morphir-ui/packages/morphir-insight/src/
- ecosystem/morphir-ui/packages/morphir-ui/src/views/insight/

Audit method

1. Reconcile PR #790 review history first. Re-prove review IDs `5103345835`,
   `5103916579`, `5104505026`, and `5105072844` against the current source and
   record each as passing, regressed, deliberately excluded, or superseded.
2. Inventory every schema-defined alternative before evaluating support:
   envelope/release spellings; distribution and module shapes; access wrappers;
   docs and attributes; names, paths, and FQNames; all type expressions; all
   patterns; all literals; all value expressions; inline and granular
   document-tree definitions.
3. For every alternative, enumerate compact, expanded, legacy-compatible, and
   recursive forms that the schema explicitly accepts. Do not infer support
   from one representative example.
4. Build a matrix across the six profiles and two entry paths. Mark each cell
   only as: supported; rejected with diagnostic; degrades to unknown; not
   implemented; or not applicable. Cite a test, controlled probe, or direct
   source trace for every non-obvious result.
5. Validate cross-profile invariants: equivalent JSON and YAML, and equivalent
   single-file and document-tree inputs, must normalize to equivalent ASTs and
   render the same selected definition in Insight and XRay.
6. Verify that every valid semantic node reaches the shared AST without an
   UnknownNode, omission, crash, or data loss, and that Insight/XRay handle every
   normalized kind. Verify unknown future tags degrade safely.
7. Probe malformed boundaries: nulls, arrays where maps are required, missing
   required fields, ambiguous access wrappers or manifests, mixed serialization
   profiles, duplicate/invalid names, inherited properties/accessors in direct
   decoder calls, unsupported versions, and size/path confinement already
   promised by the loaders. Use only trusted local fixtures and controlled
   values.
8. Run the relevant existing tests, but do not treat green tests as coverage.
   Identify matrix rows with no executable evidence.

Classification

- Code defect: a currently supported route violates its schema or loses,
  misnormalizes, or misrenders valid IR.
- Missing product capability: a specified/desired route has no complete loader
  path to Insight/XRay (for example, a loader stops at document-tree metadata).
- Fixture/spec inconsistency: published examples or fixtures violate the
  normative contract.
- Test-only gap: behavior is correct by source trace and probe but lacks durable
  coverage.

Report format

1. Findings first, ranked Critical, Important, Minor. For each finding include:
   contract citation, source location, minimal reproduction, expected versus
   observed behavior, affected matrix cells, and the smallest sensible fix
   boundary. If there are no findings, say so explicitly.
2. The complete representation matrix, including unsupported and untested
   cells. Do not omit passing rows.
3. A prior-review ledger for Codex review IDs `5103345835`, `5103916579`,
   `5104505026`, and `5105072844`, including current evidence and disposition.
4. Coverage gaps and fixture/spec inconsistencies, including #793 and
   the deliberate exact-release policy for `4.1.0`.
5. Proposed follow-up issues grouped into delivery blockers and optional
   hardening. Avoid unrelated refactors or productionization.
6. Commands/probes run and their results.

Stop after the consolidated report. Do not edit code, add tests, commit, push,
comment on a PR, or trigger a bot review.
```
acceptance_criteria: One evidence-backed matrix covers every applicable schema alternative across six input profiles and both entry paths; one ranked report distinguishes code defects, missing product capabilities, fixture/spec inconsistencies, and test-only gaps; no code changes or bot review are requested during the audit.

title: Playground: reuse a daemon session via SessionHandle instead of a cold invocation per compile
description:
Every Playground compile and generate currently starts a fresh extension invocation. The Kameo SessionActor that makes reuse possible landed on morphir-rust main (PR #142), but the CLI's NativePlaygroundProvider in crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/provider/playground.rs does not hold a SessionHandle yet, so nothing benefits from it.

Wiring it through means a compile pays extension startup once per session rather than once per click. That is also the precondition for the interaction the try-morphir experience implies: compiling on a debounce as the user types is only defensible once a compile stops spawning a process, which is why the current view deliberately compiles on explicit click only (see the comment on compile() in PlaygroundView.svelte).

Scope: hold a session per (provider, language) in the provider, route compile/generate through it, and honor DaemonError::SessionLost by evicting and respawning rather than surfacing the error.
close_reason: Shipped in finos/morphir#783 (3147cd41). SessionReuseInvoker holds one SessionHandle per provider id, keyed within that by provider incarnation (version/origin/invocation mode) so an upgrade mid-run does not keep serving the old binary. SessionLost evicts and retries once; a rejection keeps the session; a playground timeout calls the new ExtensionInvoker::abandon so a wedged actor is not left cached; native-direct falls through to the unchanged one-shot path. Also bumped the morphir-rust pin to 60cc88b, which the CLI needed before SessionHandle was reachable at all.

title: Playground: prefer an IR version the client can decode when the frontend offers a choice
description:
preferredIrVersion in morphir-ui packages/morphir-ui/src/views/playground/playground-state.svelte.ts picks the frontend's first advertised IR version whenever no target agreement narrows the choice. Nothing in that pick consults what @morphir/ir can actually decode (decode.ts hard-rejects any formatVersion other than 3), so a frontend advertising both 4 and 3 with 4 listed first yields a compile whose IR the Insight and XRay panes cannot render, even though asking for 3 would have rendered fine. The compile itself succeeds, which makes the failure look like a bug in the views rather than in the request.

Fix: among the versions that satisfy the chosen target (generation compatibility stays non-negotiable), prefer one this client can decode, and fall back to the first candidate when none is decodable so compile and generate still work and only the visualization degrades. The decodable set belongs to @morphir/ir as a single source of truth so the Playground follows automatically when v4 decoding lands.

Note the wire spells versions inconsistently: providers advertise both a bare major ('3') and a full triplet ('4.0.0'), so the match is on the major component.

Related: morphir-19s6 covers making v4 renderable at all; this issue is about not asking for an unrenderable version when a renderable one was on offer.
close_reason: Fixed in morphir-ui#29 (0910e8aa); vendored into the CLI by finos/morphir#781. preferredIrVersion now prefers a decodable IR version among those the chosen target agrees to, with DECODABLE_FORMAT_VERSIONS in @morphir/ir as the single source of truth so the predicate and decodeMorphirIr cannot drift.

title: Playground provider: contain extension output in a scratch directory instead of blocklisting options
description:
The connected Playground must never write into the user's workspace, and today that invariant is enforced by deny_output_options in crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/provider/playground.rs: it strips outputDir and pins emitParseStage=false before invoking a backend. That is a blocklist, so it only holds for the option names known when it was written. A new extension option that writes to disk, or a provider that ignores the pinned value, defeats it silently, and the failure mode is files appearing in a workspace the user never asked to modify.

Replace it with containment: run the invocation in a scratch directory the host owns, and treat a write outside it as the extension's problem rather than the host's. Artifacts already come back in-band over MEP, so nothing the Playground needs depends on where the extension writes.

Acceptance: the no-write invariant holds for an extension requesting an output path the host has never seen, proven by a test that invokes a backend with an unknown write-shaped option and asserts the workspace is untouched.
